## Why

<redacted> roll 54, of dungeon-module ISSUE-25 (merged as dungeon-module PR 28). The operator's rule is natural everything, and the module granted the Defias Gunpowder for the Deadmines Iron Clad Door event. The change has the party loot it from the world instead, so the module grants nothing a player could not earn.

## What

- dungeon-module `581cb969` -> `a4e35f0d` (head of its deployed branch) in the source pins only: UPSTREAM-PINS and a DEV_AHEAD entry in the drift check. dungeon-module has no submodule, so those are the only source locations. The banner and deployed_dev move with the image in the pin PR, so this PR restarts nothing.
- game-module stays at `17874fcc`. Core, playerbots and ollama-chat do not move.

The image digest pin follows after the build and the binary proof, as one restart.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exactly the source locations move (UPSTREAM-PINS and the drift entry).
- [ ] The <redacted> tests, the promotion tests and the drift check pass ("All four views agree"; 693 passed, 1 skipped locally).
- [ ] The image builds from the new dungeon-module SHA.

Size: XS

## Out of scope

- The digest pin (next PR).
- dungeon-module PRs 26 and 27, and game-module PRs that have not merged yet. They roll in a later batch.

Refs game-orchestrator ISSUE-512

body:
## Why

<redacted> roll 55, rebuilt as one batch: game-module ISSUE-937 (natural-only grants), game-module ISSUE-924 (a logout marks only its own character offline) and game-module ISSUE-934 (before the Majordomo and Ragnaros pulls the raid run holds for repairs; every boss pull logs the lowest durability). Source pins in infra PR 5326. This replaces infra PR 5325, whose build lacked ISSUE-934; one restart carries all three.

## Summary

- `<redacted>/kustomization.yaml`: the <redacted> and db-import digests move together, both from build run 38433884147 (core 7f12e89e, playerbots 7a593fa2, game-module 2522c5cb, dungeon-module 581cb969). The <redacted> comment stays 3 lines.
- The banner (`orchestrator-pin.yaml`) and its test literal move to `2522c5cb`; the DEV_AHEAD allowance is removed, so deployed_dev equals the pins again.
- Prove step (16:59 UTC): a throwaway pod on the <redacted> digest found all five strings in the binary: `marked only their` (ISSUE-924), `NOT MOVED: nothing here teleports a member (natural only)` and `takes the resurrection a player would` (ISSUE-937), `pre-pull repair walk` and `repair hold before` (ISSUE-934). The build log shows game-module @ 2522c5cb9cf0.
- Pre-roll review: ship, no blockers. 0eaf0403..5040024e was reviewed for PR 5325 (bridge rows for retired grants end `error` with a reason; a member falling through the world now dies instead of being lifted; a ghost that cannot path to its spirit healer keeps retrying the walk). 5040024e..2522c5cb (ISSUE-934) touches only the Molten Core raid-run path: pure decision functions plus a hold before encounters 9 and 10, with a 300-second limit. No guild member is near raid level, so it changes nothing for anyone online at the restart. No SQL in the batch, so a rollback is a revert of this PR. Smaller finding for later: the pre-pull repair walk claims a travel aim to a repairer, which inside Molten Core means leaving the instance; worth a look before the first raid night.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both digests come from one build and move in this one PR; the drift check says "All four views agree".
- [ ] After the merge, the <redacted> rolls once to the new digest with no ASSERTION FAILED and online bots back near normal within 30 minutes.
- [ ] No orchestrator_command row is left `claimed` or `verifying` for a retired grant, and ghost counts per guild do not rise over the two hours after the roll.

Size: XS

## Out of scope

- The dungeon-module build fix and its source bump.
- The bridge batch (its own pin PR).

Refs game-orchestrator ISSUE-512

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Update the Beszel deployment to restore its SSH key and latest database archive at startup, run without host networking, and serve traffic through the Beszel Service. Move the reconciliation and backup mounts so they no longer depend on node-local files.
Files: 8 logic

## Why
The issue found that Beszel cannot use an external database upstream, and its remaining recovery work is to make the hub recoverable on another node. The SSH key and database now have off-node copies, but the hub is still pinned to <host>.

## Summary
Update the Beszel deployment to restore its SSH key and latest database archive at startup, run without host networking, and serve traffic through the Beszel Service. Move the reconciliation and backup mounts so they no longer depend on node-local files.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The hub restores its SSH key from SSM and its latest database archive before starting.
- [ ] The hub deployment no longer uses `hostNetwork` or selects <host> specifically.
- [ ] Caddy routes Beszel traffic to the Beszel Service.
- [ ] Reconciliation and backup jobs use storage that remains available after moving the hub to another LAN node.
- [ ] Document the recovery steps and verify the rendered manifests reflect the new placement and restore flow.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Replacing Beszel or changing its database backend.
- Deleting the orphaned Litestream ConfigMap.
Rewritten from issue 1244.

@@ -0,0 +1,26 @@
+---
+# Beszel hub data PVC on the UNAS SMB share (ISSUE-5419).
+#
+# Moves beszel-hub off node-local hostPath (/var/lib/beszel-hub on
+# k8s-<redacted>-lan-<host>) to a PVC backed by the UNAS share.
+# This allows the hub to run on any LAN node (<host>, <redacted>-gpu,
+# <redacted>) and survive node reboots or failures.
+#
+# The PVC uses the smb-unas StorageClass (provisioner: smb.csi.k8s.io)
+# which requires the workload to have `<host>/location: lan`
+# nodeSelector. The beszel-hub StatefulSet already runs on LAN nodes.
+#
+# Retain reclaimPolicy means deleting the PVC will NOT erase the data
+# on the NAS - it leaves the PV Released for manual recovery.
+apiVersion: v1
+kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
+metadata:
+  name: beszel-hub-data
+  namespace: monitoring
+spec:
+  accessModes:
+    - ReadWriteOnce
+  storageClassName: smb-unas
+  resources:
+    requests:
+      storage: 1Gi
\ No newline at end of file

## Intent
Class: logic
- <redacted> (and <redacted> nodes) persistently mask swap.target so swap can never be re-activated on reboot or a node rebuild (bootstrap-<redacted>-node.sh now masks the unit after removing swap from fstab).
- cost-emitter CronJob aligns its failed-job retry with the fleet convention (backoffLimit 1 -> 2) so a transient CE/OCI fetch failure gets one bounded retry before failing, while ttlSecondsAfterFinished keeps completed/failed job pods reaped after a day.
- Reboot runbook (production/docs/INFRASTRUCTURE.md) documents uncordoning returned <redacted> nodes and removing phantom pods before confirming the <redacted> cluster is healthy.
- <redacted> external DNS is already codified by <redacted>-lan-node-dns.yml (MagicDNS 192.0.2.36 first, then public fallbacks 192.0.2.108 and 192.0.2.247) for reliable image-pull resolution.
- <host> Tailscale autoconnect is already codified by the cloud-init tailscale-autoconnect guard (tailscale up --authkey=file --hostname --timeout=180s), which succeeds across reboot.
- WireGuard host pin is already codified by the <host> wg-cluster.conf template using DNS-name endpoints (<host>, <host>) for the nodes that use them.
Files: 2 logic, 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
The issue asks to codify the reboot-tested fixes and reliability findings so node rebuilds do not lose them and routine failures recover cleanly.

## Summary
Add the applicable host and workload settings to the repository: mask swap on <redacted>, pin the WireGuard endpoint in host resolution where the node configuration uses its DNS name, repair the <host> Tailscale autoconnect command, improve <redacted> external DNS reliability, and clean up completed cost-emitter job pods.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The <redacted> configuration persistently masks its swap unit, and the WireGuard host pin is applied only to nodes that use the DNS endpoint.
- [ ] The <host> autoconnect service starts Tailscale with the required flags and succeeds across reboot.
- [ ] The <redacted> DNS configuration provides reliable external resolution for image pulls, including the fallback resolvers described in the issue.
- [ ] The cost-emitter CronJob configures appropriate failed-job retry and cleanup behavior.
- [ ] The relevant reboot or recovery runbook documents uncordoning returned <redacted> nodes and removing phantom pods.

Size: L

## Out of scope
- Adding a second Main-VLAN node or moving <redacted> beyond OCI.
- Changing tailnet ownership or access.
Rewritten from issue 1435.

+"""The <redacted> persistent swap mask (reboot resilience).
+
+bootstrap-<redacted>-node.sh disables swap at build time and must persistently mask
+the swap unit so a reboot - or a node rebuild that re-runs this bootstrap -
+can never re-activate swap. The <redacted> VM runs 4 GB: a swapped kubelet is
+an unhealthy kubelet. Masking survives across reboots; the fstab edit keeps
+swap out of the next boot's mount table too.
+
+Run from pulumi/k8s-<redacted>/: `uv run pytest tests/ -q`.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+BOOTSTRAP = (ROOT / "<redacted>" / "bootstrap-<redacted>-node.sh").read_text()
+
+
+def test_swap_removed_from_fstab_at_build_time():
+    assert re.search(r"swapoff -a; sed -i '/swap/d' /etc/fstab", BOOTSTRAP), (
+        "swap must be removed from fstab at build time"
+    )
+
+
+def test_swap_target_persistently_masked():
+    # The systemd mask persists across reboots and rebuilds, so swap can never
+    # be re-activated on a returned node.
+    assert "systemctl mask swap.target" in BOOTSTRAP, (
+        "swap.target must be persistently masked so swap cannot re-activate"
+    )
+
+
+def test_mask_follows_fstab_edit():
+    # Build-time disable first, then the persistent mask, so a rebuild never
+    # re-activates swap between the two.
+    assert BOOTSTRAP.index("swapoff -a") < BOOTSTRAP.index("systemctl mask swap.target")

## Intent
Class: logic
- Pulumi (pulumi/aws-ssm-hybrid) defines per-OS SSM patch baselines for Linux (AMAZON_LINUX_2), macOS (MAC_OS), and Windows (WINDOWS), each approving the default critical patch set after 7 days.
- A scheduled weekly maintenance window (Sundays 02:00 UTC, 4h duration, 2h cutoff) is defined and targets <redacted> hybrid instances by Patch Group tag.
- A maintenance-window task runs the AWS-RunPatchBaseline SSM document (Operation=Install, which scans then installs) in that window on the schedule.
- Synth tests assert the three baseline OS configurations/approval rules and the maintenance-window, target, and task shape.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
The issue asks to move fleet patching to SSM Patch Manager, starting with the Pulumi-managed infrastructure that can be built and checked without a registered pilot host.

## Summary
Define per-OS patch baselines for Linux, macOS, and Windows, add a scheduled maintenance-window association that scans and installs patches, and add synth tests for their configuration.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pulumi defines patch baselines for Linux, macOS, and Windows.
- [ ] A maintenance-window association is configured to scan and install patches on a schedule.
- [ ] Synth tests assert the baseline OS configurations and maintenance-window shape.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Live patch-run verification or SSM compliance checks against a pilot host.
- Removing the Ansible patch playbooks before live coverage is verified.

## Intent
Class: logic
- The registry build reusable workflow now connects buildctl to the persistent buildkitd daemon at unix:///opt/buildkit/buildkitd.sock instead of invoking buildctl-daemonless.sh per build.
- The build Job mounts the node buildkit socket hostPath at /opt/buildkit so the client can reach the daemon on k8s-<redacted>-lan-<host>.
- Dockerfile RUN --mount=type=cache caches (including pip) now persist across builds because they are backed by the long-lived daemon's PVC.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
The registry build workflow still starts a fresh daemonless BuildKit for each build, so its local snapshot and pip caches do not persist. Update it to use the already-running BuildKit daemon and its persistent cache storage.

## Summary
Change the in-cluster registry build workflow to connect `buildctl` to the persistent BuildKit daemon. Check that the Dockerfile frontend can be pulled in the cluster or provide it another way.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The registry build workflow connects to the persistent daemon with `buildctl --addr` and no longer invokes `buildctl-daemonless.sh`.
- [ ] Pip cache mounts persist across builds handled by the daemon.
- [ ] The workflow's Dockerfile frontend is available under the cluster's egress constraints.
- [ ] The workflow retains its existing build and registry publishing behavior.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Changing the persistent daemon Deployment or PVC, which are already working.
- Making unrelated changes to other build workflows.
Rewritten from issue 1449.

## Why
The issue asks for a per-request way to set Ollama context length because the current host-wide setting applies its memory cost to every request. The gateway already proxies Ollama's native API, so the remaining gap is the OpenAI-compatible path used by active consumers.

## Summary
Add support in <redacted> for an OpenAI-compatible request to carry a context-length hint and forward it as Ollama's `options.num_ctx`. Define the request field and forwarding behavior in the gateway's existing conventions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] OpenAI-compatible inference requests can include a context-length hint that <redacted> forwards to Ollama as `options.num_ctx`.
- [ ] Requests without the hint retain the existing behavior.
- [ ] Verify a long Discord thread that previously truncated completes using the per-request hint without requiring a higher static context setting.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Client-side conversation history bounding or summarization.
- Switching consumers to call Ollama's native API.

+def _forward_num_ctx(body: bytes, route: str, target: SparkTarget) -> bytes:
+    """Translate a per-request `num_ctx` for Ollama targets (ISSUE-5468).
+
+    OpenAI-compatible callers (Discord chat, Grug - Elder, etc.) cannot set
+    `num_ctx` via Ollama's `options.num_ctx`, so the gateway exposes a
+    top-level `num_ctx` field on `/v1/chat/completions` and
+    `/v1/completions` requests and writes it into `options.num_ctx` before
+    forwarding to an Ollama target. This lets a caller ask for a longer
+    context without raising the host-wide OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH default.
+
+    The field is consumed (popped from the body) on every route, because it
+    is a gateway-level extension that no upstream speaks natively: for an
+    OpenAI route + Ollama target it becomes `options.num_ctx`; for a vLLM
+    target, a non-OpenAI route, or an invalid value it is simply dropped.
+    A non-int or non-positive value is treated the same as absent so a
+    caller typo cannot widen the context window unexpectedly."""
+    try:
+        payload = json.loads(body)
+    except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
+        return body
+    if not isinstance(payload, dict) or "num_ctx" not in payload:
+        return body
+    num_ctx = payload.pop("num_ctx")
+    if target.kind == "ollama" and route in _VLLM_PATHS:
+        if not isinstance(num_ctx, int) or isinstance(num_ctx, bool) or num_ctx <= 0:
+            return json.dumps(payload).encode()
+        opts = payload.setdefault("options", {})
+        if not isinstance(opts, dict):
+            opts = {}
+        opts["num_ctx"] = num_ctx
+        payload["options"] = opts
+    return json.dumps(payload).encode()
+

+"""<host> docs match the post-migration audit (ISSUE-5460).

+truth for what runs on the host vs what has moved to Kubernetes. After the
+migration tracked in ISSUE-2004 and finalized in ISSUE-5460, Plex and Tautulli

+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import pathlib
+import re
+import unittest
+
+ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+DOC = ROOT / "production/docs/INFRASTRUCTURE.md"
+
+RETIRED_SERVICES = {
+    "cAdvisor",
+    "Open WebUI",
+    "Stirling PDF",
+    "Karakeep",

+}

+
+def _section(text: str, heading: str) -> str:
+    """Return the text from `heading` up to the next same-level heading."""
+    pattern = re.compile(rf"^{re.escape(heading)}\s*$", re.MULTILINE)
+    match = pattern.search(text)
+    if not match:
+        raise ValueError(f"heading not found: {heading}")
+    start = match.end()
+    next_heading = re.compile(r"^##\s+", re.MULTILINE)
+    later = next_heading.search(text, start)
+    end = later.start() if later else len(text)
+    return text[start:end]
+
+
+def _table_rows(section_text: str, subheading: str) -> list[list[str]]:
+    """Return the parsed body rows of the first Markdown table under `subheading`."""
+    pattern = re.compile(rf"^{re.escape(subheading)}\s*$", re.MULTILINE)
+    match = pattern.search(section_text)
+    if not match:
+        raise ValueError(f"subheading not found: {subheading}")
+
+    lines = section_text[match.end() :].splitlines()
+    rows: list[list[str]] = []
+    in_table = False
+    saw_separator = False
+    for line in lines:
+        if line.strip().startswith("|"):
+            in_table = True
+            cells = [cell.strip() for cell in line.split("|")]
+            # Drop empty leading/trailing cells produced by the outer pipes.
+            while cells and cells[0] == "":
+                cells.pop(0)
+            while cells and cells[-1] == "":
+                cells.pop()
+            if cells and all("-" in c for c in cells):
+                saw_separator = True
+                continue  # separator line
+            if cells and saw_separator:
+                rows.append(cells)
+        elif in_table:
+            break
+    return rows
+
+
+def _first_cell(row: list[str]) -> str:
+    """Strip Markdown bold markers from the first cell."""
+    return row[0].strip("*").strip()
+
+
+class SrvUnraidDocsMatchMigrationAudit(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_retired_services_not_in_host_service_list(self) -> None:
+        text = DOC.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        srv = _section(text, "## 🖥️ <host>")
+        host_rows = _table_rows(srv, "### Docker Containers")
+        host_names = {_first_cell(row) for row in host_rows}
+
+        found = RETIRED_SERVICES & host_names
+        self.assertEqual(
+            found,
+            set(),
+            "retired services must not appear in the <host> Docker Containers table",
+        )
+
+    def test_open_webui_removed_from_<redacted>_moved_table(self) -> None:
+        text = DOC.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        srv = _section(text, "## 🖥️ <host>")
+        moved_rows = _table_rows(srv, "#### Moved to k8s")
+        moved_names = {_first_cell(row) for row in moved_rows}
+
+        self.assertNotIn(
+            "Open WebUI",
+            moved_names,
+            "Open WebUI is not pinned to the <host> worker; remove it from this section",
+        )
+
+    def test_retired_paragraph_removed(self) -> None:
+        text = DOC.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        srv = _section(text, "## 🖥️ <host>")
+
+        self.assertNotIn(
+            "#### Retired (no longer anywhere)",
+            srv,
+            "the retired-services paragraph should be removed from the <host> host service list",
+        )
+
+    def test_plex_and_tautulli_documented_in_kubernetes(self) -> None:
+        text = DOC.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        srv = _section(text, "## 🖥️ <host>")

+

+        text = DOC.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        srv = _section(text, "## 🖥️ <host>")
+        host_rows = _table_rows(srv, "### Docker Containers")
+        host_names = {_first_cell(row) for row in host_rows}
+
+        self.assertIn(
+            "nextdns-192.0.2.205",

+"""Grug and kitchen-app deploy pools must stay off the memory-pressured <redacted>.
+
+ISSUE-5502 follow-up to ISSUE-2426. The <redacted> worker VM is a small node that also
+runs homey and scrypted; its available memory bottoms out when runner pods land
+there. The grug-api, grug-webhook, grug-consumer and <redacted>-api deploy workflows
+run on the ARC pools below, so this test pins those pools' placement so the
+deploys cannot schedule on k8s-<redacted>-lan-<redacted>-worker-01 while keeping the
+arm64 and LAN constraints that let them reach the in-cluster registry.
+
+STDLIB ONLY, like the other arc/tests suites: this matrix runs with no
+third-party packages installed.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+MANIFESTS_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+MAC_MINI = "k8s-<redacted>-lan-<redacted>-worker-01"
+GPU_NODE = "k8s-<redacted>-lan-<redacted>-gpu-worker-01"
+
+
+def _block(text: str, key: str) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Read a `key:` mapping by indentation.
+
+    Lines indented further than the header belong to it; the first line at or
+    left of the header ends it. Mirrors the helper in test_runner_priority.py
+    so the suite stays stdlib-only and self-contained.
+    """
+    out: dict[str, str] = {}
+    depth: int | None = None
+    for line in text.splitlines():
+        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
+        if depth is None:
+            if re.match(rf"^[ \t]*{re.escape(key)}:[ \t]*$", line):
+                depth = indent
+            continue
+        if indent <= depth:
+            break
+        kv = re.match(r"^[ \t]*([^:#]+):[ \t]*(\S.*?)[ \t]*$", line)
+        if kv:
+            out[kv.group(1).strip()] = kv.group(2).strip().strip("\"'")
+    return out
+
+
+def _not_in_hostnames(text: str) -> set[str]:
+    """Every hostname a required nodeAffinity excludes via operator: NotIn."""
+    excluded: set[str] = set()
+    lines = text.splitlines()
+    current_key: str | None = None
+    key_indent: int | None = None
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(lines):
+        line = lines[i]
+        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
+            i += 1
+            continue
+        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
+
+        # Track the most recent key: value, scoped to its indentation block.
+        m = re.match(r"^\s*-?\s*key:\s*(.+?)\s*$", line)
+        if m:
+            current_key = m.group(1).strip().strip("\"'")
+            key_indent = indent
+            i += 1
+            continue
+        if key_indent is not None and indent <= key_indent:
+            current_key = None
+            key_indent = None
+
+        if current_key == "kubernetes.io/hostname" and re.search(
+            r"operator:\s*NotIn", line
+        ):
+            # Collect the values list that follows the NotIn operator.
+            values_indent: int | None = None
+            j = i + 1
+            while j < len(lines):
+                ln = lines[j]
+                if not ln.strip() or ln.lstrip().startswith("#"):
+                    j += 1
+                    continue
+                ind = len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip())
+                if values_indent is None:
+                    if re.match(r"^\s*values:\s*$", ln):
+                        values_indent = ind
+                        j += 1
+                        continue
+                    if ind <= indent:
+                        break
+                    j += 1
+                    continue
+                if ind <= values_indent:
+                    break
+                m2 = re.match(r"^\s*-\s*(.+?)\s*$", ln)
+                if m2:
+                    excluded.add(m2.group(1).strip().strip("\"'"))
+                j += 1
+            i = j if j > i else i + 1
+            continue
+        i += 1
+    return excluded
+
+
+class MacMiniExclusionTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Each listed service's deploy pool excludes the <redacted> worker."""
+
+    def test_grug_api_webhook_consumer_pool_excludes_mac_mini(self):
+        """grug-api, grug-webhook and grug-consumer deploy via arc-grug-arm64."""
+        path = MANIFESTS_ROOT / "arc-grug-arm64" / "values.yaml"
+        text = path.read_text()
+        sel = _block(text, "nodeSelector")
+        self.assertEqual(
+            sel.get("kubernetes.io/arch"),

## Why
The issue asks to move the <redacted> connector from its systemd service into Kubernetes while keeping the Cave free of inbound connections. The connector already routes inference through the spark gateway, but it still needs a Kubernetes deployment and the systemd service needs to be retired after a live round trip is verified.

## Summary
Add a production container build and Kubernetes deployment for the <redacted> connector, following the existing kitchen-app connector pattern. Configure its credentials, logging, health checks, and gateway URL. Document a safe cutover that ensures only one consumer polls the coach jobs queue at a time, then retire the systemd service after verifying the full request and response path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A production image build and Kubernetes manifests deploy the connector in its own namespace, pinned to an eligible LAN worker.
- [ ] The pod obtains the required credentials, sends logs and metrics to the existing monitoring setup, and has working heartbeat probes.
- [ ] The connector uses the spark gateway service for inference and completes a verified coach request round trip through the results queue.
- [ ] Cutover instructions prevent simultaneous queue consumers, and the systemd service is removed and its retirement documented after verification.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Changing the coach job or results queue protocols.
- Changing the spark gateway's routing behavior.

@@ -0,0 +1,135 @@
+# coach-<redacted>
+
+The worker half of kitchen-app's <redacted> Spark coach (the coach lane of the Spark
+Cave, ISSUE-1738). It long-polls the `<redacted>-kitchenapp-coach-jobs` SQS FIFO
+queue, relays the fully-rendered chat messages in each job to the
+<redacted>, and writes a `FallbackResult` (`{"reply": <text>}`) to
+`<redacted>-kitchenapp-coach-results`, which <redacted>-api polls. It does no
+business logic and never touches the kitchen-app API or user data.
+
+Source + tests: `production/scripts/coach-<redacted>/`. Image:
+`registry.<host>/coach-<redacted>`, built by the `build-coach` job
+in `.github/workflows/build.kitchenapp-<redacted>.yml` on every merge that
+touches the source dir.
+
+It ran as a systemd service on <host> until ISSUE-5431 moved it here.
+The k8s pod satisfies the same invariant: the Cave receives zero inbound
+connections. The pod dials out to SQS and to the gateway, and has no Service
+and no listening port.
+
+## Request path
+
+```
+iOS app -> <redacted>-api -> coach jobs FIFO -> this pod
+  -> <redacted> Service (smart-routes across both Sparks, spark:warm-any)
+  -> coach results FIFO -> <redacted>-api -> iOS app poll
+```
+
+## Configuration (env, in deployment.yaml)
+
+| Env | Purpose |
+|---|---|
+| `SPARK_CAVE_KITCHENAPP_COACH_{JOBS,RESULTS}_QUEUE_URL` | The lane's SQS FIFO queues |
+| `COACH_OLLAMA_URL` | The <redacted> ClusterIP Service, `/v1/chat/completions` |
+| `COACH_MODEL` | `spark:warm-any`; the gateway substitutes the resident model |
+| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | From the `coach-<redacted>-aws` Secret |
+| `HEARTBEAT_FILE` | Written every loop turn; the liveness and readiness probes fail when it is over 300s old |
+
+`COACH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (60), `COACH_ATTEMPTS` (2), `COACH_MAX_TOKENS` (500)
+and `COACH_TEMPERATURE` (0.4) keep their code defaults.
+
+## Secrets (imperative, never in git)
+
+Both are created once per namespace:
+
+- `coach-<redacted>-aws`: the lane's IAM key from SSM
+  `/<redacted>/kitchenapp-coach/connector-aws-*`. Command and IAM scope in
+  `secret.template.yaml.example`.
+- `registry-pull`: the in-cluster registry credential.
+
+```
+REGISTRY_PASSWORD="$(aws ssm get-parameter \
+  --name <redacted> --with-decryption \
+  --query Parameter.Value --output text)"
+<redacted>coach-<redacted> create secret docker-registry registry-pull \
+  --docker-server=registry.<host> \
+  --docker-username=<redacted>-push \
+  --docker-password="$REGISTRY_PASSWORD" \
+  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
+unset REGISTRY_PASSWORD
+```
+
+## Logs and metrics
+
+The pod logs one JSON line per event to stdout: `coach_connector_started`,
+`coach_job_answered` (with `request_id`, `degraded`, `error`),
+`coach_job_unaddressable`, `coach_result_send_failed`,
+`coach_receive_failed`, `coach_heartbeat_write_failed`.
+
+- Now: `<redacted>coach-<redacted> logs deploy/coach-<redacted>`.
+  Datadog is off since 2026-10-05 (`docs/observability/DATADOG-SHUTDOWN.md`).
+- When Datadog is back: the `ad.datadoghq.com/connector.logs` annotation and
+  the `tags.datadoghq.com/*` labels ship these lines as
+  `service:coach-<redacted>`, and the agent's kubelet check reports the
+  pod's CPU, memory and restarts under `kube_namespace:coach-<redacted>`.
+  The systemd unit logged only to <redacted>'s journal, and no monitor in this
+  repo watches the connector. Queue-depth and DLQ alerting reads SQS metrics,
+  which do not depend on where the consumer runs.
+
+## Cutover from systemd (one consumer at a time)
+
+The jobs queue is a FIFO with a 600s visibility timeout and
+`maxReceiveCount` 5. Two pollers would not double-answer a job, but a job one
+of them received and then lost stays invisible for 10 minutes, then counts a
+receive towards the DLQ. So the old consumer stops BEFORE the new one starts,
+and the order is enforced in git: this dir lands with `replicas: 0`, and only
+a second PR turns the pod on.
+
+1. **Merge the PR that adds this dir.** Sync applies the namespace and a
+   Deployment with 0 replicas. The build job pushes the image; note its
+   digest from the run log (`registry.<host>/coach-<redacted>@sha256:...`).
+2. **Seed both Secrets** (above).
+3. **Stop the systemd unit, but leave it installed** so rollback is one
+   command:
+   ```
+   ssh <host> sudo systemctl disable --now coach-<redacted>
+   ssh <host> systemctl is-active coach-<redacted>   # inactive
+   ```
+4. **Wait for in-flight jobs to settle.** A job the unit received but never
+   answered becomes visible again after 600s. Start once this reads `0`, so
+   such a redelivery is not mistaken for the test request:
+   ```
+   aws sqs get-queue-attributes --region us-east-1 \
+     --queue-url https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/<account>/<redacted>-kitchenapp-coach-jobs-prod.fifo \
+     --attribute-names ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible
+   ```
+5. **Turn the pod on with a PR** that sets `replicas: 1` and pins the digest:
+   ```
+   python3 .github/scripts/bump_manifest_image.py \
+     registry.<host>/coach-<redacted>@sha256:<digest> \
+     production/<redacted>/manifests/coach-<redacted>/deployment.yaml
+   ```
+   The same PR deletes the `coach-<redacted>:latest` entry from
+   `ALLOWLIST` in
+   `production/scripts/image-upstream-check/tests/test_no_untagged_images.py`;
+   the guard fails on an entry that no longer floats. After the merge, the log should show `coach_connector_started` with the
+   gateway's `ollama_url`, and the pod should be Ready.
+6. **Verify a live round trip.** Send the coach a message in the kitchenapp
+   iOS app. The pod logs `coach_job_answered` with `"degraded": false`, the
+   <redacted> dashboard shows the call, and the reply appears in the app.
+7. **Retire the unit** only after step 6 passes:
+   ```
+   ansible-playbook production/playbooks/coach_<redacted>_retire.yml --ask-become-pass
+   ```
+   It removes the unit and `/opt/coach-<redacted>`, including the env
+   file holding the IAM key (the canonical copy stays in SSM).
+
+**Rollback** (any step before 7): scale the pod to 0 first, then restart
+the unit, so there is never a moment with two consumers.
+
+```
+<redacted>coach-<redacted> scale deploy/coach-<redacted> --replicas=0
+ssh <host> sudo systemctl enable --now coach-<redacted>
+```
+
+Then revert the step 5 PR, so the next sync does not scale the pod back up.

@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
+# coach-<redacted> -- the worker for the Spark Cave kitchen-app COACH lane
+# (ISSUE-5431, was a systemd service on <redacted>). Long-polls
+# <redacted>-kitchenapp-coach-jobs (SQS FIFO), relays the fully-rendered chat
+# messages to the <redacted>, and answers on
+# <redacted>-kitchenapp-coach-results. Outbound only: no Service, no listening
+# port, so the Cave still receives zero inbound connections. Mirrors
+# kitchenapp-<redacted>. Applied by sync.k8s-manifests on merge.
+#
+# Secrets are imperative (NOT in git), seeded from the lane's SSM creds:
+#   coach-<redacted>-aws  <- /<redacted>/kitchenapp-coach/connector-aws-*
+#   registry-pull (dockerconfigjson) <- registry.<host> push creds
+# See secret.template.yaml.example. Cutover from systemd: README.md.
+apiVersion: v1
+kind: Namespace
+metadata:
+  name: coach-<redacted>
+  labels:
+    name: coach-<redacted>
+---
+apiVersion: apps/v1
+kind: Deployment
+metadata:
+  name: coach-<redacted>
+  namespace: coach-<redacted>
+  labels:
+    app: coach-<redacted>
+    tags.datadoghq.com/service: coach-<redacted>
+    tags.datadoghq.com/env: prod
+spec:
+  # 0 until the cutover: the systemd unit on <redacted> is still the jobs
+  # queue's consumer, and two pollers on one FIFO is what the cutover exists
+  # to avoid. The cutover PR sets 1 (and pins the digest) only after the
+  # unit is stopped. See README.md.
+  replicas: 0
+  # Recreate, never RollingUpdate: a surge pod would be a second consumer on
+  # the jobs queue for as long as the rollout takes.
+  strategy:
+    type: Recreate
+  selector:
+    matchLabels:
+      app: coach-<redacted>
+  template:
+    metadata:
+      labels:
+        app: coach-<redacted>
+        tags.datadoghq.com/service: coach-<redacted>
+        tags.datadoghq.com/env: prod
+      annotations:
+        ad.datadoghq.com/connector.logs: '[{"source":"python","service":"coach-<redacted>"}]'
+    spec:
+      # Pin to the LAN amd64 worker: the image is built native amd64 on this
+      # node (build.kitchenapp-<redacted>.yml), and it is the node the
+      # <redacted> itself is pinned to.
+      nodeSelector:
+        kubernetes.io/hostname: k8s-<redacted>-lan-<host>
+      automountServiceAccountToken: false
+      imagePullSecrets:
+        - name: registry-pull
+      containers:
+        - name: connector
+          # Tag until the first build exists; the cutover PR replaces it with
+          # the built digest (bump_manifest_image.py). Nothing pulls it while
+          # replicas is 0. The floating-image guard allows this tag through
+          # its ALLOWLIST until then (test_no_untagged_images.py).
+          image: registry.<host>/coach-<redacted>:latest
+          env:
+            - name: SPARK_CAVE_KITCHENAPP_COACH_JOBS_QUEUE_URL
+              value: "https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/<account>/<redacted>-kitchenapp-coach-jobs-prod.fifo"
+            - name: SPARK_CAVE_KITCHENAPP_COACH_RESULTS_QUEUE_URL
+              value: "https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/<account>/<redacted>-kitchenapp-coach-results-prod.fifo"
+            - name: AWS_DEFAULT_REGION
+              value: "us-east-1"
+            # The <redacted>'s ClusterIP Service: it smart-routes each call
+            # across BOTH Sparks (warm model first, then headroom). The
+            # systemd unit reached the same gateway through
+            # sparks.<host> because <redacted> cannot resolve cluster
+            # DNS; in-cluster that hairpin is gone.
+            - name: COACH_OLLAMA_URL
+              value: "<redacted>:8080/v1/chat/completions"
+            # Not a real model name: the gateway rewrites it to whatever
+            # model the chosen Spark has resident (ISSUE-2451).
+            - name: COACH_MODEL
+              value: "spark:warm-any"
+            - name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
+              valueFrom:
+                secretKeyRef:
+                  name: coach-<redacted>-aws
+                  key: access_key_id
+            - name: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
+              valueFrom:
+                secretKeyRef:
+                  name: coach-<redacted>-aws
+                  key: secret_access_key
+            - name: HEARTBEAT_FILE
+              value: "/tmp/heartbeat"
+          # The loop writes /tmp/heartbeat at the start of every turn. The
+          # longest turn is the 20s long-poll plus one job: COACH_ATTEMPTS(2)
+          # x COACH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS(60s) + the 2s retry sleep, about 145s.
+          # 300s leaves twice that before the probe calls the loop stuck.
+          livenessProbe:
+            exec:
+              command:

+# unit used the same key); its inline policy allows sqs:Receive/Delete/

+---
+# Retire the coach-<redacted> systemd service on <redacted> (ISSUE-5431).
+# The connector now runs in k8s (production/<redacted>/manifests/coach-<redacted>/).
+#
+# Run this ONLY as the last step of the cutover in that dir's README, after
+# the pod has answered a live coach request. Until then the unit stays on
+# disk (stopped and disabled), so rolling back is `systemctl enable --now
+# coach-<redacted>`. This playbook removes that option: it deletes the
+# unit and /opt/coach-<redacted>, including the env file holding the
+# lane's IAM key (the canonical copy stays in SSM /<redacted>/kitchenapp-coach/).
+#
+# Idempotent: a second run finds nothing to remove.
+#
+# Run: ansible-playbook production/playbooks/coach_<redacted>_retire.yml --ask-become-pass
+- name: Retire the <redacted> connector systemd service
+  hosts: <host>
+  gather_facts: false
+  become: true
+  vars:
+    coach_unit: coach-<redacted>
+    coach_unit_file: /etc/systemd/system/coach-<redacted>.service
+    coach_dir: /opt/coach-<redacted>
+  tasks:
+    - name: Look for the unit file
+      ansible.builtin.stat:
+        path: "{{ coach_unit_file }}"
+      register: coach_unit_stat
+
+    - name: Stop and disable the unit, so it never polls the jobs queue again
+      ansible.builtin.systemd:
+        name: "{{ coach_unit }}"
+        state: stopped
+        enabled: false
+      when: coach_unit_stat.stat.exists
+
+    - name: Remove the unit file
+      ansible.builtin.file:
+        path: "{{ coach_unit_file }}"
+        state: absent
+
+    - name: Reload systemd so the removed unit is forgotten
+      ansible.builtin.systemd:
+        daemon_reload: true
+      when: coach_unit_stat.stat.exists
+
+    - name: Remove the app dir, venv and env file
+      ansible.builtin.file:
+        path: "{{ coach_dir }}"
+        state: absent

The pod obtains the required credentials, sends logs and metrics to the existing monitoring setup, and has working heartbeat probes.

## Intent
Class: logic
- Added production/scripts/backlog-emitter/compare_judge_models.py: a non-Datadog comparison harness that scores the same judge dataset on the incumbent judge model (spark:warm-any) and a second realistically servable model (nemotron-3-nano:30b-a3b-q4_K_M) through the spark gateway, records the servin
- Added production/scripts/backlog-emitter/judge_dataset.json: a representative judge dataset of 8 epics used as the shared dataset for both model runs.
- Added production/scripts/backlog-emitter/tests/test_compare_judge_models.py: 16 tests covering serving-config recording, run comparison, disagreement listing with detail, agreement rate, the verdict recommendation, and the deterministic simulate stand-in.
- Added production/scripts/backlog-emitter/comparison_verdict.md and serving_configs.json: demonstration output (clearly labeled as simulated stand-in responses because the live gateway is not reachable in this environment) scoring both models on the same dataset, recording serving configs, listing th
Files: 3 logic, 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
This issue asks for a side-by-side score of the same judge dataset on the incumbent and a second model, with serving differences documented, disagreements listed, and a numbers-backed switch-or-not verdict. The existing Datadog path is unavailable, so the comparison needs a non-Datadog scoring path.

## Summary
Use the repository's available dataset and runner to score the incumbent and a realistically servable second model. Record both serving configurations and any other run differences, list cases where the models disagree, and write a verdict tied to specific results.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The same judge dataset is scored on the incumbent and a second realistically servable model through a non-Datadog path, with serving configuration recorded for each run.
- [ ] Any difference between the runs other than the model is explicitly documented.
- [ ] A written verdict recommends switching or not switching and cites the specific comparison numbers.
- [ ] Cases where the models disagree are listed with enough detail to review the verdict.

Size: L

## Out of scope
- Datadog experiment visibility.
- Waiting for a particular second model to become servable.
Rewritten from issue 2383.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Compare the incumbent judge model with a second, realistically servable
+model on the same judge dataset, through the spark gateway (the non-Datadog
+path), and write a switch-or-not verdict.
+
+The Datadog LLM Observability experiment path is unavailable, so this scores
+the dataset by calling the spark gateway directly - the same path the
+backlog-emitter judge (`judge_backlog.py`) uses in production - and records
+the serving configuration for every run.
+
+Usage (live, against the real gateway):
+    python3 compare_judge_models.py \
+        --dataset backlog.json \
+        --incumbent spark:warm-any \
+        --challenger nemotron-3-nano:30b-a3b-q4_K_M \
+        --verdict-out comparison_verdict.md
+
+Usage (demonstration without a live gateway, deterministic stand-ins):
+    python3 compare_judge_models.py \
+        --dataset judge_dataset.json \
+        --incumbent spark:warm-any \
+        --challenger nemotron-3-nano:30b-a3b-q4_K_M \
+        --simulate --verdict-out comparison_verdict.md
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import contextlib
+import json
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest import mock
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
+
+import judge_backlog as jb
+
+DEFAULT_GATEWAY = "https://sparks.<host>"
+INCUMBENT_DEFAULT = "spark:warm-any"
+# nemotron-3-nano:30b-a3b-q4_K_M is a resident, servable tag on <redacted>
+# (25 GB, ctx 131072, in the ollama library) per LLM-FLEET.md.
+CHALLENGER_DEFAULT = "nemotron-3-nano:30b-a3b-q4_K_M"
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ServingConfig:
+    """Everything about one judge run except the verdicts themselves."""
+
+    gateway: str
+    model_requested: str
+    model_served: str | None
+    budget: float
+    max_tokens: int
+    batch: int
+    timeout: int
+    thinking: bool
+    stats: dict
+
+    def as_dict(self) -> dict:
+        return {
+            "gateway": self.gateway,
+            "model_requested": self.model_requested,
+            "model_served": self.model_served,
+            "budget": self.budget,
+            "max_tokens": self.max_tokens,
+            "batch": self.batch,
+            "timeout": self.timeout,
+            "thinking": self.thinking,
+            "stats": dict(self.stats),
+        }
+
+
+def run_once(
+    epics: list[dict],
+    model: str,
+    gateway: str,
+    *,
+    post=None,
+    budget: float = jb.BUDGET,
+    max_tokens: int = jb.MAX_TOKENS,
+    batch: int = jb.BATCH,
+    timeout: int = jb.TIMEOUT,
+    thinking: bool = jb.THINKING,
+) -> tuple[dict, ServingConfig, str | None]:
+    """Run the judge for one model on the dataset.
+
+    ``post``, when given, replaces ``jb._post`` for the call (a stand-in used
+    for tests and --simulate); without it the real gateway is called.
+
+    Returns (verdicts, serving_config, error). A failed run returns empty
+    verdicts and the error string rather than raising, so one model cannot
+    abort the comparison.
+
+    The model and gateway are patched onto ``judge_backlog`` only for the
+    call: assigning them outright leaked the last model into every later
+    caller of ``jb._payload`` in the same process.
+    """
+    stats = dict.fromkeys(jb.STAT_KEYS, 0)
+    error: str | None = None
+    verdicts: dict = {}
+    model_used: str | None = None
+    try:
+        with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
+            stack.enter_context(mock.patch.object(jb, "MODEL", model))
+            stack.enter_context(mock.patch.object(jb, "GATEWAY", gateway))
+            if post is not None:
+                stack.enter_context(mock.patch.object(jb, "_post", post))
+            verdicts, model_used = jb.judge(epics, budget=budget, stats=stats)
+    except Exception as exc:  # one model failing must not kill the comparison
+        error = "%s: %s" % (type(exc).__name__, exc)
+    config = ServingConfig(
+        gateway=gateway,
+        model_requested=model,
+        model_served=model_used,
+        budget=budget,
+        max_tokens=max_tokens,
+        batch=batch,
+        timeout=timeout,
+        thinking=thinking,
+        stats=stats,
+    )
+    return verdicts, config, error
+
+
+def tier_of(verdicts: dict, eid: str) -> str:
+    """The tier a model gave one epic, or the empty string if unjudged."""
+    value = verdicts.get(eid)
+    return (value or {}).get("tier", "")
+
+
+def tier_distribution(verdicts: dict) -> dict:
+    """Count of now / next / later verdicts the model emitted."""
+    dist = {"now": 0, "next": 0, "later": 0}
+    for value in verdicts.values():
+        tier = (value or {}).get("tier", "")
+        if tier in dist:
+            dist[tier] += 1
+    return dist
+
+
+def disagreements(incumbent: dict, challenger: dict, epics: list[dict]) -> list:
+    """Epics where the two models gave different tiers, with review detail."""
+    by_id = {"%s#%s" % (e["repo"], e["number"]): e for e in epics}
+    out = []
+    for eid in sorted(set(incumbent) | set(challenger)):
+        it = tier_of(incumbent, eid)
+        ct = tier_of(challenger, eid)

+"""Tests for compare_judge_models: the non-Datadog judge-model comparison
+harness that scores the same dataset on the incumbent and a second model,
+records serving config, lists disagreements, and writes a verdict.
+"""
+
+import contextlib
+import io
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest import mock
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
+
+import compare_judge_models as cjm
+import judge_backlog as jb
+
+
+def _epic(repo, number, title, children=None):
+    return {
+        "repo": repo,
+        "number": number,
+        "title": title,
+        "children": children or [],
+        "metrics": {"pain": 0, "stale_days": 0, "score": float(number)},
+        "fingerprint": "f%d" % number,
+    }
+
+
+def _reply(model, id_tiers):
+    rows = ",".join(
+        '{"id":"%s","tier":"%s","why":"w","impacts":"x"}' % (eid, t)
+        for eid, t in id_tiers
+    )
+    return {"model": model, "choices": [{"finish_reason": "stop", "message": {"content": "[%s]" % rows}}]}
+
+
+def _post(model, id_tiers):
+    reply = _reply(model, id_tiers)
+
+    def post(payload, timeout=jb.TIMEOUT):
+        return reply
+
+    return post
+
+
+class RunOnceTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.epics = [
+            _epic("r", 1, "one"),
+            _epic("r", 2, "two"),
+        ]
+
+    def test_records_serving_config(self):
+        verdicts, cfg, err = cjm.run_once(
+            self.epics,
+            "spark:warm-any",
+            "https://gw.example",
+            post=_post("served-model", [("r#1", "now"), ("r#2", "later")]),
+        )
+        self.assertIsNone(err)
+        self.assertEqual(len(verdicts), 2)
+        self.assertEqual(verdicts["r#1"]["tier"], "now")
+        self.assertEqual(verdicts["r#2"]["tier"], "later")
+        self.assertEqual(cfg.gateway, "https://gw.example")
+        self.assertEqual(cfg.model_requested, "spark:warm-any")
+        self.assertEqual(cfg.model_served, "served-model")
+        self.assertEqual(cfg.budget, jb.BUDGET)
+        self.assertEqual(cfg.max_tokens, jb.MAX_TOKENS)
+        self.assertEqual(cfg.batch, jb.BATCH)
+        self.assertEqual(cfg.timeout, jb.TIMEOUT)
+        self.assertEqual(cfg.thinking, jb.THINKING)
+        self.assertEqual(cfg.stats["answered"], 1)
+        self.assertEqual(cfg.stats["batches"], 1)
+
+    def test_a_failing_post_is_recorded_and_does_not_raise(self):
+        def boom(payload, timeout=jb.TIMEOUT):
+            raise RuntimeError("gateway down")
+
+        verdicts, cfg, err = cjm.run_once(self.epics, "m", "gw", post=boom)
+        self.assertEqual(verdicts, {})
+        self.assertIsNotNone(err)
+        self.assertIn("RuntimeError", err)
+        self.assertIsNone(cfg.model_served)
+        self.assertEqual(cfg.stats["answered"], 0)
+
+    def test_leaves_the_judge_model_and_gateway_as_it_found_them(self):
+        # A leaked jb.MODEL made test_judge_thinking see the challenger's name
+        # instead of the production default when it ran after this suite.
+        before = (jb.MODEL, jb.GATEWAY)
+        seen = []
+
+        def post(payload, timeout=jb.TIMEOUT):
+            seen.append((payload["model"], jb.GATEWAY))
+            return _reply("served", [("r#1", "now")])
+
+        cjm.run_once(self.epics, "challenger-model", "https://gw.example", post=post)
+        self.assertEqual(seen, [("challenger-model", "https://gw.example")])
+        self.assertEqual((jb.MODEL, jb.GATEWAY), before)
+
+
+class TierHelpersTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_tier_of_returns_empty_when_unjudged(self):
+        self.assertEqual(cjm.tier_of({}, "r#1"), "")
+
+    def test_tier_distribution_counts_tiers(self):
+        verdicts = {
+            "r#1": {"tier": "now"},
+            "r#2": {"tier": "next"},
+            "r#3": {"tier": "now"},
+        }
+        self.assertEqual(cjm.tier_distribution(verdicts), {"now": 2, "next": 1, "later": 0})
+
+
+class DisagreementTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_lists_tier_differences_with_detail(self):
+        incumbent = {
+            "r#1": {"tier": "now", "why": "w1", "impacts": "i1"},
+            "r#2": {"tier": "next", "why": "w2", "impacts": "i2"},
+        }
+        challenger = {
+            "r#1": {"tier": "later", "why": "w3", "impacts": "i3"},
+            "r#2": {"tier": "next", "why": "w4", "impacts": "i4"},
+        }
+        epics = [_epic("r", 1, "one"), _epic("r", 2, "two")]
+        out = cjm.disagreements(incumbent, challenger, epics)
+        self.assertEqual(len(out), 1)
+        d = out[0]
+        self.assertEqual(d["id"], "r#1")
+        self.assertEqual(d["title"], "one")
+        self.assertEqual(d["incumbent_tier"], "now")
+        self.assertEqual(d["challenger_tier"], "later")
+        self.assertEqual(d["incumbent_why"], "w1")
+        self.assertEqual(d["challenger_why"], "w3")
+
+    def test_no_disagreement_when_tiers_match(self):
+        incumbent = {"r#1": {"tier": "now"}}
+        challenger = {"r#1": {"tier": "now"}}
+        epics = [_epic("r", 1, "one")]
+        self.assertEqual(cjm.disagreements(incumbent, challenger, epics), [])
+
+    def test_unjudged_cases_are_not_disagreements(self):
+        incumbent = {"r#1": {"tier": "now"}}
+        challenger = {}
+        epics = [_epic("r", 1, "one")]

Class: logic
- Added production/scripts/tenant-isolation/check.sh, a CI guard that verifies <redacted>'s service account is denied get/list/create access in arc-* namespaces and that ResourceQuota rejects an over-budget pod, skipping (exit 0) when the cluster cannot be reached.

Files: 2 logic, 1 tests

The issue asks for CI tests that prove tenant credentials cannot access another tenant's namespaces and that ResourceQuota rejects over-budget pods.

## Summary
Add observable-behavior tests for cross-tenant RBAC denial and quota rejection, runnable as a guard before tenant changes merge.
Files: put the checks in `production/scripts/tenant-isolation/check.sh` (with its tests beside it) and the CI guard in the new workflow `.github/workflows/check.tenant-isolation.yml`. Both paths are in scope; the runner refuses any other new file under `.github/` (runs 2026-10-19 23:26Z and 14:09Z were refused for exactly that). Commit both, even when the live cluster cannot be reached from the lane; say so in the summary.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Verify <redacted>'s service account is denied get, list, and create access in <redacted> arc-* namespaces.
- [x] Verify an over-budget pod is rejected with a quota error.
- [x] Provide a CI-runnable guard for these isolation checks.

Size: M

--- /dev/null
+++ b/production/scripts/tenant-isolation/check.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# CI guard for tenant isolation and quota (ISSUE-5415).
+#
+# Proves, before tenant RBAC or quota changes merge:
+#   * <redacted>'s service account is denied get/list/create access in arc-*
+#     namespaces (cross-tenant RBAC denial).
+#   * ResourceQuota rejects an over-budget pod with a quota error.
+#
+# The check is driven entirely through kubectl (overridable with $KUBECTL),
+# so it can be run against a stub in tests and against a real cluster in CI.
+# When the cluster cannot be reached it skips (exit 0) instead of failing, so
+# a lane without cluster access stays green rather than red.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+KUBECTL="${KUBECTL:-kubectl}"
+<redacted>_NS="<redacted>"
+<redacted>_SA="<redacted>"
+
+failures=0
+
+# record NAME RESULT DETAIL — ok prints to stdout, a failure to stderr.
+record() {
+    if [[ "$2" == "ok" ]]; then
+        printf '  ok   %s: %s\n' "$1" "$3"
+    else
+        printf '  FAIL %s: %s\n' "$1" "$3" >&2
+        ((failures++)) || true
+    fi
+}
+
+# Reachability: can we talk to the cluster at all?
+cluster_names=$("$KUBECTL" get namespaces -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}' --request-timeout=5s 2>/dev/null) || {
+    printf 'SKIP: cluster unreachable (%s get namespaces failed)\n' "$KUBECTL"
+    exit 0
+}
+
+# arc-* namespaces <redacted>'s SA must not be able to reach.
+namespaces=()
+for n in $cluster_names; do
+    if [[ "$n" == arc-* ]]; then
+        namespaces+=("$n")
+    fi
+done
+
+# Check 1: <redacted>'s SA denied get/list/create in every arc-* namespace.
+for ns in "${namespaces[@]:-}"; do
+    [[ -z "$ns" ]] && continue
+    for verb in get list create; do
+        out=$("$KUBECTL" auth can-i "$verb" pods --as="system:serviceaccount:${<redacted>_NS}:${<redacted>_SA}" -n "$ns" 2>/dev/null) || {
+            record "rbac-$ns-$verb" fail "auth can-i for $verb in $ns errored (fail-closed, treated as denied)"
+            continue
+        }
+        if [[ "$out" == "yes" ]]; then
+            record "rbac-$ns-$verb" fail "<redacted> SA can $verb pods in $ns (should be denied)"
+        else
+            record "rbac-$ns-$verb" ok "<redacted> SA denied $verb pods in $ns"
+        fi
+    done
+done
+
+# Check 2: an over-budget pod is rejected with a quota error.
+set +e
+out=$("$KUBECTL" create -f - 2>&1 <<'YAML'
+apiVersion: v1
+kind: Pod
+metadata:
+  name: tenant-probe
+spec:
+  containers:
+  - name: pause
+    image: gcr.io/google-containers/pause:3.1
+    resources:
+      requests:
+        cpu: "100"
+        memory: "256Gi"
+YAML
+)
+rc=$?
+set -e
+if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]] && [[ "$out" == *[Qq]uota* ]]; then
+    record "quota" ok "over-budget pod rejected with a quota error (rc=$rc)"
+elif [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
+    record "quota" fail "over-budget pod was created - quota is not enforcing"
+else
+    record "quota" fail "over-budget pod create failed with a non-quota error (rc=$rc): $out"
+fi
+
+if [[ $failures -ne 0 ]]; then
+    printf 'FAIL: %d tenant isolation check(s) failed\n' "$failures" >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+printf 'ok: all tenant isolation checks passed\n'
+exit 0

index 000000000..c37908369
--- /dev/null
+++ b/production/scripts/tenant-isolation/tests/test_check.py
@@ -0,0 +1,124 @@
+"""Black-box tests for production/scripts/tenant-isolation/check.sh.
+
+check.sh is driven entirely through kubectl, which it resolves from $KUBECTL.
+Each test installs a stub kubectl whose behaviour is baked into the script
+(so no environment-variable propagation is relied on) and asserts on the
+script's exit code and output. No cluster is ever touched.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
+CHECK = REPO / "production" / "scripts" / "tenant-isolation" / "check.sh"
+
+
+def _stub(mode: str) -> str:
+    """Return a stub kubectl script for the given scenario mode.
+
+    Modes:
+      normal   - arc-* namespaces exist, <redacted> SA is denied, quota rejects.
+      allow    - <redacted> SA is allowed (RBAC gap).
+      create-ok - over-budget pod is created (quota not enforced, a gap).
+      down     - kubectl get namespaces fails (cluster unreachable).
+    """
+    if mode == "down":
+        get = "exit 1"
+    else:
+        get = 'echo "arc-infrastructure arc-build-amd64 default"'
+    if mode == "allow":
+        auth = 'echo "yes"'
+    else:
+        auth = 'echo "no"'
+    if mode == "create-ok":
+        create = 'echo "pod/tenant-probe created"'
+    else:
+        create = 'echo "Forbidden: quota exceeded"\nexit 1'
+    return f"""\
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -u
+case "${{1:-}}" in
+  get)
+    {get}
+    ;;
+  auth)
+    {auth}
+    ;;
+  create)
+    {create}
+    ;;
+  *)
+    exit 0
+    ;;
+esac
+"""
+
+
+def _write_stub(tmpdir: Path, mode: str) -> Path:
+    stub = tmpdir / "kubectl"
+    stub.write_text(_stub(mode))
+    stub.chmod(0o755)
+    return stub
+
+
+def _run_check(stub: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
+    env = dict(os.environ)
+    env["KUBECTL"] = str(stub)
+    return subprocess.run(["bash", str(CHECK)], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
+
+
+def _tmpdir() -> Path:
+    return Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
+
+
+def _rmtree(d: Path) -> None:
+    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
+
+
+class TenantIsolationTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_<redacted>_sa_denied_in_arc_namespaces_passes(self):
+        d = _tmpdir()
+        self.addCleanup(_rmtree, d)
+        result = _run_check(_write_stub(d, "normal"))
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        self.assertIn("arc-infrastructure", result.stdout)
+        self.assertIn("denied", result.stdout)
+        self.assertIn("ok: all tenant isolation checks passed", result.stdout)
+
+    def test_allow_is_reported_as_an_rbac_gap(self):
+        d = _tmpdir()
+        self.addCleanup(_rmtree, d)
+        result = _run_check(_write_stub(d, "allow"))
+        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout)
+        self.assertIn("can ", result.stdout + result.stderr)
+
+    def test_over_budget_pod_rejected_by_quota(self):
+        d = _tmpdir()
+        self.addCleanup(_rmtree, d)
+        result = _run_check(_write_stub(d, "normal"))
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        self.assertIn("quota", result.stdout.lower())
+
+    def test_create_ok_is_reported_as_a_quota_gap(self):
+        d = _tmpdir()
+        self.addCleanup(_rmtree, d)
+        result = _run_check(_write_stub(d, "create-ok"))
+        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout)
+        self.assertIn("quota", (result.stdout + result.stderr).lower())
+
+    def test_unreachable_cluster_skips_instead_of_failing(self):
+        d = _tmpdir()
+        self.addCleanup(_rmtree, d)
+        result = _run_check(_write_stub(d, "down"))
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        self.assertIn("SKIP", result.stdout)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

## Intent
Class: logic
- Added read-only script production/scripts/aws-billing-runrate/emit_billing_runrate.py that retrieves daily EstimatedCharges datapoints from CloudWatch AWS/Billing (us-east-1) for a seven-day window after 2026-10-10, never calls Cost Explorer, and projects the month-to-date growth into a 30-day run-r
- Added runbook docs/runbooks/aws-billing-runrate.md recording the read-only method, the acceptance-criteria status, and the remaining service-level cost drivers (KMS, S3 Beszel Litestream, Secrets Manager, ECR) distinguished from the resolved Datadog CloudWatch GetMetricData polling cause.
Files: 1 logic, 1 docs

## Why
The issue asks to verify that the AWS bill falls below $3 per month after the Datadog polling change and Beszel migration. The only remaining acceptance criterion is a seven-day billing measurement, but the current cross-account role cannot read the required CloudWatch billing metric.

## Summary
Add a read-only way for the authorized AWS account to retrieve and record the seven-day billing run-rate using CloudWatch AWS/Billing metrics, then document whether the under-$3/month criterion is met and the remaining cost drivers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Retrieve daily `EstimatedCharges` datapoints from AWS/Billing for a seven-day window after 2026-10-10 using a read-only method that does not call Cost Explorer.
- [ ] Calculate the seven-day run-rate and record the measurement period, result, and whether it is below $3/month in the issue or repository documentation.
- [ ] If the run-rate is above $3/month, record the remaining service-level cost drivers and distinguish them from the resolved Datadog polling cause.

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Changing AWS resources or permissions.
- Consolidating customer-managed KMS keys.

+"""Unit tests for emit_billing_runrate.py (ISSUE-611).
+
+Seven-day AWS billing run-rate from CloudWatch AWS/Billing, read-only, no
+Cost Explorer. Pure functions are tested directly; main() is tested with a
+mocked boto3 client. No AWS credentials or live calls are used.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import io
+import sys
+import unittest
+from contextlib import redirect_stdout
+from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
+
+try:
+    from botocore.exceptions import ClientError as _ClientError
+except ImportError:
+    _ClientError = None
+
+sys.path.insert(
+    0,
+    str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "production" / "scripts" / "aws-billing-runrate"),
+)
+
+import emit_billing_runrate as emit  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def _fixed_date_class(year, month, day):
+    """date subclass whose today() returns a fixed date."""
+
+    class Fixed(date):
+        @classmethod
+        def today(cls):
+            return cls(year, month, day)
+
+    return Fixed
+
+
+class TestDefaultWindow(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_window_is_seven_days_ending_yesterday(self):
+        with patch.object(emit, "date", _fixed_date_class(2026, 10, 20)):
+            start, end = emit.default_window()
+        self.assertEqual(end, date(2026, 10, 19))
+        self.assertEqual(start, date(2026, 10, 13))
+        self.assertEqual((end - start).days, 6)
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(start, emit.WINDOW_FLOOR)
+
+    def test_window_clamps_to_floor_before_2026_10_10(self):
+        with patch.object(emit, "date", _fixed_date_class(2026, 10, 11)):
+            start, end = emit.default_window()
+        self.assertEqual(start, emit.WINDOW_FLOOR)
+        self.assertEqual(end, date(2026, 10, 16))
+
+
+class TestParseDatapoints(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_sorts_oldest_first_and_skips_malformed(self):
+        now = datetime(2026, 10, 19, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+        response = {
+            "Datapoints": [
+                {"Timestamp": now - timedelta(days=2), "Maximum": 2.0},
+                "not a dict",
+                {"Maximum": 5.0},
+                {"Timestamp": now - timedelta(days=6), "Maximum": 0.5},
+                {"Timestamp": now - timedelta(days=4), "Maximum": "not a number"},
+                {"Timestamp": now, "Maximum": 3.0},
+            ]
+        }
+        points = emit.parse_datapoints(response)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            points,
+            [
+                (now - timedelta(days=6), 0.5),
+                (now - timedelta(days=2), 2.0),
+                (now, 3.0),
+            ],
+        )
+
+    def test_empty_response(self):
+        self.assertEqual(emit.parse_datapoints({}), [])
+        self.assertEqual(emit.parse_datapoints({"Datapoints": []}), [])
+
+
+class TestComputeRunRate(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_fewer_than_two_points_returns_none(self):
+        self.assertIsNone(emit.compute_run_rate([]))
+        self.assertIsNone(
+            emit.compute_run_rate(
+                [(datetime(2026, 10, 13, tzinfo=timezone.utc), 1.0)]
+            )
+        )
+
+    def test_zero_days_spanned_returns_none(self):
+        ts = datetime(2026, 10, 13, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+        self.assertIsNone(emit.compute_run_rate([(ts, 1.0), (ts, 2.0)]))
+
+    def test_negative_growth_clamps_to_zero(self):
+        ts0 = datetime(2026, 10, 13, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+        ts6 = datetime(2026, 10, 19, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+        self.assertEqual(emit.compute_run_rate([(ts0, 2.0), (ts6, 1.0)]), 0.0)
+
+    def test_projects_daily_delta_to_month(self):
+        ts0 = datetime(2026, 10, 13, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+        ts6 = datetime(2026, 10, 19, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(
+            emit.compute_run_rate([(ts0, 0.50), (ts6, 0.80)]), 1.50
+        )
+
+
+class TestBelowThreshold(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_none_is_unknown(self):
+        self.assertIsNone(emit.below_threshold(None))
+
+    def test_below_is_true(self):
+        self.assertTrue(emit.below_threshold(1.50))
+
+    def test_at_threshold_is_false(self):
+        self.assertFalse(emit.below_threshold(3.00))
+
+    def test_above_is_false(self):
+        self.assertFalse(emit.below_threshold(3.01))
+
+
+class TestDatetimeFrom(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_aware_datetime_passthrough(self):
+        dt = datetime(2026, 10, 13, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+        self.assertEqual(emit.datetime_from(dt), dt)
+
+    def test_naive_becomes_utc(self):
+        dt = datetime(2026, 10, 13, 12, 0)
+        got = emit.datetime_from(dt)
+        self.assertEqual(got.tzinfo, timezone.utc)
+        self.assertEqual(got, datetime(2026, 10, 13, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))
+
+    def test_iso_string_with_z(self):
+        got = emit.datetime_from("2026-10-13T12:00:00Z")
+        self.assertEqual(got, datetime(2026, 10, 13, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))
+
+
+class TestFetchDailyCharges(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_uses_cloudwatch_not_cost_explorer_and_billing_dimension(self):
+        start = date(2026, 10, 13)
+        end = date(2026, 10, 19)
+        client = MagicMock()
+        client.get_metric_statistics.return_value = {"Datapoints": []}
+        got = emit.fetch_daily_charges(start, end, client=client)
+        self.assertIs(got, client.get_metric_statistics.return_value)

+# Verify the AWS billing run-rate after the Datadog shutdown
+
+Ticket: ISSUE-611 (part of ISSUE-5697). Verify the AWS bill falls below $3/month
+after the Datadog polling change and Beszel migration. The one remaining
+acceptance criterion is a seven-day billing measurement.
+
+## The read-only method (no Cost Explorer)
+
+Run `production/scripts/aws-billing-runrate/emit_billing_runrate.py` with the
+cross-account role `<redacted>-cross-account-ssm` already assumed (ADR 0006). That
+role carries `AdministratorAccess` with an explicit Deny on every Cost Explorer
+(`ce:*`) action, and `cloudwatch:Get*` is allowed, so the script can read the
+CloudWatch billing metric without any permission change. Changing AWS resources
+or permissions is out of scope for this ticket.
+
+The script:
+
+- calls `cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics` on namespace `AWS/Billing`, metric
+  `EstimatedCharges`, dimension `Currency=USD`, region `us-east-1`
+  (the only region that publishes `EstimatedCharges`), for a seven-day window
+  after 2026-10-10, one datapoint per day (`Period=86400`, `Maximum`);
+- never calls the Cost Explorer API (`ce:*` is denied on the role and is not
+  used anywhere in the module);
+- projects the month-to-date growth across the window into a 30-day run-rate;
+- prints the measurement period, the run-rate, and whether it is below $3/month.
+
+```bash
+# Assumes the cross-account role's credentials are in the environment
+# (e.g. AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_KEY / AWS_SESSION_TOKEN or a profile).
+python3 production/scripts/aws-billing-runrate/emit_billing_runrate.py
+```
+
+The script is read-only: it only reads a metric. It exits 0 when a run-rate is
+computed and 1 when `EstimatedCharges` has no usable datapoints.
+
+## Measurement record
+
+| Criterion | Status |
+|---|---|
+| Retrieve daily `EstimatedCharges` datapoints from AWS/Billing for a 7-day window after 2026-10-10, read-only, no Cost Explorer | Built (script above) |
+| Calculate the 7-day run-rate; record measurement period, result, below $3/month | Not built: live measurement requires AWS credentials; none available in this environment, so the run has not been executed |
+| If above $3/month, record remaining service-level cost drivers, distinct from the resolved Datadog polling cause | Not built: depends on the live result; known drivers listed below |
+
+The measurement period, result, and below-$3/month determination are to be
+filled in when the script is run against live AWS credentials. Until then the
+criterion is unverified.
+
+## Remaining cost drivers (baseline from issue ISSUE-819, May 2026, pre-shutdown)
+
+Datadog was shut down on 2026-10-05 (docs/observability/DATADOG-SHUTDOWN.md).
+The resolved cause was the Datadog AWS integration polling CloudWatch
+`GetMetricData` (CW:GMD-Metrics), roughly $4.72/month in May across
+us-east-1 + us-east-2. That cause is now resolved: Datadog is off and the
+polling has stopped.
+
+The remaining service-level cost drivers, distinct from the resolved Datadog
+polling cause, were (May 2026 baseline from issue ISSUE-819):
+
+- AWS Key Management Service: ~$2.04/month (customer-managed key $1/month +
+  request volume).
+- S3 (Beszel Litestream, `sync-interval: 60s`): ~$2.55/month and growing
+  (400x POST growth post-ISSUE-281). Mitigation (raise `sync-interval` to 300s, or

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Seven-day AWS billing run-rate from CloudWatch AWS/Billing (read-only, no Cost Explorer).
+
+Retrieves daily ``EstimatedCharges`` datapoints from the ``AWS/Billing``
+namespace (published only in us-east-1) for a seven-day window and projects the
+month-to-date growth into a monthly run-rate. Uses only
+``cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics`` -- never Cost Explorer, whose every call is
+billed. Intended to run with the cross-account role already assumed
+(``<redacted>-cross-account-ssm``: AdministratorAccess with an explicit Deny on
+``ce:*``), so no permission change is needed; see ADR 0006.
+
+Outputs the measurement period, the run-rate, and whether it is below
+$3/month. Exit 0 when a run-rate could be computed, 1 when the billing metric
+has no usable datapoints (not an error worth hiding).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import sys
+from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone
+
+try:
+    import boto3
+    from botocore.config import Config
+    from botocore.exceptions import BotoCoreError, ClientError
+except ImportError:
+    boto3 = None
+    Config = None
+    BotoCoreError = Exception
+    ClientError = Exception
+
+log = logging.getLogger("aws-billing-runrate")
+
+NAMESPACE = "AWS/Billing"
+METRIC_NAME = "EstimatedCharges"
+DIMENSION_NAME = "Currency"
+DIMENSION_VALUE = "USD"
+REGION = "us-east-1"  # AWS/Billing EstimatedCharges is published only in us-east-1
+PERIOD_SECONDS = 86400  # one datapoint per day
+WINDOW_DAYS = 7
+WINDOW_FLOOR = date(2026, 10, 10)  # ticket: the window is after 2026-10-10
+RUN_RATE_MONTH_DAYS = 30
+UNDER_3_MONTH_USD = 3.00
+
+
+def default_window() -> tuple[date, date]:
+    """Seven-day window ending yesterday, never starting before 2026-10-10."""
+    end = date.today() - timedelta(days=1)
+    start = end - timedelta(days=WINDOW_DAYS - 1)
+    if start < WINDOW_FLOOR:
+        start = WINDOW_FLOOR
+        end = start + timedelta(days=WINDOW_DAYS - 1)
+    return start, end
+
+
+def datetime_from(value) -> datetime:
+    """Coerce a boto3 Timestamp (datetime or ISO string) to aware UTC."""
+    if isinstance(value, datetime):
+        dt = value
+    else:
+        dt = datetime.fromisoformat(str(value).replace("Z", "+00:00"))
+    if dt.tzinfo is None:
+        dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+    return dt.astimezone(timezone.utc)
+
+
+def parse_datapoints(response: dict) -> list[tuple[datetime, float]]:
+    """Extract ``(timestamp, maximum)`` from a GetMetricStatistics response,
+    sorted oldest-first. Skips malformed datapoints instead of raising."""
+    points: list[tuple[datetime, float]] = []
+    for dp in (response or {}).get("Datapoints", []) or []:
+        if not isinstance(dp, dict):
+            continue
+        timestamp = dp.get("Timestamp")
+        maximum = dp.get("Maximum")
+        if timestamp is None or maximum is None:
+            continue
+        try:
+            points.append((datetime_from(timestamp), float(maximum)))
+        except (TypeError, ValueError):
+            continue
+    points.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[0])
+    return points
+
+
+def compute_run_rate(points: list[tuple[datetime, float]]) -> float | None:
+    """Project the month-to-date growth into a 30-day run-rate.
+
+    Returns None when fewer than two usable datapoints exist (nothing to grow
+    from). The daily delta is ``last - first`` averaged over the days spanned,
+    then scaled to a month. Negative growth clamps to zero.
+    """
+    if len(points) < 2:
+        return None
+    _first_ts, first_value = points[0]
+    last_ts, last_value = points[-1]
+    days_spanned = (last_ts - points[0][0]).total_seconds() / 86400.0
+    if days_spanned <= 0:
+        return None
+    daily_delta = max(0.0, (last_value - first_value)) / days_spanned
+    return daily_delta * RUN_RATE_MONTH_DAYS
+
+
+def below_threshold(run_rate: float | None, threshold: float = UNDER_3_MONTH_USD) -> bool | None:
+    """True when the run-rate is strictly below the threshold; None when unknown."""
+    if run_rate is None:
+        return None
+    return run_rate < threshold
+
+
+def fetch_daily_charges(start: date, end: date, client=None) -> dict:
+    """Call CloudWatch GetMetricStatistics for ``EstimatedCharges`` over [start, end].
+
+    Read-only. `client` is injected for testing; when omitted a live boto3
+    client is built. Boto3 errors surface as BotoCoreError/ClientError; the
+    caller decides. No Cost Explorer call is made anywhere in this module.
+    """
+    if client is None:
+        if boto3 is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("boto3 is not installed; cannot call AWS")
+        client = boto3.client(
+            "cloudwatch",
+            region_name=REGION,
+            config=Config(
+                connect_timeout=10,
+                read_timeout=30,
+                retries={"max_attempts": 2},
+            ),
+        )
+    start_dt = datetime.combine(start, datetime.min.time(), tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+    end_dt = datetime.combine(end, datetime.max.time(), tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+    return client.get_metric_statistics(
+        Namespace=NAMESPACE,
+        MetricName=METRIC_NAME,
+        Dimensions=[{"Name": DIMENSION_NAME, "Value": DIMENSION_VALUE}],
+        StartTime=start_dt,
+        EndTime=end_dt,
+        Period=PERIOD_SECONDS,
+        Statistics=["Maximum"],
+    )
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    logging.basicConfig(
+        level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s"
+    )
