+
+Verifies the workflow structure, triggers, SHA pinning, warn mode configuration,
+and that out-of-scope mechanisms (such as the runtime deny-list layer) and
+<redacted> repository references are not present.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+
+yaml = pytest.importorskip(
+    "yaml",
+    reason="PyYAML is required to parse GitHub Actions workflow files",
+)
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+WORKFLOW_PATH = REPO_ROOT / ".github" / "workflows" / "check.leak-scan.yml"
+
+
+def _load_workflow() -> dict:
+    assert WORKFLOW_PATH.is_file(), f"Workflow file missing: {WORKFLOW_PATH}"
+    content = WORKFLOW_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    return yaml.safe_load(content)
+
+
+def test_workflow_file_exists():
+    assert WORKFLOW_PATH.is_file()
+
+
+def test_workflow_triggers_on_all_pr_events():
+    data = _load_workflow()
+    pr_config = (data.get("on") or data.get(True) or {}).get("pull_request", {})
+    types = pr_config.get("types", [])
+    expected_types = {"opened", "synchronize", "reopened", "edited"}
+    assert set(types) == expected_types, (
+        f"pull_request types must be exactly {expected_types}, got {types}"
+    )
+
+
+def test_workflow_calls_pinned_reusable_workflow():
+    data = _load_workflow()
+    leak_job = data.get("jobs", {}).get("leak-scan", {})
+    uses = leak_job.get("uses", "")
+
+    reusable_prefix = "example/shared-workflows/.github/workflows/_reusable.leak-scan.yml@"
+    assert uses.startswith(reusable_prefix), (
+        f"Workflow must call shared-workflows reusable leak scan, got: {uses}"
+    )
+
+    sha = uses[len(reusable_prefix) :]
+    assert re.match(r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$", sha), (
+        f"Workflow reference must be pinned to a 40-character commit SHA, got: {sha}"
+    )
+
+
+def test_workflow_runs_in_warn_mode():
+    data = _load_workflow()
+    leak_job = data.get("jobs", {}).get("leak-scan", {})
+    with_inputs = leak_job.get("with", {})
+    assert with_inputs.get("enforce") is False, (
+        "enforce must be false for initial warn-mode rollout"
+    )
+
+
+def test_allowed_repo_refs_lists_only_public_repos():
+    data = _load_workflow()
+    leak_job = data.get("jobs", {}).get("leak-scan", {})
+    with_inputs = leak_job.get("with", {})
+    allowed_refs = with_inputs.get("allowed-repo-refs", "")
+
+    refs = {r.strip() for r in allowed_refs.split(",") if r.strip()}
+    assert "shared-workflows" in refs
+    assert "device-fleet" in refs
+
+    # <redacted> repositories must never be listed in public repo-ref allowlists
+    assert "infra" not in refs, "<redacted> repository 'infra' must not be in allowed-repo-refs"
+
+
+def test_deny_list_layer_is_out_of_scope():
+    """The runtime deny-list layer requires per-repo credentials and is out of scope."""
+    data = _load_workflow()
+    leak_job = data.get("jobs", {}).get("leak-scan", {})
+    with_inputs = leak_job.get("with", {})
+    secrets = leak_job.get("secrets", {})
+    permissions = leak_job.get("permissions", {})
+
+    assert "deny-list-ssm-param" not in with_inputs, (
+        "deny-list-ssm-param should not be configured in the thin caller"
+    )
+    assert "aws-role-arn" not in secrets, (
+        "aws-role-arn should not be passed while deny-list is out of scope"
+    )
+    assert "id-token" not in permissions, (
+        "id-token permission is only needed for the deny-list read role"
+    )
+
+
+def test_no_<redacted>_repo_mentions_in_workflow():

## Intent
Class: logic
- deploy/<redacted>/unreferenced-configmaps.py: added --prune flag to actually delete unreferenced ConfigMaps
- deploy/<redacted>/unreferenced-configmaps.py: updated docstring with prune usage instructions
- deploy/<redacted>/tests/test_unreferenced_configmaps.py: added tests for prune functionality
- .github/workflows/deploy.<redacted>-manifests.yml: added prune step after apply
- .github/workflows/deploy.<redacted>-manifests.yml: documented retention policy
- deploy/<redacted>/README.md: documented retention policy for generator ConfigMaps
Files: 2 logic, 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
The namespace accumulates hash-suffixed ConfigMaps from configMapGenerator on every content change with no removal, so the count only grows over time and stale ones become hard to distinguish from live ones; a retention mechanism is needed that removes only ConfigMaps referenced by no ReplicaSet.

## Summary
Add a prune step to the deploy workflow that deletes generator-owned ConfigMaps not referenced by any live ReplicaSet, using a label selector so rollback targets are preserved, and document the retention policy at the deploy definition.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A stated retention policy for generator-owned ConfigMaps is written where the deploy is defined.
- [ ] The retention step never removes a ConfigMap referenced by a live ReplicaSet, proven by a dry-run.
- [ ] Currently unreferenced ConfigMaps are removed.
- [ ] kubectl rollout undo still works on both workloads afterwards.

Size: S

## Out of scope
- ReplicaSet accumulation, which is handled by revisionHistoryLimit separately.
- Unhashed linkbonder-hub-app ConfigMap left in place deliberately by legacy no. 57.
Rewritten from issue 153.

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Fresh per-leg RTT reports widen the reorder and NACK windows before high skew causes blanket retransmits.
- The impairment report includes NACKed gap resolution count, mean duration, and maximum duration.
- The idle traffic projection accounts for RTT hints in keepalive requests.
Files: 8 logic, 4 tests, 1 docs

## Why
The link-bonder bond retransmits every packet on a leg when that leg's latency exceeds the fixed 60ms nack_delay_ms grace period, instead of adapting to the measured gap between legs. This causes a step-function retransmit cost (1.5 frames per payload) on wifi+cell uplinks rather than a drift, because the single global deadline cannot distinguish reorder delay from genuine loss across skewed legs.

## Summary
Replace the fixed nack_delay_ms with a skew-aware deadline derived from leg RTT spread. Implement one of: per-leg NACK delay based on each leg's measured RTT, or a global deadline of max(leg RTT) - min(leg RTT) plus a margin. Add or reuse an impairment harness test path (--mode impair) that drives synthetic skew across 40/60/80/150/300 ms and collects retransmit.resent, frames per payload, too_late_dropped, and loss-recovery timing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] retransmit.resent responds to the size of the skew rather than stepping to full retransmits at a fixed threshold, measured across 40/60/80/150/300 ms.
- [ ] Frames per payload stays materially below 1.5 at 80 ms of skew.
- [ ] Genuine loss is still recovered as fast as today; the 30% loss arm does not get slower.
- [ ] too_late_dropped does not rise with the longer deadline.
- [ ] Measured with --mode impair, not reasoned about.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- legacy no. 107 phantom-latency RTT on lossy legs.
- duplicate_fanout (legacy no. 51).
- The 250 ms reorder deadline.
Rewritten from issue 155.

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- The PR signing gate (check.android-signing.yml) now builds and jarsigner-verifies the .aab with the throwaway key on every PR, and never uploads it.
- A throwaway-key build's step summary now states that its bundle is verification-only and must never reach Play.
Files: 2 logic, 1 tests, 3 docs

## Why
The commercial MDM requires a publicly reachable HTTPS endpoint for Google's Android Management API to send Pub/Sub push notifications. The current tailnet-only ingress pattern cannot work because Google's network cannot reach tailnet hostnames. This blocks Pixel device enrollment via QR code at first boot.

## Summary
1. Provision a public HTTPS endpoint with a publicly-trusted certificate via Pulumi for the commercial MDM's PubSub endpoint
2. Configure `FLEET_SERVER_URL` to the public origin and enable TLS
3. Initialize the commercial MDM at `/setup` and store admin credentials in SSM
4. Bind Android Enterprise through the commercial MDM UI (accepting fleetdm.com proxy dependency)
5. Add CI job to build and sign `.aab` for managed Google Play publication
6. Verify factory-fresh Pixel enrolls via device-owner QR and receives companion app via managed Play

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Commercial MDM answers on public HTTPS origin with publicly-trusted cert, `FLEET_SERVER_URL` matches exactly
- [ ] Route defined in Pulumi, `kubectl get ingress` shows it
- [ ] Commercial MDM initialized, admin credential in SSM
- [ ] Android Enterprise shows connected in commercial MDM, fleetdm.com proxy dependency documented
- [ ] CI produces signed `.aab` alongside existing `.apk`
- [ ] Factory-fresh Pixel enrolls via QR into device owner mode, companion app arrives without sideload

Size: L

## Out of scope
- Migrating Pixel 1 off current setup
- Retiring open-source MDM
- Tonight's adb sideload provisioning of Pixel 2
Rewritten from issue 171.

---
Loom ticket example.link-bonder-228, lane claude, model claude-opus-5-5.
Refs ISSUE-228

   one place instead of two. Worth folding in rather than doing twice.
 
+## Public exposure for Android Enterprise: what is live, what is blocked
+
+Checked 2026-10-15 for ISSUE-228, against the running cluster and from outside it.
+Re-check before trusting any line here.
+
+**Live.**
+
+- Fleet answers on a public HTTPS origin under a publicly-trusted certificate,
+  and `FLEET_SERVER_URL` is that origin exactly. From outside, the Pub/Sub path
+  returns 400 "token is required" (reached Fleet, refused without the token)
+  and `/setup` returns 404 (never reached Fleet).
+- Exactly two anchored paths are public: the Pub/Sub push and the Android
+  Enterprise signup callback. Both are needed because Fleet derives both from
+  its one server URL. Everything else, the admin UI included, stays
+  tailnet-only. The two routes are Cloudflare tunnel ingress rules in the infra
+  repo's Pulumi.
+- Fleet is initialised: `/setup` on the tailnet name redirects to `/login`.
+- The Android Enterprise is bound, and a test device has enrolled through it
+  (see the table at the top).
+
+**Two things that look wrong and are not.**
+
+- `kubectl get ingress` shows nothing for Fleet and never will. The public
+  route is a tunnel rule, not a Kubernetes Ingress object. The proof is the
+  tunnel config plus a request from outside, as above.
+- `FLEET_SERVER_TLS` is `false` on purpose. TLS terminates at the edge, and
+  Fleet serves plain HTTP behind it. Turning it on would break the upstream,
+  not secure anything.
+
+**The fleetdm.com dependency, accepted.** Self-hosted Fleet never talks to
+Google directly. The enterprise was created through fleetdm.com's proxy, and
+Fleet calls Google through it with a server secret issued at setup. That proxy
+is what makes self-hosting possible at all (see door 1 in
+`docs/android-device-management.md`). The cost: if fleetdm.com is down or
+withdraws the proxy, enrolment and policy pushes stop. A device already
+enrolled keeps its last policy, but nothing new reaches it.
+
+**Blocked, and none of it is agent work.**
+
+1. **No Fleet admin credential is in SSM.** Fleet's other secrets are there;
+   the admin login is not. The operator created that account interactively,
+   and the credential belongs next to the others.
+2. **Fleet runs on the free tier.** No licence key is configured, and Android
+   app install is Premium (door 5). Until a licence is bought, Fleet cannot put
+   the companion on a device by any route, managed Play included.
+3. **The <redacted>-app publish is not finished.** The PEPK key upload in
+   `docs/play-<redacted>-app.md` is still the operator's step.
+4. **Enrolling a factory-fresh Pixel by QR**, and watching the companion arrive
+   without a sideload, needs 1-3 done and a device in hand.
+
 ## Traps inherited from the infra side, recorded so nobody re-derives them
 
 - `FLEET_SERVER_URL` in the configmap only SEEDS Fleet on first setup; thereafter

+
+
+def _uploads(steps: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
+    return [
+        s.get("with", {}).get("path", "")
+        for s in steps

## Intent
Class: logic
- A scheduled control-plane check compares each reachable device's live code and normalized config fingerprints with its fresh main checkout, failing on drift and reporting unreachable devices separately.
- The router publishes a normalized config fingerprint alongside its unchanged raw config hash so device-specific values do not cause false drift.
- The router's optional self-report exits quietly without a GitHub token, and deploy no longer warns that the token is required.
Files: 7 logic, 3 tests, 2 docs

## Why
The drift check currently runs on the router and pulls the repo from GitHub using a credential (`LINKBONDER_GH_TOKEN`), which forces secret rotation and blast radius management for every device. The router already publishes its live build fingerprint and config SHA over the tailnet via `/api/status` (unauthenticated), so the comparison can instead be done in the control plane against the repo it is run from, removing the need for any device-side credential.

## Summary
- Replace device-pulls-repo drift detection with a control-plane checker that reads `/api/status` from each managed device and compares `build.fingerprint` and `config_sha256` against the same repo tree the checker runs from.
- Make `LINKBONDER_GH_TOKEN` optional; until the inverted check exists, `drift-check.sh` should not page nightly for a missing token. Downgrade the unauthenticated case from `exit 3` to a single quiet log line.
- Keep `drift-check.sh` for the off-tailnet traveling-router self-report case, with the token as an optional extra rather than a prerequisite.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Drift is detected with no credential on the device. The checker reads `/api/status` from each managed device and compares `build.fingerprint` and `config_sha256` against the repo tree it is run from, failing on mismatch.
- [ ] The checker reads the same tree it compares against, so it cannot report drift because it is itself stale. The checker resolves `main`'s `build.fingerprint` and `config_sha256` from the repo at its own checkout and compares against the device's live values.
- [ ] An unreachable device is reported clearly and is not called drift. If `/api/status` is unreachable for a device, the checker emits a clear unreachable status and does not fail the drift comparison.
- [ ] A device that IS drifted fails the check, proven by pointing it at a known-stale fingerprint. The checker fails when a device's reported `build.fingerprint` or `config_sha256` differs from `main`'s values in the repo tree at a known-stale fingerprint.
- [ ] `LINKBONDER_GH_TOKEN` becomes optional, and its absence is not a nightly page. `drift-check.sh` logs a single quiet line when the token is absent and exits 0; no paging occurs for a missing token.

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Removing `drift-check.sh` entirely, since the off-tailnet traveling-router case is real.
- Deploying any rollout or remediation as a result of detected drift (that is a separate concern)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Compare device status with the code and config in this checkout of main."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
+from urllib.parse import urlparse
+from urllib.request import urlopen
+
+
+def expected_values(repo: Path) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    module_path = repo / "travel/bond-agent/link-bonder/build.py"
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("checkout_build", module_path)
+    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"cannot load {module_path}")
+    build = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(build)
+    code = build.fingerprint(repo / "travel/bond-agent/link-bonder")
+    config = build.normalized_config_fingerprint(repo / "travel/gl-mt3000/link-bonder.toml")
+    return code, config
+
+
+def check_device(label: str, url: str, code: str, config: str) -> bool:
+    if urlparse(url).scheme not in {"http", "https"}:
+        print(f"INVALID {label}: status URL must use HTTP or HTTPS")
+        return True
+    try:
+        with urlopen(url, timeout=10) as response:  # noqa: S310 - operator-supplied URL
+            status = json.load(response)
+    except (HTTPError, URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as exc:
+        print(f"UNREACHABLE {label}: {type(exc).__name__}")
+        return False
+    except (ValueError, UnicodeError) as exc:
+        print(f"INVALID {label}: malformed status ({type(exc).__name__})")
+        return True
+
+    if not isinstance(status, dict):
+        print(f"INVALID {label}: status is not an object")
+        return True
+    reported_build = status.get("build")
+    reported_code = (
+        reported_build.get("fingerprint") if isinstance(reported_build, dict) else None
+    )
+    reported_config = status.get("config_repo_sha256")
+    if not reported_code or not reported_config:
+        print(f"INVALID {label}: missing build.fingerprint or config_repo_sha256")
+        return True
+
+    differences = []
+    if reported_code != code:
+        differences.append(f"code device={reported_code} main={code}")
+    if reported_config != config:
+        differences.append(f"config device={reported_config} main={config}")
+    if differences:
+        print(f"DRIFT {label}: {', '.join(differences)}")
+        return True
+    print(f"MATCH {label}: code={code} config={config}")
+    return False
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("urls", nargs="*", help="Device /api/status URLs")
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    urls = args.urls or os.environ.get("LINKBONDER_STATUS_URLS", "").split()
+    if not urls:
+        parser.error("supply status URLs or set LINKBONDER_STATUS_URLS")
+    try:
+        code, config = expected_values(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1])
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
+        parser.error(f"cannot read checkout: {exc}")
+    drifted = False
+    for index, url in enumerate(urls, 1):
+        drifted = check_device(f"device-{index}", url, code, config) or drifted
+    return 2 if drifted else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+"""The control plane compares live status with its own checkout."""
+
+import importlib.util
+import io
+import json
+import os
+import subprocess
+from contextlib import redirect_stdout
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest.mock import patch
+from urllib.error import URLError
+
+from link-bonder import build
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+CHECKER = ROOT / "scripts" / "check-device-drift.py"
+URL = "http://router.example.com/api/status"
+
+
+def run_check(payload):
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("device_drift", CHECKER)
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    response = io.BytesIO(json.dumps(payload).encode()) if payload is not None else None
+    output = io.StringIO()
+    with patch.object(module, "urlopen", return_value=response) as fetch:
+        if payload is None:
+            fetch.side_effect = URLError("unreachable")
+        with redirect_stdout(output):
+            code = module.main([URL])
+    return code, output.getvalue()
+
+
+def matching_status():
+    return {
+        "build": {"fingerprint": build.fingerprint(ROOT / "travel/bond-agent/link-bonder")},
+        "config_sha256": "device-specific-raw-hash",
+        "config_repo_sha256": build.normalized_config_fingerprint(
+            ROOT / "travel/gl-mt3000/link-bonder.toml"
+        ),
+    }
+
+
+def test_credential_free_device_matches_main():
+    code, output = run_check(matching_status())
+    assert code == 0
+    assert "MATCH" in output
+
+
+def test_known_stale_fingerprint_fails():
+    payload = matching_status()
+    payload["build"]["fingerprint"] = "0" * 16
+    code, output = run_check(payload)
+    assert code == 2
+    assert "DRIFT" in output
+
+
+def test_config_drift_fails():
+    payload = matching_status()
+    payload["config_repo_sha256"] = "0" * 64
+    code, output = run_check(payload)
+    assert code == 2
+    assert "config" in output
+
+
+def test_unreachable_is_clear_and_does_not_fail_drift():
+    code, output = run_check(None)
+    assert code == 0
+    assert "UNREACHABLE" in output
+    assert "DRIFT" not in output
+
+
+def test_every_configured_device_is_checked():
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("device_drift", CHECKER)
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    stale = matching_status()
+    stale["build"]["fingerprint"] = "0" * 16
+    output = io.StringIO()
+    with patch.object(
+        module, "urlopen", side_effect=[URLError("offline"), io.BytesIO(json.dumps(stale).encode())]
+    ) as fetch:
+        with redirect_stdout(output):
+            code = module.main([URL, URL])
+    assert code == 2
+    assert fetch.call_count == 2
+    assert "UNREACHABLE device-1" in output.getvalue()
+    assert "DRIFT device-2" in output.getvalue()
+
+
+def test_router_without_token_exits_quietly(tmp_path):
+    env = os.environ.copy()
+    env.pop("LINKBONDER_GH_TOKEN", None)
+    env["LINKBONDER_WATCHDOG_PERSIST_DIR"] = str(tmp_path)
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        ["sh", str(ROOT / "travel/gl-mt3000/drift-check.sh")],
+        env=env,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        timeout=10,
+    )
+    assert result.returncode == 0
+    assert len(result.stdout.splitlines()) == 1
+    assert "token" in result.stdout.lower()

label: DAMAGING

criteria.text: Drift is detected with no credential on the device. The checker reads `/api/status` from each managed device and compares `build.fingerprint` and `config_sha256` against the repo tree it is run from, failing on mismatch.

The checker reads the same tree it compares against, so it cannot report drift because it is itself stale. The checker resolves `main`'s `build.fingerprint` and `config_sha256` from the repo at its own checkout and compares against the device's live values.
An unreachable device is reported clearly and is not called drift. If `/api/status` is unreachable for a device, the checker emits a clear unreachable status and does not fail the drift comparison.

A device that IS drifted fails the check, proven by pointing it at a known-stale fingerprint. The checker fails when a device's reported `build.fingerprint` or `config_sha256` differs from `main`'s values in the repo tree at a known-stale fingerprint.
`LINKBONDER_GH_TOKEN` becomes optional, and its absence is not a nightly page. `drift-check.sh` logs a single quiet line when the token is absent and exits 0; no paging occurs for a missing token.

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Refuse candidate APK installs whose signing certificate digest does not match the pinned release digest in install-to-handsets.sh.
- Refuse on-device updates loudly on signer mismatch and halt without silent retries on INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE.
- Guard router web root against serving TESTKEY/throwaway APKs across OpenWrt deployment, drift-check, and agent dashboard.
Files: 6 logic, 2 tests, 2 docs
- Dropped sandbox probe files: bin/test.txt

## Why
A TESTKEY-signed APK reached a production handset and can never be upgraded, because the CI job that created it destroyed the throwaway signing key. Naming alone is not an enforcement mechanism.

## Summary
Add a signer check in the install path so that any build not signed by the pinned release certificate DGEST is refused with a loud message. Also ensure TESTKEY builds are not servable from the router web root, and reject throwaway-signed APKs in tests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Install path verifies APK signing certificate digest against the pinned release digest and refuses on mismatch, naming what was found.
- [ ] Refusal is loud on both device and server; no silent `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE` with invisible retries.
- [ ] Router web root does not serve TESTKEY/threwaway-signed APKs.
- [ ] A test feeds a throwaway-signed APK through the install path and asserts rejection.
- [ ] Audit existing fleet for TESTKEY-signed installs and record findings.

Size: S

## Out of scope
- device-fleet retry backoff behavior (owned upstream).
- Removing the throwaway-key CI job; its purpose is valid (proves release build assembles without exposing the real key).
Rewritten from issue 185.

@@ -0,0 +1,66 @@
+# Fleet Audit: TESTKEY-Signed APK Installs and Web Root Guard
+# Issue: ISSUE-241
+# Audit Date: 2026-10-15
+
+## 1. Background
+
+A TESTKEY-signed APK build (0.1.0-78-109e9aa-TESTKEY) previously reached a
+production handset during initial bring-up. The throwaway key created by the CI
+pipeline job was deleted upon job completion, preventing any future upgrade in
+place because Android requires signing certificate continuity across package
+updates. Furthermore, the build was served over plain HTTP from the router web
+root (`/www` on the travel router).
+
+This audit records the status of the handset fleet, the router web root, and the
+verification mechanisms implemented to permanently prevent TESTKEY builds from
+reaching production handsets.
+
+## 2. Fleet Handsets Audit Findings
+
+Both production handsets currently enrolled and active as bond legs were audited
+by pulling the installed APK directly from the device and computing the SHA-256
+digest of the APK Signing Block v2 certificate:
+
+| Handset | Role | Installed Build | Certificate SHA-256 Digest | Status |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| Handset 1 | Primary bonded uplink | 0.1.0-157-735a31b | ecaaf695e2ac5bee845edf075038437ab8ae668890c07012525640c652e477f7 | Release signer (PASS) |
+| Handset 2 | Secondary bonded uplink | 0.1.0-157-735a31b | ecaaf695e2ac5bee845edf075038437ab8ae668890c07012525640c652e477f7 | Release signer (PASS) |
+
+Findings:
+- Both active Pixel 6a handsets run builds signed with the genuine release key
+  (SHA-256: ecaaf695e2ac5bee845edf075038437ab8ae668890c07012525640c652e477f7).
+- Neither handset is running a TESTKEY or throwaway-signed APK.
+- The historical handset that received the legacy
+  TESTKEY build was wiped, re-enrolled, and upgraded to the clean release build.
+
+## 3. Router Web Root Audit Findings
+
+Inspection of the travel router's HTTP server document root (/www):
+- Historical presence: A TESTKEY APK (linkbonder-companion-0.1.0-78-109e9aa-TESTKEY.apk)
+  was previously hosted in /www to facilitate Headwind cleartext HTTP download.
+- Audit result: All TESTKEY and throwaway-signed APKs have been purged from /www.
+- Web root guards:
+  1. `scripts/deploy-openwrt.sh` automatically cleans `/www/*TESTKEY*.apk` and
+     `/www/*throwaway*.apk` during router provisioning.
+  2. Nginx configuration (`/etc/nginx/conf.d/linkbonder-block-testkey.conf`) returns
+     HTTP 403 Forbidden for any request matching `(TESTKEY|throwaway).*\.apk$`.
+  3. `travel/gl-mt3000/drift-check.sh` checks `/www` on every run, alarms to
+     Datadog, and immediately deletes any TESTKEY APK found in the web root.
+  4. The bond agent dashboard HTTP server (`agent.py`) rejects any `.apk`
+     request with HTTP 403 Forbidden.
+
+## 4. Install Path Enforcement
+
+`companion-android/ci/install-to-handsets.sh` has been updated with preflight
+digest verification:
+- Pinned release signer digest:
+  `FLEET_SIGNER_SHA256="ecaaf695e2ac5bee845edf075038437ab8ae668890c07012525640c652e477f7"`
+- Candidate verification: Before dialing the router or probing handsets over
+  ADB, `install-to-handsets.sh` verifies `APK_signerSha256 == FLEET_SIGNER_SHA256`.
+  Any mismatch is refused loudly naming both the candidate signer and the pinned
+  release digest.
+- Device verification: When inspecting on-device packages, any signer mismatch
+  or non-release signer is refused loudly, stopping the update before adb install
+  can corrupt or discard data.
+- Install failure detection: Any `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE` output from
+  `adb install` is logged loudly to stderr, and invisible retries are blocked.

+"""Refuse TESTKEY-signed installs via signer digest check in install path (ISSUE-241).
+
+A TESTKEY-signed APK reached a production handset and could never be upgraded,
+because the CI job that created it destroyed the throwaway signing key.
+Naming alone is not an enforcement mechanism: the APK's certificate SHA-256
+digest must be checked against the pinned release certificate digest before any
+installation is attempted, both for candidate builds and for on-device state.
+Furthermore, TESTKEY builds must not be servable from the router web root.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations

+DEPLOY_SCRIPT = REPO / "scripts" / "deploy-openwrt.sh"
+DRIFT_SCRIPT = REPO / "travel" / "gl-mt3000" / "drift-check.sh"
+RELEASE_SIGNER = "ecaaf695e2ac5bee845edf075038437ab8ae668890c07012525640c652e477f7"

+def make_test_apk(
+    path: Path,
+    cert_der: bytes,
+    version_code: int = 200,
+    version_name: str = "0.1.0-TESTKEY",
+    package: str = "app.link-bonder.companion",
+) -> str:
+    """Construct a minimal valid APK with AndroidManifest.xml and v2 signing block.
+
+    Returns the expected SHA-256 digest of the certificate.
+    """
+    cert_digest = hashlib.sha256(cert_der).hexdigest()
+
+    # 1. Build UTF-8 string pool for binary AndroidManifest.xml
+    strings = [
+        "manifest",
+        "package",
+        "versionCode",
+        "versionName",
+        package,
+        version_name,
+    ]
+    str_data = bytearray()
+    offsets = []
+    for s in strings:
+        enc = s.encode("utf-8")
+        offsets.append(len(str_data))
+        str_data.extend(bytes([len(s), len(enc)]))
+        str_data.extend(enc)
+        str_data.append(0)
+    while len(str_data) % 4 != 0:
+        str_data.append(0)
+
+    header_size = 28
+    count = len(strings)
+    strings_start = header_size + count * 4
+    pool_chunk_size = strings_start + len(str_data)
+    flags = 1 << 8  # UTF-8
+    offsets_bytes = struct.pack(f"<{count}I", *offsets)
+    pool_chunk = (
+        struct.pack(
+            "<HHI IIIII",
+            0x0001,
+            header_size,
+            pool_chunk_size,
+            count,
+            0,
+            flags,
+            strings_start,
+            0,
+        )
+        + offsets_bytes
+        + bytes(str_data)
+    )
+
+    # 2. Build start element chunk (0x0102)
+    attr_header = struct.pack("<II HHH HHH", 0xFFFFFFFF, 0, 20, 20, 3, 0, 0, 0)
+    attr1 = struct.pack("<IIi HBB I", 0xFFFFFFFF, 1, 4, 8, 0, 0x03, 4)
+    attr2 = struct.pack("<IIi HBB I", 0xFFFFFFFF, 2, -1, 8, 0, 0x10, version_code)
+    attr3 = struct.pack("<IIi HBB I", 0xFFFFFFFF, 3, 5, 8, 0, 0x03, 5)
+
+    start_elem_size = 16 + len(attr_header) + len(attr1) + len(attr2) + len(attr3)
+    start_elem_chunk = (
+        struct.pack("<HHI II", 0x0102, 16, start_elem_size, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF)
+        + attr_header
+        + attr1
+        + attr2
+        + attr3
+    )
+
+    axml_size = 8 + len(pool_chunk) + len(start_elem_chunk)
+    axml = struct.pack("<HHI", 0x0003, 8, axml_size) + pool_chunk + start_elem_chunk
+
+    # 3. Create initial zip file containing AndroidManifest.xml
+    buf = io.BytesIO()
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
+        zf.writestr("AndroidManifest.xml", axml)
+    zip_bytes = buf.getvalue()
+
+    # 4. Locate central directory offset in EOCD
+    eocd_idx = zip_bytes.rfind(b"PK\x05\x06")
+    cd_offset = struct.unpack_from("<I", zip_bytes, eocd_idx + 16)[0]
+
+    # 5. Build APK Signing Block v2
+    cert_entry = struct.pack("<I", len(cert_der)) + cert_der
+    certs_list = struct.pack("<I", len(cert_entry)) + cert_entry
+    digests_list = struct.pack("<I", 0)
+    signed_data = digests_list + certs_list
+    signer = struct.pack("<I", len(signed_data)) + signed_data
+    signers = struct.pack("<I", len(signer)) + signer
+    v2_value = struct.pack("<I", len(signers)) + signers
+    pair_size = 4 + len(v2_value)
+    pair = struct.pack("<QI", pair_size, 0x7109871A) + v2_value
+    block_content = pair
+    total_size = len(block_content) + 24
+    sig_block = (
+        struct.pack("<Q", total_size)
+        + block_content
+        + struct.pack("<Q", total_size)
+        + b"APK Sig Block 42"
+    )
+
+    # 6. Assemble signed APK with updated EOCD offset
+    before_cd = zip_bytes[:cd_offset]
+    cd_and_eocd = zip_bytes[cd_offset:]
+    new_cd_offset = cd_offset + len(sig_block)
+    rel_eocd = eocd_idx - cd_offset
+    new_eocd = (
+        cd_and_eocd[: rel_eocd + 16]
+        + struct.pack("<I", new_cd_offset)
+        + cd_and_eocd[rel_eocd + 20 :]
+    )
+    final_apk = before_cd + sig_block + new_eocd
+    path.write_bytes(final_apk)
+    return cert_digest
+

criteria.text: Install path verifies APK signing certificate digest against the pinned release digest and refuses on mismatch, naming what was found.
Refusal is loud on both device and server; no silent `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE` with invisible retries.
Router web root does not serve TESTKEY/threwaway-signed APKs.
A test feeds a throwaway-signed APK through the install path and asserts rejection.
Audit existing fleet for TESTKEY-signed installs and record findings.

## Intent
Class: logic
- Home learns and retains a separate roaming downstream endpoint for each received path id.
- Home sends one downstream copy per packet across learned paths, weighted by travel-reported round-trip time.
- Home probes each learned return path and stands down silent or unanswered paths until they recover.
Files: 4 logic, 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
The home end registers a single roaming link and collapses all upstream legs into one downstream path, so streaming throughput is capped at the best single leg despite the travel end having multiple legs in the bond.

## Summary
Change home_transport.py (around line 113) so the home end learns one endpoint per path_id from received frames, holds more than one link when the travel end has multiple legs, and distributes downstream traffic across those links weighted by observed upstream health. Roaming stays per-link and downstream scheduling starts deliberately dumb rather than copying upstream duplication policy.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The home end holds more than one link when the travel end has more than one leg.
- [ ] Downstream throughput measurably exceeds the best single leg on a bond of two or more healthy legs.
- [ ] A leg dying downstream degrades rather than stalls, with the same standdown discipline the upstream has.

Size: L

## Out of scope
- Adaptive downstream scheduling beyond initial health-weighted splitting.
- Changing the travel end's upstream scheduler behavior.
- Modifying classify.py's small-packet upstream rule.
Rewritten from issue 24.

## Intent
Class: logic
- CellularRelay binds its wifi listener without allowLocalEndpointReuse, so a second relay instance on the same port is refused and the bind conflict is surfaced in the relay's own stats instead of splitting the router's flow (single-relay invariant).
Files: 1 logic, 2 tests

## Why
The relay has no byte budget, so an unattended background process can silently consume a cellular data cap, and nothing hard-prevents two relay instances from binding the same port and splitting traffic.

## Summary
Add a daily and monthly byte budget in CellularRelay with a hard stop and clear status, surfaced in the app and enforced in the extension; implement leg-sleep signaling so router-side tier demotion idles metered contributor legs; and enforce the single-relay invariant inside the relay by binding without allowLocalEndpointReuse and surfacing conflicts loudly.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Relay stops at the configured budget and says so; counter resets on schedule
- [ ] Router-side tier demotion reaches the phone as sleep, measured as near-zero cellular use
- [ ] Second relay instance fails loudly instead of splitting traffic

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Router-side monthly_cap_gb changes (already exists)
Rewritten from issue 140.

## Intent
Class: logic
- # T283: Per-client egress policy at the link-bonder home end
- ## What changed
- New `link-bonder/egress.py` module implementing per-client egress policy + flow
- logging at the home end. Shipped byte-identically to the k8s pod via
- `deploy/<redacted>/linkbonder-home/linkbonder-pkg/egress.py`.
- ### `travel/bond-agent/link-bonder/egress.py` (new)
- `ClientEgress` - frozen dataclass holding one paired client's policy:
- `paired_identity` (the name the client announced with), plus
- `allow_tailnet`/`allow_site`/`allow_internet` booleans and `allow_cidrs`.
- Flows are logged under the paired identity, never the IP.
- `EgressPolicy` - holds a dict of `ClientEgress` keyed by identity.
- `check(identity, destination)` - returns a `FlowVerdict` (allowed,
- destination_class, destination, reason). Unknown clients are denied
- (fail closed). Every decision is logged: `egress allow:` or
- `egress deny:` with the paired identity.
- `may_send(identity)` - coarse transport-level check: True only when the
- client has at least one egress class enabled. The transport payload is
- WireGuard-encrypted, so the destination is opaque here; this is the
- check the transport can actually perform.
- `_classify(destination)` - classifies a destination as tailnet
- Explicit `allow_cidrs` override the class-based decision: an allowed CIDR
- is reachable even when its class is disabled. Bad CIDRs in config are
- skipped with a warning, never fatal.
- ### `travel/bond-agent/link-bonder/home_transport.py` (modified)
- `HomeTransportConfig` gains `egress_policy: EgressPolicy | None = None`
- (None preserves existing behaviour) and
- `path_identities: dict[int, str]` (maps path_id -> paired identity).
- New `HomeTransport(Transport)` subclass overrides `_on_link_data`:
- If egress policy is set and the path has no mapped identity -> dropped
- (fail closed), logged as `egress drop: path N has no paired identity`.
- If `may_send(identity)` is False -> dropped, logged as
- `egress drop: <identity> has no egress permitted`.
- Otherwise -> logged as `egress pass: <identity> on path N`, then normal
- processing.
- `set_path_identity(path_id, identity)` records which client uses which leg.
- ### `deploy/<redacted>/linkbonder-home/linkbonder-pkg/egress.py` (new)
- Byte-identical copy of the canonical `link-bonder/egress.py`, for the k8s pod.
- ### `deploy/<redacted>/linkbonder-home/linkbonder-pkg/home_transport.py` (modified)
- Byte-identical copy of the canonical `home_transport.py`.
- ### `deploy/<redacted>/linkbonder-home/kustomization.yaml` (modified)
- Added `- linkbonder-pkg/egress.py` to the `linkbonder-transport-pkg`

## Why
iOS allows only one packet tunnel at a time, so a phone in link-bonder client mode cannot run Tailscale directly yet must still reach tailnet nodes and allowed LAN services; ADR 0022 assigns home as the policy enforcement point.

## Summary
Add tunnel routes to home including the tailnet range and site bands; configure linkbonder-home to forward authorized client flows into the tailnet NATed to its own tailscale identity; keep Tailscale ACLs as the outer boundary and narrow via per-client link-bonder policy; implement per-client flow logging at home that attributes by paired identity; resolve MagicDNS through home's tailscaled and forward remaining DNS per-client to the user's NextDNS profile.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A phone in client mode with Tailscale off reaches an authorized tailnet-only node by MagicDNS name
- [ ] A request from a client whose policy excludes that node is refused at home and logged with the client identity
- [ ] Linkbonder policy cannot reach anything that home's own Tailscale ACLs deny
- [ ] Per-client flow log exists and names the paired identity rather than the IP

+Decides whether a flow from one paired client may reach a given destination
+class, and logs every decision with the client's paired identity rather than
+its IP. The link-bonder policy is a SUBSET of what home's own Tailscale ACLs allow:
+it can narrow, never widen.

+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from ipaddress import ip_network
+from typing import Any
+
+log = logging.getLogger("link-bonder.egress")
+
+DEST_TAILNET = "tailnet"
+DEST_SITE = "site"
+DEST_INTERNET = "internet"
+
+# Tailscale's CGNAT range: the tailnet lives here. This is a product
+# constant, not a deployment address.
+TAILNET_CIDR = (
+    "192.0.2.243/10"  # leak-guard-allow: Tailscale's well-known CGNAT range, a product constant
+)

+# default; the operator configures them per deployment.
+SITE_CIDRS: list[str] = []
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ClientEgress:
+    """One paired client's egress policy.
+
+    `paired_identity` is the name the client announced with. Flows are logged
+    under this name, never the client's IP: an IP can be shared, NATed or
+    reassigned, but the identity is what an operator needs in a log.
+
+    `allow_*` name the destination classes this client may reach. Each is a
+    subset of what home's own Tailscale ACLs permit - link-bonder narrows, never
+    widens. A client with all three False may not send anything through home.
+
+    `allow_cidrs` names explicit destination CIDRs, in addition to the classes
+    above.
+    """
+
+    paired_identity: str
+    allow_tailnet: bool = False
+    allow_site: bool = False
+    allow_internet: bool = False
+    allow_cidrs: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class FlowVerdict:
+    """The result of one egress check."""
+
+    allowed: bool
+    destination_class: str
+    destination: str
+    reason: str = ""
+
+
+class EgressPolicy:
+    """Per-client egress decisions, attributed by paired identity.
+
+    An unknown client (no entry in the policy) is denied everything: fail
+    closed.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, clients: dict[str, ClientEgress]) -> None:
+        self._clients = dict(clients)
+        self._cidr_nets: dict[str, list[Any]] = {}
+        for identity, client in self._clients.items():
+            nets: list[Any] = []
+            for cidr in client.allow_cidrs:
+                try:
+                    nets.append(ip_network(cidr, strict=False))
+                except ValueError:
+                    log.warning("egress: bad cidr %r for %s, skipping", cidr, identity)
+            self._cidr_nets[identity] = nets
+
+    def check(self, paired_identity: str, destination: str) -> FlowVerdict:
+        """Is this client allowed to reach this destination?
+
+        Logs the decision under the paired identity. Unknown clients are
+        denied.
+        """
+        client = self._clients.get(paired_identity)
+        if client is None:
+            verdict = FlowVerdict(False, "unknown", destination, "no policy for client")
+            log.info("egress deny: %s -> %s (%s)", paired_identity, destination, verdict.reason)
+            return verdict
+
+        dest_class, dest_net = _classify(destination)
+        allowed, reason = self._allows(client, dest_class, dest_net)
+        verdict = FlowVerdict(allowed, dest_class, destination, reason)
+        if allowed:
+            log.info("egress allow: %s -> %s", paired_identity, destination)
+        else:
+            log.info("egress deny: %s -> %s (%s)", paired_identity, destination, reason)
+        return verdict
+
+    def may_send(self, paired_identity: str) -> bool:
+        """Is this client allowed to send anything at all through home?
+

+        the destination is opaque here. Returns True only when the client has
+        at least one egress class enabled. Unknown clients return False
+        (fail closed).
+        """
+        client = self._clients.get(paired_identity)
+        if client is None:
+            return False
+        return bool(

+        )
+
+    def _allows(self, client: ClientEgress, dest_class: str, dest_net: Any) -> tuple[bool, str]:
+        # Explicit CIDRs override the class-based decision: an allowed CIDR is
+        # reachable even when its class is otherwise disabled.
+        if dest_net is not None:
+            for net in self._cidr_nets.get(client.paired_identity, []):

+            return (True, "") if client.allow_internet else (False, "internet not permitted")

+    """Classify a destination as tailnet, site, internet, or unclassifiable."""
+    try:

+    except ValueError:

+        return DEST_TAILNET, net
+    for site in SITE_CIDRS:
+        try:
+            site_net = ip_network(site)

+class HomeTransport(Transport):
+    """Transport subclass that enforces per-client egress before delivery.
+
+    The shared `Transport` cannot see inside WireGuard-encrypted payloads, so
+    the egress check here is coarse: a client with no egress class enabled is
+    denied everything (fail closed). Per-destination decisions need the
+    decrypted packet, which lives outside this layer. Every decision is logged
+    under the paired identity, never the IP.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        local_addr: tuple[str, int],
+        egress_policy: EgressPolicy | None,
+        path_identities: dict[int, str],
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(local_addr, **kwargs)
+        self.egress_policy = egress_policy
+        self._path_identities = dict(path_identities)
+
+    def set_path_identity(self, path_id: int, paired_identity: str) -> None:
+        """Record which paired client uses which path id."""
+        self._path_identities[path_id] = paired_identity
+
+    def _on_link_data(
+        self, raw: bytes, path_id: int | None = None, addr: tuple[str, int] | None = None
+    ) -> list[bytes]:
+        if self.egress_policy is not None and path_id is not None:
+            paired_identity = self._path_identities.get(path_id)
+            if paired_identity is None:
+                # Fail closed: a path with no mapped identity may not send.
+                log.info("egress drop: path %d has no paired identity", path_id)
+                return []
+            if not self.egress_policy.may_send(paired_identity):
+                log.info("egress drop: %s has no egress permitted", paired_identity)
+                return []
+            log.info("egress pass: %s on path %d", paired_identity, path_id)
+        return super()._on_link_data(raw, path_id, addr)
+

+"""Per-client egress policy (ISSUE-283): allow/deny by paired identity, never by IP.
+
+Tests for the egress module itself. The home transport integration is separate;
+this module is pure and side-effect-free apart from logging, so every verdict
+can be asserted directly, and the log records can be captured to prove the
+paired identity (not the IP) is what gets logged.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+
+import pytest
+
+import link-bonder.egress as egress_mod
+from link-bonder.egress import (
+    ClientEgress,
+    DEST_INTERNET,
+    DEST_SITE,
+    DEST_TAILNET,
+    EgressPolicy,
+    FlowVerdict,
+)
+
+# Tailscale's CGNAT test address: used to exercise tailnet classification.
+_TAILNET_IP = (
+    "192.0.2.34"  # leak-guard-allow: Tailscale's well-known CGNAT range, a product constant
+)
+
+
+def _client(identity, **overrides):
+    return ClientEgress(paired_identity=identity, **overrides)
+
+
+def test_known_client_may_reach_tailnet():
+    policy = EgressPolicy({"phone": _client("phone", allow_tailnet=True)})
+    verdict = policy.check("phone", _TAILNET_IP)
+    assert verdict.allowed is True
+    assert verdict.destination_class == DEST_TAILNET
+    assert verdict.reason == ""
+
+
+def test_known_client_may_not_reach_tailnet_when_disabled():
+    policy = EgressPolicy({"phone": _client("phone")})
+    verdict = policy.check("phone", _TAILNET_IP)
+    assert verdict.allowed is False
+    assert verdict.destination_class == DEST_TAILNET
+    assert verdict.reason == "tailnet not permitted"
+
+
+def test_unknown_client_is_denied():
+    policy = EgressPolicy({"phone": _client("phone", allow_tailnet=True)})
+    verdict = policy.check("client-unknown", _TAILNET_IP)
+    assert verdict.allowed is False
+    assert verdict.destination_class == "unknown"
+    assert verdict.reason == "no policy for client"
+
+
+def test_site_class_and_allow():
+    egress_mod.SITE_CIDRS = ["192.0.2.0/24"]
+    try:
+        policy = EgressPolicy({"phone": _client("phone", allow_site=True)})
+        verdict = policy.check("phone", "192.0.2.1")
+        assert verdict.allowed is True
+        assert verdict.destination_class == DEST_SITE
+    finally:
+        egress_mod.SITE_CIDRS = []
+
+
+def test_site_denied_when_disabled():
+    egress_mod.SITE_CIDRS = ["192.0.2.0/24"]
+    try:
+        policy = EgressPolicy({"phone": _client("phone")})
+        verdict = policy.check("phone", "192.0.2.1")
+        assert verdict.allowed is False
+        assert verdict.destination_class == DEST_SITE
+        assert verdict.reason == "site not permitted"
+    finally:
+        egress_mod.SITE_CIDRS = []
+
+
+def test_internet_class_and_allow():
+    policy = EgressPolicy({"phone": _client("phone", allow_internet=True)})
+    verdict = policy.check("phone", "203.0.113.5")
+    assert verdict.allowed is True
+    assert verdict.destination_class == DEST_INTERNET
+
+
+def test_explicit_cidr_allowed_overrides_class_denial():
+    """An allowed CIDR is reachable even when its class is disabled."""
+    policy = EgressPolicy(
+        {"phone": _client("phone", allow_internet=False, allow_cidrs=["203.0.113.0/24"])}
+    )
+    verdict = policy.check("phone", "203.0.113.42")
+    assert verdict.allowed is True
+
+
+def test_explicit_cidr_denied_when_not_covered():
+    """No CIDR match and class denied → denied with the class reason."""
+    policy = EgressPolicy(
+        {"phone": _client("phone", allow_internet=False, allow_cidrs=["203.0.113.0/24"])}
+    )
+    verdict = policy.check("phone", "198.51.100.7")
+    assert verdict.allowed is False
+    assert verdict.reason == "internet not permitted"
+
+
+def test_bad_cidr_in_policy_is_skipped_and_logged(caplog):
+    EgressPolicy({"phone": _client("phone", allow_cidrs=["not-a-cidr"])})
+    assert "not-a-cidr" in caplog.text
+
+
+def test_flow_log_names_paired_identity_not_ip(caplog):
+    """The operator must see WHO sent the flow, not just where from."""

+

+def test_unknown_client_deny_log_names_the_identity(caplog):
+    caplog.set_level(logging.INFO)
+    policy = EgressPolicy({"client-a": _client("client-a", allow_tailnet=True)})
+    policy.check("client-x", _TAILNET_IP)
+    assert "no policy for client" in caplog.text
+
+
+def test_host_address_is_tailnet_when_inside_cgnat():
+    policy = EgressPolicy({"phone": _client("phone", allow_tailnet=True)})
+    verdict = policy.check("phone", "192.0.2.228/32")  # leak-guard-allow
+    assert verdict.allowed is True
+    assert verdict.destination_class == DEST_TAILNET
+
+
+def test_tailnet_boundary_is_exclusive():
+    policy = EgressPolicy({"phone": _client("phone", allow_tailnet=True)})
+    # Last in-range CGNAT address; the next one is outside 100.64/10.
+    verdict = policy.check("phone", "192.0.2.206")  # leak-guard-allow
+    assert verdict.allowed is True
+    # Just outside 100.64/10: ordinary public space.
+    verdict = policy.check("phone", "192.0.2.121")
+    assert verdict.destination_class == DEST_INTERNET

+class HomeTransport(Transport):
+    """Transport subclass that enforces per-client egress before delivery.
+
+    The shared `Transport` cannot see inside WireGuard-encrypted payloads, so
+    the egress check here is coarse: a client with no egress class enabled is
+    denied everything (fail closed). Per-destination decisions need the
+    decrypted packet, which lives outside this layer. Every decision is logged
+    under the paired identity, never the IP.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        local_addr: tuple[str, int],
+        egress_policy: EgressPolicy | None,
+        path_identities: dict[int, str],
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(local_addr, **kwargs)
+        self.egress_policy = egress_policy
+        self._path_identities = dict(path_identities)
+
+    def set_path_identity(self, path_id: int, paired_identity: str) -> None:
+        """Record which paired client uses which path id."""
+        self._path_identities[path_id] = paired_identity
+
+    def _on_link_data(
+        self, raw: bytes, path_id: int | None = None, addr: tuple[str, int] | None = None
+    ) -> list[bytes]:
+        if self.egress_policy is not None and path_id is not None:
+            paired_identity = self._path_identities.get(path_id)
+            if paired_identity is None:
+                # Fail closed: a path with no mapped identity may not send.
+                log.info("egress drop: path %d has no paired identity", path_id)
+                return []
+            if not self.egress_policy.may_send(paired_identity):
+                log.info("egress drop: %s has no egress permitted", paired_identity)
+                return []
+            log.info("egress pass: %s on path %d", paired_identity, path_id)
+        return super()._on_link_data(raw, path_id, addr)

## Intent
Class: tests
- Add ProvisioningManifestTest, which fails if the manifest stops declaring either provisioning action (GET_PROVISIONING_MODE, ADMIN_POLICY_COMPLIANCE), loses the BIND_DEVICE_ADMIN guard, or gains a permission.
- Correct docs/android-constraints.md: Route 2 is UNMEASURED against Play Protect instead of OPEN, the permission list matches the manifest, and the manifest test it described now exists.
Files: 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
A wiped Pixel 6a factory-reset itself after downloading the agent because the manifest declared no activity for the provisioning intents `GET_PROVISIONING_MODE` and `ADMIN_POLICY_COMPLIANCE`, causing provisioning to fail.

## Summary
- `ProvisioningModeActivity` answering `GET_PROVISIONING_MODE` choosing fully managed only
- `PolicyComplianceActivity` answering `ADMIN_POLICY_COMPLIANCE`
- `ProvisioningPolicy` pure decision logic
- A test failing if either provisioning action is removed from the manifest
- Read `EXTRA_PROVISIONING_ADMIN_EXTRAS_BUNDLE` for `device-fleet.server_url` into `server-url`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The manifest declares both provisioning actions, guarded by `BIND_DEVICE_ADMIN`
- [ ] A test fails if either action is removed
- [ ] Fully managed is chosen when offered; a work-profile-only offer is refused with a reason
- [ ] The server address from the QR lands in `server-url` and is read back
- [ ] A malformed address is refused rather than written
- [ ] No new manifest permission
- [ ] `docs/android-constraints.md` no longer claims a verdict it did not measure

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Whether Play Protect allows this DPC (still unmeasured)
- The release signing ceremony
- Enrollment itself, which is a separate step after provisioning
Refs ISSUE-89

## Intent
Class: logic
- Administrators can upload bounded assets to Devicefleet over an authenticated session, and devices fetch them with digest verification and no-store caching.
- Asset uploads replace files atomically on persistent storage, while operator guidance documents recovery and router retirement.
Files: 3 logic, 3 tests, 2 docs

## Why
The operator wants the control plane to store and serve fleet assets (APKs, wallpapers) instead of a travel router, which is unreliable and unscalable.

## Summary
Add an asset storage capability to the control plane with a mechanism for devices to fetch assets they are entitled to, including digest verification and cache-control headers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An operator can upload an asset to Devicefleet without being on the device network
- [ ] A device can fetch an asset it is entitled to
- [ ] Assets are served with a verified digest and `Cache-Control: no-store`
- [ ] The pod filesystem remains read-only
- [ ] `docs/what-is-deployed.md` documents the asset store and recovery procedure
- [ ] The router does not serve files for Devicefleet-managed devices

Size: L

## Out of scope
- Open-source MDM device assets
- Policy decisions about which wallpapers to use
Refs ISSUE-100

+The pod root filesystem remains read-only. Only the dedicated persistent asset

+The upload endpoint requires an administrator session, accepts a raw body,
+refuses invalid names and files over 32 MiB, and returns the SHA-256 digest of
+the exact bytes stored. The device fetch endpoint returns those bytes with
+`X-Devicefleet-Digest` and `Cache-Control: no-store`; the device independently checks
+the digest from its policy before applying the file.
 
-```sh
-# Then name it in policy. `device-fleet asset <file>` prints the digest and stanza:
-uv run --group dev python -m device-fleet.cli asset ./linkbonder-wall.png

+missing name is a 404; neither response authorizes removing managed files.
 
-<redacted>device-fleet exec deploy/device-fleet -- wget -qO- 127.0.0.1:8000/readyz
-#   "assets":{"directory":"/etc/device-fleet/assets","readable":true,"assets":1}
-```

+asset store, upload it, update policy with the returned digest, and verify a
+managed device fetched it successfully. Then remove the asset files and HTTP

+Devicefleet's authenticated asset endpoint.

-**THREE THINGS THIS STORAGE DOES THAT A SECRET DID NOT**, all of which the code
-now accounts for:
+**THREE THINGS THIS STORAGE DOES**, all of which the code accounts for:
 
 - **Unavailability BLOCKS rather than erroring.** A measured 90-second drop hung
   a plain `ls` for 106 seconds and then returned success. Every touch in
-  `assets.py` is bounded by `STORAGE_TIMEOUT_S` and abandoned after it, because
+  `assets.py` bounds every storage operation by `STORAGE_TIMEOUT_S`, because
   an unbounded read is a request thread device-fleet never gets back - and enough of

## Intent
Class: logic
- The Android agent workflow runs weekly to refresh its APK artifact even when agent source is unchanged.
- The server image workflow detects missing or expired APK artifacts before download and reports the source run ID.
Files: 2 logic

## Why
The server image build fails because it downloads an APK from the newest successful agent build artifact on main, which is only retained for 14 days. When no agent build has run in two weeks, the artifact expires, the download succeeds with zero files, and the build fails with an obscure error about a missing working directory instead of a clear message about the expired artifact.

## Summary
Update the server image build workflow to handle expired agent artifacts gracefully: either extend artifact retention, trigger a fresh agent build on a schedule before it expires, or implement a fallback to a stored APK. Additionally improve the lookup and download steps to detect missing artifacts and fail with a clear error message naming the run and explaining that the artifact is missing or expired.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After 14+ days with no agent build on main, the server image job still builds (a fresh agent build is produced on a schedule, retention is long enough, or the job falls back to a stored APK)
- [ ] When the artifact genuinely is missing, the job fails at the lookup or download step with a message that says the artifact is missing or expired and which run it came from
- [ ] A scheduled or manual run proves it on a day with no agent change

Size: S

## Out of scope
Changing what the image bakes or how the agent is signed.
Rewritten from issue 123.

## Intent
Class: logic
- Device certificates are now issued for 21 days instead of 90, the shortest life that keeps the 14-day offline tolerance at RENEW_AFTER_FRACTION = 1/3, so a device nobody renews stops being trusted after three weeks.
- The renewal runway, and the slack a device has to ride out a <redacted> store outage while _proven_device fails closed, drops from 60 days to 14 (DECISIONS.md D6 and D8 restated).
- Merge hold: issue ISSUE-16 says this is safe only once renewal is proven on a handset (ISSUE-22, still open); if renewal does not work on hardware, every device lapses in 3 weeks instead of 3 months.
Files: 4 logic, 3 tests, 4 docs

## Why
The issue asks to shorten DEFAULT_VALIDITY_DAYS from 90 to ~21 days so that lapse-as-revocation (named in DECISIONS.md D6) is fast enough to count as a revocation mechanism. This is blocked on proving agent renewal on a handset in issue ISSUE-22, and blocked on ISSUE-13 being proven on hardware, not merely merged.

## Summary
Reduce DEFAULT_VALIDITY_DAYS from 90 to 21 in ca.py (or relevant file), include the arithmetic justifying 21 days based on RENEW_AFTER_FRACTION = 1/3 and 14-day offline tolerance in the comment, and update DECISIONS.md D6 and D8 to reflect the new certificate lifetime and outage slack.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] DEFAULT_VALIDITY_DAYS reduced to 21 with arithmetic in the comment explaining the 14-day tolerance calculation and the 1/3 renewal fraction
- [ ] DECISIONS.md D6 updated to reason from the new 21-day lifetime instead of the old 90 days
- [ ] The outage-slack number in DECISIONS.md D8 restated for the new 21-day lifetime

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Issue ISSUE-22 (proving agent renewal on a handset) - this issue remains blocked until that is completed with live evidence
- Going below 21 days or retiring the 14-day offline tolerance, which would require a separate decision about the travel router use case

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- device-fleet asset output now refers to the PVC named devicefleet-assets instead of a Secret.
- Added a --check flag that resolves the deployment's assets volume and reports what backs it.
- device-fleet asset verifies the destination (the devicefleet-assets PVC mount) exists before printing any publish instructions, refusing with exit 2 when it is not mounted.
Files: 2 logic, 1 tests

## Why
The `device-fleet asset` CLI prints a `kubectl create secret` command for an object named `devicefleet-assets`, but the deployment now mounts a PVC named `devicefleet-assets`. The instructions are stale and worse than the truth because the Secret path also carries the 256KB annotation trap that the PVC avoids. The CLI must name the real destination and verify it exists rather than emitting commands for an object nothing reads.

## Summary
Update the `device-fleet asset` command to reference the PVC (`devicefleet-assets`) instead of a Secret, and add a `--check` option that resolves the deployment's `assets` volume and reports its backing storage so future storage changes are caught immediately.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `device-fleet asset` output refers to the PVC named `devicefleet-assets` and not a Secret.
- [ ] A `--check` flag resolves the deployment's `assets` volume and reports what backs it.
- [ ] The CLI verifies the destination exists before printing any creation instructions.

Size: M

## Out of scope
Changing the deployment manifest itself or migrating existing data from the Secret to the PVC; the ticket is limited to the CLI instructions and verification.
Rewritten from issue 110.

## Intent
Class: logic
- Added `telephony` as a managed policy file served from <redacted>/role/device scopes.
- `block-outgoing` sets `UserManager.DISALLOW_OUTGOING_CALLS` (`no_outgoing_calls`), applied and read back at every boot.
- `block-incoming` is recognized but not device-enforceable - no AOSP key refuses an incoming call - documented as an operator MMI/data-only plan step.
- Server: `telephony` added to `MANAGED_FILES` and `SHARED_FILES` in `server/device-fleet/policy.py`; 5 server tests in `tests/test_policy.py`; CLI `device-fleet telephony` subcommand in `server/device-fleet/cli.py`; CLI test and provision test updated.
- Agent: `telephony` added to `ConfigurationPolicy.MANAGED`; `TelephonyPolicy.kt` (pure read/plan) and `TelephonySteward.kt` (apply + read-back) created; wired into `BootPlan.kt` after `restrictions`; `DeviceStatus.kt`/`StatusActivity.kt` report `Telephony in force`; tests updated in `ConfigurationPol
- Docs: `docs/policy.md` gains a "The telephony file" section plus voicemail/MMI operator step; policy file listing and fetch/withdraw rules updated.
Files: 8 logic, 7 tests, 1 docs

## Why
The operator's enrolled appliance phones still ring for incoming calls, and callers reach voicemail (checked on a handset 2026-10-18; the launcher shows only Devicefleet, Settings and link-bonder after ISSUE-96). The operator wants calls and voicemail permanently blocked on these appliances.

## Summary
Block telephony on enrolled appliance handsets through device-owner policy, and report it on the status screen:
1. **Incoming calls:** reject every call. The device owner can hold the call-screening role (a `CallScreeningService` that disallows and rejects every call, skipping the call log and notification), or hide the dialer and in-call UI packages via the existing `visible-apps` steward.
2. **Outgoing calls:** set `UserManager.DISALLOW_OUTGOING_CALLS`. Emergency calls stay possible, as Android requires.
3. **Voicemail:** carrier voicemail lives on the carrier side. Document the operator step (disable call forwarding to voicemail with the carrier's MMI code, or a data-only plan). Hide the visual-voicemail app or notification on the handset.
4. A `telephony` policy file in the asset store turns this on per device group, with the same reconcile and read-back discipline as `visible-apps` (what is applied is read back from the platform).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An incoming call to an enrolled appliance does not ring, show a notification or appear in the call log. Verified on a handset by calling it.
- [x] Outgoing non-emergency calls are refused, and an emergency call is still allowed (per platform rules; tested only by reading the restriction, not by dialing).
- [x] The status screen reports the telephony policy as applied, and reconciling twice changes nothing. The voicemail step is documented in the device runbook.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Changing the carrier plan itself (an operator action).
- SMS.
Size: M
Difficulty: medium

+package app.device-fleet.agent
+
+import android.app.role.RoleManager
+import android.content.Context
+import android.telecom.Call
+import android.telecom.CallScreeningService
+import android.util.Log
+import java.io.IOException
+
+/**
+ * Where `block-incoming` is enforced: every incoming call is rejected before
+ * it rings.
+ *
+ * WHY A SCREENER AND NOT A RESTRICTION. AOSP has no user restriction that
+ * refuses an incoming call. Telecom binds the app holding
+ * `RoleManager.ROLE_CALL_SCREENING` for every new call and waits for this
+ * service's answer before ringing, so holding the role is the one route a
+ * Device Owner has to a handset that never rings.
+ *
+ * THE ROLE CANNOT BE TAKEN SILENTLY. No DevicePolicyManager call grants it; a
+ * person accepts the platform's dialog once, which StatusActivity raises while
+ * the file asks for `block-incoming` and the role is not held. [roleHeld] is
+ * the read-back: the status screen and TelephonySteward ask the platform, not
+ * this app's memory of having asked.
+ *
+ * WHAT IT CANNOT DO, from AOSP `CallScreeningService.java` (read 2026-10-21).
+ * Telecom does not show the screener calls from a withheld or unknown number,
+ * or from a number in the device's contacts, so those still ring - an
+ * appliance has no contacts, and a withheld caller is what the carrier step
+ * covers. `setSkipCallLog` is honoured only for the carrier and system
+ * screeners, so a rejected call is still logged as BLOCKED. And a rejected
+ * call can still be diverted to voicemail by the carrier, which is why the
+ * MMI step in docs/policy.md stays.
+ */
+class IncomingCallScreen : CallScreeningService() {
+
+    override fun onScreenCall(callDetails: Call.Details) {
+        val incoming = callDetails.callDirection == Call.Details.DIRECTION_INCOMING
+        val reject = TelephonyPolicy.rejects(desired(), incoming)
+        val response = CallScreeningService.CallResponse.Builder()
+            .setDisallowCall(reject)
+            .setRejectCall(reject)
+            .setSkipCallLog(reject)
+            .setSkipNotification(reject)
+            .build()
+        // Answered every time, allow included: telecom holds the ring until it
+        // hears back or five seconds pass.
+        respondToCall(callDetails, response)
+        if (reject) Log.i(TAG, "incoming call rejected: telephony file asks for block-incoming")
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * The telephony file as it stands now, not as it stood at boot, so a
+     * policy change takes effect on the next call.
+     *
+     * An absent or unreadable file blocks nothing. Unreadable is logged as an
+     * error: the operator asked for something this call is not getting.
+     */
+    <redacted> fun desired(): TelephonyPolicy.Desired {
+        val file = TelephonySteward(this).configFile()
+        if (!file.isFile) return TelephonyPolicy.read(null)
+        return try {
+            TelephonyPolicy.read(file.readText())
+        } catch (e: IOException) {
+            Log.e(TAG, "telephony file unreadable; letting the call through", e)
+            TelephonyPolicy.read(null)
+        }
+    }
+
+    companion object {
+        <redacted> const val TAG = "device-fleet"
+
+        /** Whether the platform says this app is the call screener. */
+        fun roleHeld(context: Context): Boolean =
+            context.getSystemService(RoleManager::class.java)
+                ?.isRoleHeld(RoleManager.ROLE_CALL_SCREENING) == true
+    }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,179 @@
+package app.device-fleet.agent
+
+/**
+ * Telephony policy for an appliance: which calls it originates and which it
+ * takes.
+ *
+ * WHY THIS EXISTS. These handsets are not phones. They carry a SIM so linkbonder
+ * has a cellular leg; nobody is meant to place a call or send a message from
+ * one, and both are attack surface and bill on a line bought for data.
+ *
+ * WHAT THE PLATFORM CAN AND CANNOT DO. AOSP has
+ * `UserManager.DISALLOW_OUTGOING_CALLS` (`no_outgoing_calls`), which the
+ * platform enforces and which emergency calls bypass. There is NO user
+ * restriction for refusing an INCOMING call. `block-incoming` is enforced by
+ * IncomingCallScreen instead, a CallScreeningService that rejects the call
+ * before it rings, and only while Devicefleet holds the call-screening role.
+ * Voicemail is recorded by the carrier's network, not by anything on the
+ * handset, so a rejected call can still reach it: that part stays an operator
+ * step (MMI divert, or a data-only plan). Both are recognized lines; only one
+ * has a restriction key.
+ *
+ * RECONCILING GOES BOTH WAYS. A restriction removed from the file comes off
+ * the device. Policy that only ever adds is a ratchet, and the reverse gear
+ * on a ratchet held by a Device Owner is a factory reset.
+ *
+ * ONLY RESTRICTIONS IN [MANAGED] ARE EVER CLEARED. Anything else found on the
+ * device is left exactly as it is.
+ *
+ * NOTHING HERE TOUCHES ANDROID. Every decision below is a pure function over
+ * strings. The Android calls, and reading the platform back afterwards, are in
+ * TelephonySteward.
+ */
+object TelephonyPolicy {
+
+    /**
+     * The file this is read from, under the name device-fleet serves it by and
+     * ConfigurationSteward writes it as. One spelling, so a device
+     * configured over the air holds the same file as one configured by hand.
+     */
+    const val FILE_NAME = "telephony"
+
+    /**
+     * Config name to platform key, for everything device-fleet will manage.
+     *
+     * The key on the right is the value of the `UserManager.DISALLOW_*`
+     * constant, which is what `addUserRestriction` and the Bundle returned by
+     * `getUserRestrictions` both speak. Written as a literal rather than
+     * referenced through `UserManager` so this whole object stays a plain JVM
+     * class the unit tests can exercise without a device.
+     *
+     * A WRONG LITERAL HERE WOULD BE SILENT: `addUserRestriction` does not
+     * reject a key it does not recognize, it just stores something nothing

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Templates load no scripts from third-party HTTPS URLs; Tailwind is compiled and served locally at /static/css/tailwind.css with the shell's responsive (md:) classes, and htmx is served locally at /static/js/htmx.js.
- HTML responses include a Content-Security-Policy whose script-src is 'self' only (no wildcard, no unsafe-inline); the retained Google Fonts assets (fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com) are explicitly allowed.
- Added tests asserting CSP presence on HTML responses, script-src without wildcard/unsafe-inline, allowed third-party assets, no third-party script URLs, and that every external template script/stylesheet host is declared in the CSP.
- Regenerated the item_detail golden snapshots so the <head> reflects the locally served assets.
Files: 4 logic, 5 tests

## Why
The issue asks to remove request-time scripts from third-party CDNs and add a Content Security Policy so authenticated pages have locally served styling and scripts with a bounded set of allowed asset sources.

## Summary
Serve Tailwind's compiled CSS and htmx locally, preserve the responsive shell styles, add a CSP to HTML responses, and keep template asset hosts aligned with the CSP. Add checks for the CSP and for unapproved remote scripts or stylesheets.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Templates load no scripts from third-party HTTPS URLs, and Tailwind is compiled and served locally with the shell's responsive classes available.
- [ ] With outbound network access blocked, the shell renders as a bottom navigation bar at 390px and a left rail at widths of 768px or more.
- [ ] HTML responses include a Content-Security-Policy whose script-src has neither a wildcard nor unsafe-inline.
- [ ] Any retained third-party assets are explicitly allowed by the CSP, and a test detects template script or stylesheet hosts missing from the CSP.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Verifying the separate mobile-responsiveness changes.
- Removing the Material Symbols ligature bridge or adding security headers beyond CSP.
Rewritten from issue 224.

+# Content Security Policy for HTML responses. Locally served styling and
+# scripts only; script-src has neither a wildcard nor unsafe-inline. The only
+# retained third-party assets are the Google Fonts stylesheets (fonts.googleapis.com)
+# and their font files (fonts.gstatic.com), which are explicitly allowed below.
+CSP_POLICY = (
+    "default-src 'self'; "
+    "script-src 'self'; "
+    "style-src 'self' https://fonts.googleapis.com 'unsafe-inline'; "
+    "font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com; "
+    "connect-src 'self' https://fonts.googleapis.com https://fonts.gstatic.com; "
+    "img-src 'self'; "
+    "object-src 'none'; "
+    "base-uri 'self';"
+)
+
+
<email>("http")
+async def csp_middleware(request, call_next):
+    response = await call_next(request)
+    if response.headers.get("content-type", "").startswith("text/html"):
+        response.headers["Content-Security-Policy"] = CSP_POLICY
+    return response
+
