body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Home-screen widget now renders the router's bond, not just this phone: iOS and Android both carry a persisted bond snapshot with its own staleness threshold, so the medium tile can list the router's legs.
- Medium widget leg list draws a leg held in reserve as "held in reserve" rather than as a failure, and draws a leg with weight the transport does not hold as not carrying (tokens.json weightIsNotMembership, reserveIsNotBroken).
- Android gains a Glance home-screen widget (small and medium) that renders RelayVerdict from disk; there was previously no Android widget at all, only the WidgetContent model.
- Android widget reads the relay report and the bond snapshot from disk rather than from the in-memory RelayStatusStore, so a widget redrawn in a fresh process no longer renders "Off" while the relay is carrying.

## Why
The issue requests home-screen widgets on both iOS and Android that answer "is it working, and on what" by rendering the existing `RelayVerdict` output directly, without re-deriving any part of it. This extends the app's core thesis to the home screen so users can see the verdict at a glance from their dashboard or launcher.

## Summary
Build Small and Medium widgets for iOS (WidgetKit) and Android (Glance) that render `RelayVerdict`. For iOS, the WidgetKit extension joins the app-group `UserDefaults` and reads from `RelayStatusStore`, which already persists reports with `RelayVerdict.evaluate` producing the verdict sentence. For Android, first persist `RelayReport` to disk (following the precedent of `BootConfigStore` and `BootLogFile`) since the current `RelayStatusStore` is an in-memory singleton that returns `null` in a fresh process, then build the Glance widget on top of persisted data with proper staleness handling. Use semantic color tokens only (never the marketing palette), honor the staleness threshold so stale widgets do not assert freshness, and treat unmeasured values as absent. The verdict must be read, never recomputed. One accent dot indicates live, degraded, or down state.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Small and Medium widgets on both iOS and Android, rendering `RelayVerdict` rather than re-deriving any part of it
- [ ] Test that the widget shows the STALE state when the stored report is older than the staleness threshold, and fails if the widget renders the last good verdict instead
- [ ] Medium widget leg list distinguishes carrying from present-but-not-carrying (`weightIsNotMembership`) and draws a reserve leg as reserve, not failure (`reserveIsNotBroken`)
- [ ] Colors come from the generated tokens so a token change moves the widget with everything else
- [ ] Renders correctly in light and dark modes, and in the launcher's themed mode on Android

- Real-device visual verification (the "what it looks like on a real home screen" acceptance criterion requires physical hardware)
- Interactivity (buttons to start or stop tunnels from the home screen)
- The Large widget size (deferred until Small and Medium have been lived with)
- Lock-screen and StandBy widgets
- Any change to how the verdict itself is computed

## Intent
Class: logic
- linkbonder-clienthome.yaml now opens with a PARKED note: not to be applied until a phone client (legacy no. 27) can reach it; no runtime change
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
The linkbonder-clienthome manifest in deploy/<redacted>/ reads as live infrastructure but has never been deployed because there is no phone client to terminate. It should be explicitly marked as parked until legacy no. 27 lands.

## Summary
Add a comment at the top of the manifest stating it is parked behind legacy no. 40, that no image build exists yet, and that it must not be applied until a phone client can reach it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The manifest states plainly that it is parked, why, and what unblocks it (legacy no. 27).
- [ ] Nothing in deploy/<redacted>/ reads as deployable without either being deployed or carrying such a note.
- [ ] The Go code and manifest are retained without deletion.

Size: XS

## Out of scope
- The multi-client home protocol design itself (legacy no. 24).
- The actual image build, publish, or deployment of the workload.
Refs ISSUE-128

@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
+"""linkbonder-clienthome.yaml must say, at the top, that it is parked (ISSUE-208).
+
+It reads as live infrastructure but has never been deployed: there is no phone
+client to terminate. Any target that is not auto-applied has to carry a plain
+note saying so, or the next reader takes it for something that is running.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from pathlib import Path
+
+<redacted> = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+MANIFEST = <redacted> / "linkbonder-clienthome" / "linkbonder-clienthome.yaml"
+TARGETS = <redacted> / "targets.tsv"
+
+# The note must sit in the first lines so it is the first thing read.
+HEADER_LINES = 12
+
+
+def _header() -> str:
+    # No try/except on purpose: under pytest a missing manifest already fails
+    # this test with a FileNotFoundError that names the full path.
+    return "\n".join(MANIFEST.read_text().splitlines()[:HEADER_LINES])
+
+
+def _parked_targets() -> list[str]:
+    rows = [
+        line.split()
+        for line in TARGETS.read_text().splitlines()
+        if line.strip() and not line.startswith("#")
+    ]
+    return [r[0] for r in rows if r[1] == "dispatch"]
+
+
+def test_the_manifest_opens_with_a_parked_note():
+    head = _header()
+    assert "PARKED" in head, "no PARKED marker in the first lines"
+    assert "legacy no. 27" in head, "the note must name what unblocks it"
+    assert "must not be applied" in head, "the note must forbid an apply"
+
+
+def test_every_dispatch_only_target_is_this_parked_manifest():
+    """A new dispatch-only target needs its own note and its own check."""
+    assert _parked_targets() == ["linkbonder-clienthome"]

## Intent
Class: logic
- iOS NextDNS settings: when iOS reports the per-user DNS setting disabled, the screen now says it was either never turned on or preempted by another VPN or DNS app, and names Settings > General > VPN & Device Management > DNS as the fix.
- NextDNS status wording moved into LinkbonderCompanionKit (DNSSettingsController.Status.headline/detail) so it is unit-tested; the settings screen reads it from there.
- docs/ios-client-mode.md documents which resolver wins in each mode (no tunnel, contribute, split tunnel, full tunnel) with the per-user DoH setting, and a device check for per-profile attribution.
Files: 2 logic, 2 tests, 1 docs

## Why
Users want their own NextDNS profile reporting their own device name wherever the phone is, not the router's shared profile. NextDNS supports per-user profiles in the DoH URL itself.

## Summary
iOS: add NEDNSSettingsManager with a per-user profile id and device name entered in Settings. The dns-settings entitlement is already in provisioning profiles; this is app code only. Show clearly when iOS reports the setting disabled due to another VPN/DNS app preempting it. Android: deep-link to <redacted> DNS with PROFILE.dns.nextdns.io when the app exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each phone's queries appear in its OWN NextDNS profile logs under the configured device name, on travel-router wifi and on cellular
- [ ] Interaction with the packet tunnel documented (which resolver wins in each mode)
- [ ] A per-user NextDNS profile id can be entered in Settings and saved
- [ ] The device name can be entered in Settings and saved

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Router-side NextDNS changes (travel-router keeps its own profile for LAN clients)
Refs ISSUE-136

-  preempt. The interaction has NOT been tested; this is design intent, not a

+- **ISSUE-25's `NEDNSSettingsManager`** is a separate, system-wide setting: the
+  per-user NextDNS DoH URL `https://dns.nextdns.io/<profile>/<device>`. Apple's
+  rule for combining the two (WWDC20 "Enable encrypted DNS"): "if a VPN is
+  active, resolution within the VPN tunnel will use the VPN's DNS settings and
+  not your system-wide settings." So, per mode, with the per-user setting
+  selected:
+
+  | Mode | Who resolves | Lands in the user's own NextDNS profile? |
+  |---|---|---|
+  | No tunnel (any wifi, cellular) | per-user DoH | yes |
+  | Contribute (no `dnsSettings`) | per-user DoH | yes |
+  | Client, split tunnel | tunnel for `ts.net`, per-user DoH for the rest | yes, except tailnet names |
+  | Client, full tunnel (`matchDomains = [""]`) | tunnel's resolver | no - home's resolver sees them |
+
+  On the travel router's wifi the per-user DoH goes to NextDNS over HTTPS
+  through the bond, not to the router's own resolver, so the router's shared
+  profile never sees these queries. Full-tunnel attribution needs home to
+  forward per client (ADR 0022); until then that mode reports to home's profile.
+
+  iOS keeps one DNS configuration selected at a time and saving never selects
+  it, so `isEnabled` is false both before the user turns it on and after another
+  VPN or DNS app is selected over it. The settings screen says so, with the
+  path to fix it (`DNSSettingsController.Status.detail`).
+
+  The table is Apple's documented behaviour, not yet a measurement. To check it
+  on a phone: set a profile and device name, select Linkbonder under Settings >
+  General > VPN & Device Management > DNS, browse once on the travel router's
+  wifi and once on cellular with wifi off, and confirm both appear in that
+  profile's NextDNS logs under the device name.

## Intent
Class: tests
- The reboot scan now checks shell scripts across the repository and rejects graceful reboot commands even after adb or sysrq on the same line.

## Why
Remote reboots of a travel router can hang forever because procd disarms the watchdog during shutdown, and a `reboot` command can get stuck in the shutdown sequence while sysrq reboots bypass it entirely.

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Loss driven DEGRADED state now requires twelve consecutive readings and twelve healthy readings to recover, while raw loss reporting and immediate failover remain unchanged.
Files: 2 logic, 2 tests

## Why
The loss estimator reports link loss as a proportion of a 40-sample window, but at a 24-sample resolution the reading quantizes to 0, 4.17, or 8.33 percent. A true 5% loss rate produces ordinary sampling variance where both 0 and 2 lost probes are common outcomes (~29% and ~22% of windows), so the leg's DEGRADED state flaps between up and degraded across seeds. The issue asks for a fix that addresses variance rather than widening the existing hysteresis band, which is already two quanta wide.

## Summary
Implement consecutive-reading hysteresis: require k readings past the threshold to enter DEGRADED and k below to leave, which is independent of both resolution and variance. This costs per-leg state alongside the existing recovery margin. Alternatively, smooth what the policy reads (a decaying average) while the console keeps the raw honest measurement. The RTT axis behavior must remain unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At a fixed injected loss of 5%, the leg state is the same across at least four seeds, proven from harness JSON
- [ ] No run alternates between up and degraded the way seeds 7 and 90210 do today, shown by state_passes
- [ ] A leg whose loss genuinely crosses the threshold still degrades, and one past failover_loss_pct still goes down
- [ ] The reported loss_pct on the console remains a real measurement
- [ ] The RTT axis behavior is unchanged
- [ ] A test fails without the fix on the VARIANCE (a sequence of readings from one true loss rate), not on a single hardcoded value

Size: S

## Out of scope
- The binary-loss bug (legacy no. 115)
- bufferbloat_shed_ratio and the RTT path (legacy no. 107)
- The retransmit step function (legacy no. 108)
- Widening recovery_margin, which is disproved as a solution in the issue
Rewritten from issue 173.

body:
## Intent
Class: tests
- The watchdog re-arm tests use a fixed shared clock, so exhausted-budget trips stay down regardless of the runner's wall clock.
Files: 1 tests

## Why
`tests/test_watchdog_rearm.py::test_budget_is_capped_so_a_flapping_device_stays_down` fails now and then on the unmodified main tree. When it does, a lane run stops before its agent starts and files a factory incident that holds link-bonder tickets. On 2026-10-19 the zen lane's run of example.link-bonder-309-r2 failed it at main 962c639 with `AssertionError: stays tripped until a human intervenes` (line 272), and filed factory ISSUE-1008. CI on the same commit passed, and two earlier lane runs that day passed the same base check.
The test seeds the rearm budget with `int(time.time())` ("inside the window; see set_tripped") and then runs the watchdog. The window is judged against the clock, so it is suspected that a slow run, or one crossing a second boundary, sees the budget outside the window and clears the trip. The test should not depend on wall-clock timing.

## Summary
- Make the test (and `set_tripped`/`set_budget` in its harness if needed) independent of wall-clock timing. For example, seed the budget timestamp well inside the window, or inject the clock the watchdog reads.
- Keep the anti-flap behavior it checks unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The test passes 200 runs in a row (`pytest -q tests/test_watchdog_rearm.py -k flapping --count 200` or a loop), including under `--timeout` load.
- [ ] A test still fails if the watchdog re-arms or clears the trip once the budget is exhausted.
- [ ] Live: no link-bonder factory incident titled "validation base-check" names `test_watchdog_rearm` in the 7 days after the merge (loom factory incidents).
Size: XS

Size: XS

## Out of scope
- Changing the watchdog's rearm budget or window.
- Other link-bonder tests.

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- The status screen now distinguishes an existing identity with unreadable dates from an unenrolled device and does not offer enrollment in that state.
- The status screen now displays the identity stance as a separate fact.
Files: 2 logic, 1 tests

## Why
When the agent asks an already-enrolled device to enroll again, the app home shows an empty enrollment form instead of the device's status. `EnrollActivity` constructs a `FileIdentityStore` but never calls `hasIdentity()`, so a valid certificate (`device.crt`, `CN=Pixel 6a`) goes undiscovered. For a Device Owner this app is the sole representation of the managing agent, so a false "you are not enrolled" message misleads the person holding the phone. The vocabulary for the right screen already exists: `IdentityLifecycle.Stance` models `Current`, `ShouldRenew`, `Lapsed`, `ClockBehind`, and `Unenrolled`, but is used only by the renewal path.

## Summary
Make the app's home a status screen and surface enrollment only from it. The status screen must show, all knowable on-device:
- Managed / not managed, from `isDeviceOwner`
- The identity's stance, and the certificate's not-after and renew-after
- The control plane URL, from `server-url`
- Restrictions actually in force, read back from `getUserRestrictions`
- Agent version
- When the agent last reconciled anything
Add a sync button: today the only trigger for reconciliation is `BOOT_COMPLETED`, a protected broadcast that cannot be fired from adb, so neither a person holding the phone nor an operator over adb can make it check in.
Extract the decision logic (has identity, stance, managed state, should enroll) into a pure object with tests; the Activity only renders.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An enrolled device does not show an enrollment form
- [ ] The screen names the stance, not just "enrolled"
- [ ] Restrictions shown are read back from the platform, not from config
- [ ] Sync reconciles and updates a visible last-check-in
- [ ] An unenrolled device can still reach enrollment
- [ ] Decision logic is a pure object with tests; the Activity only renders
- [ ] No new manifest permission

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Pushing diagnostics to Datadog. The agent deliberately carries no Datadog SDK to keep its four-permission profile that cleared Play Protect. The honest shape is agent -> device-fleet -> Datadog over the identity the device already holds, filed separately.
- The web console.
Refs ISSUE-92

## Intent
Class: logic
- device-fleet wallpaper now writes and verifies the matching wallpaper policy so the agent can apply the pushed image at boot.
Files: 1 logic, 2 tests, 1 docs

## Why
`device-fleet restrictions` and `device-fleet wallpaper` fail to place files in the agent's files directory because the directory is not world-traversable (`0700`), so the shell `cp` approach does not work. The same shell-based technique is relied upon by both commands and neither places a file on a device.

## Summary
Replace the `cp`-based push with an `adb shell "run-as app.device-fleet.agent sh -c 'cat > <path>'"` pipeline that writes through the app. Correct the misleading comment about the files dir being world-traversable. Keep the failure path loud so silent no-ops are not reintroduced.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `device-fleet restrictions` places the file on a device device-fleet owns
- [ ] `device-fleet wallpaper` does too, verified by the agent actually applying it
- [ ] The failure path stays loud - the current guard is the only reason this was caught rather than silently doing nothing
- [ ] The comment claiming the files dir is world-traversable is corrected
- [ ] Whatever replaces `run-as` is chosen with the release build in mind

Size: M

## Out of scope
- The restriction reconcile itself, which is proven working on hardware.
Refs ISSUE-90

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- A proven device presenting a certificate this CA signed that the <redacted> does not hold now gets it recorded from the certificate itself (real serial, not_before, not_after; issued_at and first_seen recovered as not_before plus the CA backdate), on any route that goes through _proven_device.
- Recording happens only after proofs.verify answers OK, so a certificate another CA signed, or a copy of one of ours presented without its key, still writes no row.
- Recording is idempotent: a device that proves repeatedly stays one device row with one certificate row, and a known certificate costs no extra store query on the ordinary path.
- A revoked device presenting an unrecorded certificate is still refused (403), and that certificate is now recorded so the CRL built from the <redacted> names it.
- New administrator route GET /v1/<redacted>/unrecorded lists, per device, every certificate this process signed that the store does not hold ("deferred" in the backlog, or "dropped" after backlog overflow or a permanent store refusal); it reads only memory and answers while the store is down.
- GET /v1/<redacted> now carries the same list as "unrecorded" beside the roll, so devices an outage cost are named once the store is back.
- Behavior change pinned by a rewritten test: an unrecorded device that proves can now renew; renewal still answers 403 "not in the <redacted>" when the store refused the record.
- New metric proof.unrecorded counts certificates written from a proof.
- Opt-in tests against a real PostgreSQL (DEVICEFLEET_TEST_DATABASE_URL) were run locally against PostgreSQL 17, including issue-during-outage, pod restart, then proof; the production store itself was not touched and the first device's row should be confirmed there after deploy.
Files: 2 logic, 2 tests, 3 docs

## Why
The first device Devicefleet enrolled has a certificate signed by this CA but no row in the <redacted>, making it invisible to listing and revocation. Issuance succeeded silently without a recorded <redacted> entry, and there is no way for an operator to see "issued but unrecorded" status per device.

## Summary
Provide a mechanism to record a device whose certificate was already issued (either by having the device present its certificate on next boot, or via an operator command that verifies the CA signed it). Also surface per-device "issued but unrecorded" status so operators can see when a specific device lacks a <redacted> row.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A device presenting a certificate this CA issued gets a <redacted> row matching its real serial and dates
- [ ] Nothing can write a <redacted> row for a certificate this CA did not issue
- [ ] A certificate issued while the store was unavailable is visible as unrecorded, per device, not just counted
- [ ] Recording the same device twice does not create a second device row
- [ ] Verified against the live store, not a fixture

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Drawing the device list in the console UI
- Renewal handling (legacy no. 44)
Rewritten from issue 104.

title: Record and surface devices enrolled before the store existed

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- The agent posts every check-in step's outcome and concerns, plus the installed versionCode of each managed package, to the new proven endpoint POST /v1/device/report.
- device-fleet stores the newest report per device in a new <redacted>_report table and returns it as "report" on GET /v1/<redacted>/{key_id}, with a concern count for monitors.
- The report route is bounded per field and to 16 KiB in total, rate-limited to one per device per minute, and answers 503 rather than queuing when the <redacted> store is down.
- Bytes that downloaded and failed to install are not fetched again for 30 minutes, doubling per failure up to a day, and the step reports BACKING_OFF.
- Before downloading, the agent compares the installed copy's signer with the signer a previous download of the same digest showed, and refuses with a WELDED concern naming INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE instead of retrying.
Files: 13 logic, 6 tests, 2 docs

## Why
The agent never reports install outcomes or versionCode to the server, so an MDM cannot tell if an app install succeeded. This issue asks for the agent to POST per-step outcomes, concerns, and installed versionCode per managed package so the server can truthfully answer "did it work" and so monitors can alert on failures (ref legacy no. 83).

## Summary
Add a reporting path from agent to server. After each step (download, install, etc.), the agent sends the step outcome and any concerns, plus the installed versionCode for each managed package. The server stores this so the status screen and external monitors reflect reality. Also add backoff for failing installs and a signer check: before downloading an APK the agent compares the fetched signer against the installed package signer; if they differ it refuses the install with a concern naming INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE instead of retrying.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Agent POSTs step outcome and concerns to server after each step (download, install, etc.)
- [ ] Agent POSTs installed versionCode for each managed package after install attempts
- [ ] Server accepts and stores step outcomes and versionCodes from agent
- [ ] Failing installs back off so the same 19.5MB payload is not re-fetched every check-in
- [ ] Before downloading, agent compares fetched APK signer to installed package signer and refuses with a concern if they differ
- [ ] Refusal surfaces as a concern naming INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE rather than retrying forever

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Adding an uninstall verb to device-fleet (operator can only re-sign or manually uninstall today; that is a separate decision)
- Alerting logic on the legacy monitor itself (legacy no. 83); this ticket only provides the data the monitor needs
- Changing /v1/device/config from pull-only to push (this adds POST reporting alongside existing pull, not a replacement)
Refs ISSUE-111

diff --git a/agent/android/app/src/main/java/app/device-fleet/agent/InstallGate.kt b/agent/android/app/src/main/java/app/device-fleet/agent/InstallGate.kt
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..96fc6e5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/agent/android/app/src/main/java/app/device-fleet/agent/InstallGate.kt
@@ -0,0 +1,132 @@
+package app.device-fleet.agent
+
+/**
+ * Whether to download an application's bytes at all, decided before spending
+ * them (ISSUE-146).
+ *
+ * WHY THIS EXISTS. An APK signed by a different key than the installed copy
+ * can never install over it - Android answers INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE
+ * every time - and the agent fetched the same 19.5 MB four times in eleven
+ * minutes on a phone that is itself somebody's uplink, failing identically
+ * each time, because nothing remembered the last attempt. Two rules end that:
+ *
+ *   BACK OFF. Bytes that failed to install are not fetched again until a wait
+ *   that doubles with each failure has passed. Keyed by the DIGEST the policy
+ *   names, so an operator who publishes a fixed build is not made to wait for
+ *   the broken one's clock.
+ *
+ *   REFUSE RATHER THAN RETRY. Once a download has shown which key signed those
+ *   bytes, that answer cannot change - the digest pins the bytes - so a later
+ *   check-in compares it against the installed copy's signer WITHOUT
+ *   downloading, and refuses with a concern naming the reason.
+ *
+ * Pure, so the deciding is tested on a JVM; `AppInstallSteward` reads the
+ * signers off the platform and keeps the record in `InstallLedger`.
+ */
+object InstallGate {
+
+    const val INCOMPATIBLE = "INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE"
+
+    /**
+     * Longer than the fifteen-minute check-in, or the first wait would expire
+     * before the next run and backing off would change nothing.
+     */
+    const val FIRST_BACKOFF_S: Long = 30 * 60
+
+    /** A day: a broken build is still retried daily, not abandoned. */
+    const val MAX_BACKOFF_S: Long = 24 * 60 * 60
+
+    /** How often installing one set of bytes has failed, and when to try again. */
+    data class Attempts(val failures: Int, val retryAtS: Long)
+
+    sealed interface Decision {
+        object Fetch : Decision
+
+        /** Failed recently; not fetched again until [attempts] says so. */
+        data class Wait(val attempts: Attempts) : Decision
+
+        /** Known to be signed by a key the installed copy will not accept. */
+        object Incompatible : Decision
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * @param installed the installed copy's signer digests; null when it is
+     *   not installed, empty when they could not be read.
+     * @param remembered the signer lineage of these exact bytes, from an
+     *   earlier download; null when none has been seen.
+     */
+    fun decide(
+        replaceIfSignerDiffers: Boolean,
+        installed: Set<String>?,
+        remembered: Set<String>?,
+        attempts: Attempts?,
+        nowS: Long,
+    ): Decision {
+        // THE REPLACE FLAG OPTS OUT OF THE REFUSAL, not out of the backoff: a
+        // line that authorizes removing the installed copy is asking for the
+        // mismatch to be resolved, and the steward does that after a download.
+        val knownToDiffer = !replaceIfSignerDiffers && installed != null && remembered != null &&
+            compatible(installed, remembered) == false
+        return when {
+            knownToDiffer -> Decision.Incompatible
+            attempts != null && nowS < attempts.retryAtS -> Decision.Wait(attempts)
+            else -> Decision.Fetch
+        }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Would Android accept bytes with this signer lineage over this install?
+     *
+     * THE LINEAGE, NOT ONLY THE CURRENT KEY. A v3 APK whose key rotated carries
+     * the history back to the old one and installs in place; comparing current
+     * keys alone would call that a mismatch and refuse an update that works.
+     * Null when either side could not be read - "I could not tell" must never
+     * read as "they differ".
+     */
+    fun compatible(installed: Set<String>, incomingLineage: Set<String>): Boolean? {
+        if (installed.isEmpty() || incomingLineage.isEmpty()) return null
+        return incomingLineage.containsAll(installed)
+    }
+
+    /** One more failure, and the wait before the next attempt. */
+    fun failed(previous: Attempts?, nowS: Long): Attempts {
+        val failures = (previous?.failures ?: 0) + 1
+        return Attempts(failures, nowS + backoffS(failures))
+    }
+
+    <redacted> fun backoffS(failures: Int): Long {
+        // Doubling stops well before a shift could overflow: 2^6 already
+        // passes a day from half an hour.
+        val doublings = (failures - 1).coerceIn(0, 16)
+        return (FIRST_BACKOFF_S shl doublings).coerceAtMost(MAX_BACKOFF_S)
+    }
+
+    /** The concern for a refusal, naming the reason Android would give. */
+    fun incompatible(packageName: String, asset: String): String =
+        "$packageName: $INCOMPATIBLE - the installed copy is signed by a different " +
+            "key, so $asset cannot install over it and is not downloaded again. " +
+            "Add 'replace-if-signer-differs' to the policy line to remove it " +
+            "first - THAT DELETES ITS DATA - or wipe the device."
+
+    /** The concern for a wait, saying when the next attempt is. */
+    fun waiting(packageName: String, attempts: Attempts, nowS: Long): String {
+        val minutes = ((attempts.retryAtS - nowS).coerceAtLeast(0) + 59) / 60
+        return "$packageName: installing failed ${attempts.failures} times; " +
+            "next attempt in ${minutes}m"
+    }
+
+    fun write(attempts: Attempts): String = "${attempts.failures}:${attempts.retryAtS}"
+
+    /** Null for anything damaged: no record is a fetch, never a refusal. */
+    fun readAttempts(text: String?): Attempts? {
+        val parts = text?.split(":")?.takeIf { it.size == 2 } ?: return null
+        val failures = parts[0].toIntOrNull() ?: return null
+        val retryAtS = parts[1].toLongOrNull() ?: return null
+        return Attempts(failures, retryAtS)
+    }
+
+    fun writeSigners(signers: Set<String>): String = signers.sorted().joinToString(",")
+
+    fun readSigners(text: String?): Set<String>? =
+        text?.split(",")?.filter { it.isNotEmpty() }?.toSet()?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }
+}
diff --git a/agent/android/app/src/main/java/app/device-fleet/agent/InstallLedger.kt b/agent/android/app/src/main/java/app/device-fleet/agent/InstallLedger.kt
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..6fe199c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/agent/android/app/src/main/java/app/device-fleet/agent/InstallLedger.kt
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+package app.device-fleet.agent
+
+import android.content.Context
+
+/**
+ * What earlier check-ins learned about installing each set of bytes, so the
+ * next one does not have to download them to find out again (ISSUE-146).
+ *
+ * Keyed by the sha256 the policy names. Those bytes cannot change under that
+ * name, so neither can their signer, and a failure recorded against them is a
+ * failure of exactly what would be fetched next. A policy that names a new
+ * build names a new digest and starts clean.
+ *
+ * DEVICE-PROTECTED, like everything else the boot path touches: install-apps
+ * runs from BOOT_COMPLETED, which on a locked phone fires before first unlock.
+ * The decisions themselves are `InstallGate`'s; this only remembers.
+ */
+class InstallLedger(context: Context) {
+
+    <redacted> val prefs = context.createDeviceProtectedStorageContext()
+        .getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_<redacted>)
+
+    fun attempts(digest: String): InstallGate.Attempts? =
+        InstallGate.readAttempts(prefs.getString(ATTEMPTS + digest, null))
+
+    /** Record one more failed install of these bytes, and return the new wait. */
+    fun failed(digest: String, nowS: Long): InstallGate.Attempts {
+        val attempts = InstallGate.failed(attempts(digest), nowS)
+        prefs.edit().putString(ATTEMPTS + digest, InstallGate.write(attempts)).apply()
+        return attempts
+    }
+
+    /** The signer lineage a download of these bytes showed, if one did. */
+    fun signers(digest: String): Set<String>? =
+        InstallGate.readSigners(prefs.getString(SIGNERS + digest, null))
+
+    fun rememberSigners(digest: String, lineage: Set<String>) {
+        if (lineage.isEmpty()) return
+        prefs.edit().putString(SIGNERS + digest, InstallGate.writeSigners(lineage)).apply()
+    }
+
+    /** These bytes installed: nothing about them needs remembering any more. */
+    fun succeeded(digest: String) {
+        prefs.edit().remove(ATTEMPTS + digest).remove(SIGNERS + digest).apply()
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Forget every digest the policy no longer names, so the record is bounded
+     * by the install file rather than by every build ever published.
+     */
+    fun keepOnly(digests: Set<String>) {
+        val stale = prefs.all.keys.filter { key ->
+            val digest = key.removePrefix(ATTEMPTS).removePrefix(SIGNERS)
+            digest !in digests
+        }
+        if (stale.isEmpty()) return
+        val edit = prefs.edit()
+        stale.forEach { edit.remove(it) }
+        edit.apply()
+    }
+
+    <redacted> companion object {
+        const val PREFS = "devicefleet-install-ledger"
+        const val ATTEMPTS = "attempts:"
+        const val SIGNERS = "signers:"
+    }
+}
diff --git a/agent/android/app/src/main/java/app/device-fleet/agent/ProvenPost.kt b/agent/android/app/src/main/java/app/device-fleet/agent/ProvenPost.kt
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e0bda7b
--- /dev/null
+++ b/agent/android/app/src/main/java/app/device-fleet/agent/ProvenPost.kt
@@ -0,0 +1,78 @@
+package app.device-fleet.agent
+
+import org.json.JSONObject
+
+/**
+ * One POST to device-fleet carrying this device's proof: challenge, sign, send.
+ *
+ * SHARED BY EVERY UPLOAD rather than written into each, because the server
+ * authenticates every device route in one place (`_proven_device`) and the
+ * client side of that should be one place too. Diagnostics and the check-in
+ * report both go up through this; a third upload is a path and a body, not a
+ * third copy of the handshake.
+ */
+class ProvenPost(
+    <redacted> val transport: EnrollmentClient.Transport,
+    <redacted> val identity: ConfigurationClient.Identity,
+) {
+    sealed interface Sent {
+        object Accepted : Sent
+        data class Refused(val status: Int) : Sent
+        data class Unreachable(val cause: String) : Sent
+        object NotEnrolled : Sent
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Sign a fresh nonce and POST [fields] with the proof added.
+     *
+     * @param accepted the status device-fleet answers when it took the upload.
+     */
+    fun send(path: String, fields: JSONObject, accepted: Int = 202): Sent {
+        val certificate = try {
+            identity.certificatePem() ?: return Sent.NotEnrolled
+        } catch (_: Exception) {
+            return Sent.Unreachable("identity unavailable")
+        }
+        val nonce = when (val challenge = challenge()) {
+            is Challenge.Nonce -> challenge.value
+            is Challenge.Failed -> return challenge.sent
+        }
+        val signature = try {
+            identity.signBase64(nonce)
+        } catch (_: Exception) {
+            return Sent.Unreachable("keystore signing failed")
+        }
+        fields.put("nonce", nonce)
+            .put("signature_b64", signature)
+            .put("certificate_pem", certificate)
+        val reply = try {
+            transport.post(path, fields.toString())
+        } catch (e: Exception) {
+            return Sent.Unreachable(e.javaClass.simpleName)
+        }
+        return if (reply.status == accepted) Sent.Accepted else Sent.Refused(reply.status)
+    }
+
+    <redacted> sealed interface Challenge {
+        data class Nonce(val value: String) : Challenge
+        data class Failed(val sent: Sent) : Challenge
+    }
+
+    <redacted> fun challenge(): Challenge {
+        val reply = try {
+            transport.post(CHALLENGE_PATH, "{}")
+        } catch (e: Exception) {
+            return Challenge.Failed(Sent.Unreachable(e.javaClass.simpleName))
+        }
+        if (reply.status != 201) return Challenge.Failed(Sent.Refused(reply.status))
+        return try {
+            Challenge.Nonce(JSONObject(reply.body).getString("nonce"))
+        } catch (_: Exception) {
+            Challenge.Failed(Sent.Unreachable("unreadable challenge"))
+        }
+    }
+
+    companion object {
+        const val CHALLENGE_PATH = "/v1/auth/challenge"
+    }
+}
diff --git a/agent/android/app/src/main/java/app/device-fleet/agent/ReportClient.kt b/agent/android/app/src/main/java/app/device-fleet/agent/ReportClient.kt

--- /dev/null
+++ b/agent/android/app/src/main/java/app/device-fleet/agent/ReportClient.kt
@@ -0,0 +1,116 @@
+package app.device-fleet.agent
+
+import org.json.JSONArray
+import org.json.JSONObject
+import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets
+
+/**
+ * Tell device-fleet what this check-in did, so whether it worked is a question the
+ * console can answer (ISSUE-146).
+ *
+ * THE GAP THIS CLOSES. `/v1/device/config` is pull-only, and every step's
+ * `concerns()` used to end on this phone's own status screen - which needs
+ * somebody holding it. An install that failed identically at every check-in was
+ * visible only as repeated downloads in the server log. This sends every step's
+ * outcome and concerns, and the installed versionCode of each managed package,
+ * once per check-in, after the steps have run.
+ *
+ * ONE POST AFTER THE LAST STEP, NOT ONE PER STEP. Each upload costs a challenge
+ * and a signature, and device-fleet keeps one report per device, so per-step posts
+ * would be eleven round trips to write the same row eleven times. The one case
+ * that ends the process before the post - device-fleet installing ITSELF - is the
+ * case that succeeded, and the next check-in reports the new version.
+ *
+ * BOUNDED HERE so device-fleet never has to refuse it: the server's limits are per
+ * field and per row, and a report it refuses is a check-in nobody hears about.
+ */
+class ReportClient(
+    transport: EnrollmentClient.Transport,
+    identity: ConfigurationClient.Identity,
+) {
+    <redacted> val post = ProvenPost(transport, identity)
+
+    /**
+     * @param versions every managed package to its installed versionCode, null
+     *   where it is not installed - which is an answer, not a missing one.
+     */
+    fun send(steps: List<SyncReport.Step>, versions: Map<String, Long?>): ProvenPost.Sent {
+        val fields = JSONObject()
+            .put("steps", bounded(steps))
+            .put("packages", packages(versions))
+        return post.send(REPORT_PATH, fields)
+    }
+
+    <redacted> class Entry(val name: String, val outcome: String, val concerns: List<String>)
+
+    /** What is left of the byte budget, spent one string at a time. */
+    <redacted> class Budget(var left: Int) {
+        /** The whole string if it fits, otherwise nothing. */
+        fun whole(text: String): String? {
+            val size = bytes(text)
+            if (size > left) return null
+            left -= size
+            return text
+        }
+
+        /** As much of the string as fits. */
+        fun prefix(text: String): String {
+            var cut = text.take(left.coerceAtLeast(0))
+            while (bytes(cut) > left) cut = cut.dropLast(1)
+            left -= bytes(cut)
+            return cut
+        }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Every step, CONCERNS BEFORE OUTCOMES. The concern is what an operator or
+     * a monitor acts on; the outcome is context. When the budget runs out it is
+     * the context that is cut, so a long outcome early in the plan cannot crowd
+     * out the one concern at the end of it.
+     */
+    <redacted> fun bounded(steps: List<SyncReport.Step>): JSONArray {
+        val entries = steps.take(MAX_STEPS).map { step ->
+            Entry(
+                name = step.name.take(MAX_NAME_CHARS),
+                outcome = step.outcome.toString().take(MAX_LINE_CHARS),
+                concerns = step.outcome.concerns().take(MAX_CONCERNS).map { it.take(MAX_LINE_CHARS) },
+            )
+        }
+        val budget = Budget(MAX_REPORT_BYTES - entries.sumOf { bytes(it.name) })
+        val concerns = entries.map { entry -> entry.concerns.mapNotNull { budget.whole(it) } }
+        val outcomes = entries.map { budget.prefix(it.outcome) }
+        return JSONArray(
+            entries.indices.map { i ->
+                JSONObject()
+                    .put("name", entries[i].name)
+                    .put("outcome", outcomes[i])
+                    .put("concerns", JSONArray(concerns[i]))
+            }
+        )
+    }
+
+    <redacted> fun packages(versions: Map<String, Long?>): JSONArray = JSONArray(
+        versions.entries.take(MAX_PACKAGES).map { (name, code) ->
+            JSONObject().put("package", name).put("version_code", code ?: JSONObject.NULL)
+        }
+    )
+
+    companion object {
+        const val REPORT_PATH = "/v1/device/report"
+        const val MAX_STEPS = 32
+        const val MAX_CONCERNS = 32
+        const val MAX_PACKAGES = 64
+        const val MAX_NAME_CHARS = 64
+        const val MAX_LINE_CHARS = 512
+
+        /**
+         * Below device-fleet's 16384, deliberately. The server bounds what it KEEPS,
+         * after redacting credential-shaped text, and a redaction can be longer
+         * than what it replaced - so a report sized to the exact limit here
+         * could be refused there.
+         */
+        const val MAX_REPORT_BYTES = 12_288
+
+        <redacted> fun bytes(text: String) = text.toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8).size
+    }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@
+package app.device-fleet.agent
+
+import android.content.Context
+
+/**
+ * Sends the check-in report (ISSUE-146) over the platform transport, with the
+ * managed packages' versions read from the platform after the steps ran.
+ */
+class ReportSteward(<redacted> val context: Context) {
+    fun send(steps: List<SyncReport.Step>): ProvenPost.Sent {
+        return try {
+            val baseUrl = KeystoreIdentity.serverBaseUrl(context)
+            if (baseUrl.isBlank()) {
+                return ProvenPost.Sent.Unreachable("no server configured")
+            }
+            val client = ReportClient(
+                HttpTransport(baseUrl, connectTimeoutMs = 5_000, readTimeoutMs = 5_000),
+                KeystoreIdentity(context),
+            )
+            client.send(steps, AppInstallSteward(context).managedVersions())
+        } catch (e: Exception) {
+            ProvenPost.Sent.Unreachable(e.javaClass.simpleName)
+        }
+    }
+}

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Added the device renewal endpoint at /v1/enroll/renew with signed proof and same-key renewal.
- Refused renewal for keys absent from the <redacted> and told lapsed devices to enroll again.
- Updated the Android agent and tests to call the canonical renewal endpoint.
Files: 2 logic, 2 tests, 3 docs

## Why
The server has no renewal endpoint, so `renew_after`, `IdentityLifecycle.stance()` returning `ShouldRenew`, and `backoffSeconds()` are dead code. Without renewal, lapse becomes a fleet-wide expiry date rather than a revocation mechanism, forcing expensive human-assisted re-enrollment.

## Summary
Add a `/v1/enroll/renew` endpoint that issues a second certificate to the same device, proving possession of the device's current key (via `proof.py`), requiring no pairing code and no vouch, and recording the new certificate against the same device in the <redacted> store.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A device holding a valid certificate can obtain a new one without a human
- [ ] Renewal proves possession of the device's current key
- [ ] Renewal does not require a pairing code or a vouch
- [ ] The <redacted> records a second certificate against the SAME device
- [ ] A device whose certificate has already lapsed is refused, and the refusal says it must enroll again
- [ ] A device presenting a key that is not in the <redacted> is refused
- [ ] The agent actually calls the renewal endpoint, with a test that fails if it stops

Size: L

## Out of scope
- Changing what lapse means. It stays the revocation mechanism.
- Certificate lifetime, which is a separate decision.
Refs ISSUE-99

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Increase scanned-path pairing code TTL to 600s to cover measured 332s Pixel 6a provisioning runs
Files: 2 logic, 3 tests, 2 docs

## Why
A Pixel 6a real provisioning run (factory reset to presenting the QR) takes 332s, measurably longer than `DEFAULT_CODE_TTL_S = 300.0`, causing a 410 refusal on the scanned path. The TTL must cover the measured provisioning time, not an assumed one.

## Summary
Increase the scanned-path pairing code TTL based on the measured 332s provisioning run, and document the measurement against the existing security reasoning so the next change starts from data, not an estimate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A QR-provisioned Pixel (Pixel 6a) can complete enrolment from factory reset without racing a timer
- [ ] The chosen window is justified against the measured provisioning run duration
- [ ] The security argument for a short window is preserved in comments or docs

Size: S

## Out of scope
- [ ] The agent crash that prevented the documented typed fallback from being reachable
Rewritten from issue 113.

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Web and worker no longer start a Datadog tracer: the ddtrace dependency and its patch_all() instrumentation are removed, so test runs stop printing dropped-traces and '--- Logging error ---' noise.
- JSON log lines no longer include dd.trace_id / dd.span_id; service, env and version tags from DD_* env vars are unchanged.
Files: 5 logic, 2 tests, 1 docs

## Why
Datadog has been shut down, but the `ddtrace` pytest plugin still builds and drops traces on each run, adding overhead and noisy logging. Disable the plugin or remove the dependency while preserving the capture pod's use of `DD_VERSION` for image pinning.

## Summary
Remove the unused test tracing behavior and any dependency that is no longer needed, without changing capture pod image version pinning.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Worker test runs emit no dropped-traces message or `--- Logging error ---` block.
- [ ] The `ddtrace` dependency is removed, or its pytest plugin is explicitly disabled.
- [ ] `DD_VERSION` remains available to capture pod image selection, and capture pod image tests pass.
- [ ] Worker and full test suites pass without reducing test coverage.
- [ ] If `ddtrace` is removed, no service Python files import it and dependency sync succeeds.

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Re-enabling Datadog telemetry or adding a Datadog API key.
- Removing DogStatsD metrics or changing capture pod image pinning strategy.
Rewritten from issue 246.

+"""Structured JSON logging carries the unified service tags without a tracer (ISSUE-263)."""
+
+import ast
+import json
+import logging
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from services.core import observability
+
+SERVICES_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+
+
+def _imported_roots(path: Path) -> set[str]:
+    roots = set()
+    for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(path.read_text())):
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
+            roots.update(alias.name.split(".")[0] for alias in node.names)
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
+            roots.add(node.module.split(".")[0])
+    return roots
+
+
+def test_no_service_module_imports_ddtrace():
+    # Datadog is shut down: a tracer only builds spans it then fails to send,
+    # flooding every test run with "dropping N traces" + "--- Logging error ---".
+    offenders = [
+        str(path.relative_to(SERVICES_DIR))
+        for path in SERVICES_DIR.rglob("*.py")
+        if "ddtrace" in _imported_roots(path)
+    ]
+    assert offenders == []
+
+
+def test_formatter_emits_dd_identity_from_env(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("DD_SERVICE", "media-library-worker")
+    monkeypatch.setenv("DD_ENV", "dev")
+    monkeypatch.setenv("DD_VERSION", "abc123")
+    record = logging.LogRecord("svc", logging.INFO, __file__, 1, "hello %s", ("you",), None)
+
+    entry = json.loads(observability.JSONFormatter().format(record))
+
+    assert entry["message"] == "hello you"
+    assert entry["level"] == "INFO"
+    assert entry["service"] == "media-library-worker"
+    assert entry["env"] == "dev"
+    assert entry["version"] == "abc123"

## Intent
Class: logic
- canonical.resolve_or_create_media_item now dedupes books by (owner_id, isbn) then (owner_id, openlibrary_id)
- canonical.resolve_or_create_media_item persists isbn and openlibrary_id on the create path
- canonical.resolve_or_create_media_item takes explicit igdb_id/isbn/openlibrary_id kwargs; ExternalRef removed
- media_items.resolve_media_item removed; its two callers now use the canonical facade
- manual_entry resolves through canonical.resolve_or_create_media_item; no resolve_media_item references remain
- tests exercise the canonical resolver including a resolve-create-resolve same-ISBN round trip
- Note: no git commit was created because the sandbox keeps `.git` read-only
- (index.lock write denied); the three source files above are modified and all
- checks pass.
Files: 3 logic, 2 tests

## Why
The canonical media item resolver handles games but does not deduplicate books or persist their ISBN and OpenLibrary identifiers. Move that behavior into the canonical resolver so book connectors and manual entry share one implementation.

## Summary
Update `canonical.resolve_or_create_media_item` to find books by owner and ISBN, then by owner and OpenLibrary ID, and persist both identifiers on creation. Route manual entry through this facade, remove the duplicate `media_items.resolve_media_item` implementation, and update resolver tests to exercise the canonical function.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] The canonical resolver deduplicates books by `(owner_id, isbn)` and then `(owner_id, openlibrary_id)`.
- [x] Creating a book through the canonical resolver persists its ISBN and OpenLibrary ID.
- [x] Manual entry uses the canonical resolver, and no references to the old `resolve_media_item` function remain.
- [x] Tests exercise the canonical resolver and include a resolve-create-resolve case proving the same ISBN returns one MediaItem.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Match-confidence scoring.
- Changes to `search_candidates` or `Candidate`.
- Schema or migration changes.
Part of ISSUE-264

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Connector credentials are now encrypted with a per-user data key (user_accounts.wrapped_dek) wrapped by the existing root key DL_CREDENTIAL_KEY, created on the user's first credential write.
- Both the data-key wrap (user) and each credential (user, connector id, platform) authenticate their context as AES-GCM associated data, so a ciphertext or wrapped key copied to another user's or connector's row fails to decrypt and the connector goes REAUTH_REQUIRED.
- Steam API key connect/reconnect, session-cookie capture, and Steam/Epic sync now seal and open credentials through seal_credential/open_credential with the owning user and connector; runtime no longer reads the old single-key format.
- Alembic revision b4d6f8a0c2e4 re-encrypts existing credentials into per-user envelopes on deploy (idempotent, aborts on an unreadable row) and its downgrade restores the single-key format for rollback.
- The web migrate initContainer now receives DL_CREDENTIAL_KEY and DL_DD_ENV=prod so the backfill runs with the real root key and stays fail-closed.
- DESIGN section 29 documents root-key custody and the backfill runbook (backup prerequisite, deploy window, rollback order).
Files: 11 logic, 9 tests, 2 docs

## Why
The issue asks to replace the shared credential encryption key with per-user envelope encryption and bind each credential to its user and connector, reducing the impact of key compromise and preventing ciphertext transplant.

## Summary
Add per-user data encryption keys wrapped by the existing root key, bind both wrapping and credential encryption to user and connector context, update credential callers, and provide an idempotent backfill for existing encrypted credentials with rollback guidance.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each connector credential uses a per-user data key wrapped by the existing root key.
- [ ] User and connector or provider context is authenticated on both DEK wrapping and credential encryption; cross-user or cross-connector transplant fails authentication.
- [ ] Credential encrypt/decrypt callers pass the owning user and connector context.
- [ ] An idempotent migration re-encrypts existing credentials and documents rollback.
- [ ] Tests cover cross-user isolation, and non-development environments retain fail-closed behavior.
- [ ] Documentation covers root-key custody and the backup prerequisite for running the backfill.

Size: L

## Out of scope
- Per-user Steam Web API key changes.
- Root key rotation or a broader tenant-isolation audit.
Rewritten from issue 154.

Two front-end mechanisms coexist: **HTMX** for same-URL partial swaps (the `/library` filter/search re-renders just `#grid`) and **vanilla-JS ES modules** (no build step) for the interactive overlays (⌘K palette, Sync Console, notifications, conflicts). **CDN Tailwind** + a `:root` design-token stylesheet (`tokens.css`) + a canonical custom-CSS file (`ledger.css`). **Deployed as a k8s Deployment** on the k8s-<redacted> (Talos <redacted> nodes), NOT as Lambda — but the web app retains a Mangum `lambda_handler.py` so the code stays portable to AWS Lambda if a Phase-2 migration ever happens. |

UserAccount is keyed `(oidc_issuer, oidc_subject)` (email is non-unique). Sessions are **revocable server-side** via the `user_sessions` table, carried in a signed session cookie (`samesite=lax`, required for the OAuth handshake). NOT Cognito/USER_PASSWORD_AUTH. Connector credentials are separate from user identity. |
 | **Database** | PostgreSQL. Neon serverless free tier for now (in-cluster Postgres deferred — see ADRs / project notes); migrate later via `pg_dump`/`pg_restore` with no application code change (`database_url` is config). SQLAlchemy 2.0 + Alembic. Connection string in SSM at `/example/media-library/database_url` (SecureString) → k8s secret `media-library-secrets`. Local dev: `.env` (gitignored). Pooler host (`-pooler` suffix) for pooling. Migrations run on every deploy via the web Deployment's `migrate` initContainer (`alembic upgrade head`). |
-| **Credential storage** | **AES-256-GCM** symmetric encryption (`services/core/crypto.py`: `encrypt_credential`/`decrypt_credential`), key from `settings.credential_key` (32-byte key in SSM `/example/media-library/credential_key`, seeded into `media-library-secrets`). **Fail-closed** outside dev envs (a missing key raises rather than falling back to the insecure dev key). Ciphertext stored on the connector account; server never holds plaintext at rest. NOT KMS per-user-CMK envelope (that was the earlier design; the shipped form is a single app key). **Session-capture, not passwords** (ADR-0003, supersedes ADR-0002's phased plan): for scraped sources we store only the captured **session cookies**, never the platform username/password — 2FA/CAPTCHA blocks headless auto-login (e.g. Epic) and stored third-party passwords are a non-starter for a public SaaS. |
+| **Credential storage** | **Per-user AES-256-GCM envelopes** (DESIGN section 29, ISSUE-252). The **root key** `settings.credential_key` (32-byte key in SSM `/example/media-library/credential_key`, seeded into `media-library-secrets`) wraps a random **data key (DEK) per user** (`user_accounts.wrapped_dek`); the DEK encrypts each connector credential. Both layers authenticate their context as AAD (the wrap: user; the credential: user + connector + platform), so a ciphertext or wrapped DEK moved to another user's or connector's row fails to decrypt. Callers use `services/core/domain/credentials.py` (`seal_credential`/`open_credential`, passing the owning user and connector), not `crypto.py` directly. **Fail-closed** outside dev envs (a missing root key raises rather than falling back to the insecure dev key). Ciphertext stored on the connector account; server never holds plaintext at rest. Not KMS: the root key is an app secret, not a cloud CMK. **Session-capture, not passwords** (ADR-0003, supersedes ADR-0002's phased plan): for scraped sources we store only the captured **session cookies**, never the platform username/password — 2FA/CAPTCHA blocks headless auto-login (e.g. Epic) and stored third-party passwords are a non-starter for a public SaaS. |
 | **Session capture** | The Plaid/MX-style connect flow: the user logs into the platform *themselves* (their own 2FA + CAPTCHA) inside a hosted, **isolated per-user browser** on the LAN scraper, and Digital Ledger keeps **only the resulting session cookies** (encrypted). The headless scraper later reuses those cookies to read the user's library; on expiry the connector goes REAUTH_REQUIRED and the user re-connects. The login UI is a polished modal popup (Plaid Link aesthetic). |

+"""Re-encrypt connector credentials into per-user envelopes (ISSUE-252).
+
+Shared by the Alembic migration and its test so the two cannot drift. Works on
+a raw Connection (not the ORM models) so later model changes cannot alter what
+the migration does.
+
+`upgrade_credentials` moves every pre-ISSUE-252 single-key blob to the per-user
+envelope format (DESIGN section 29), creating a wrapped DEK for each user that holds a
+credential. `downgrade_credentials` reverses it so the previous release can read
+credentials again. Both are idempotent: a row already in the target format is
+detected by authenticating it and is left byte-for-byte unchanged. A row
+readable in neither format aborts the run (naming the connector) rather than
+being skipped, since a wrong root key would otherwise look like "nothing to do".
+
+Prerequisite: back up `user_accounts` and `connector_accounts` before running
+(DESIGN section 29, "Envelope backfill runbook").
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+from cryptography.exceptions import InvalidTag
+from sqlalchemy import Connection, text
+
+from services.core.crypto import (
+    CredentialContext,
+    decrypt_credential,
+    decrypt_legacy_credential,
+    encrypt_credential,
+    encrypt_legacy_credential,
+    wrap_new_dek,
+)
+
+_CREDENTIAL_ROWS = text(
+    "SELECT c.id, c.owner_id, c.platform, c.encrypted_credential, u.wrapped_dek "
+    "FROM connector_accounts c JOIN user_accounts u ON u.id = c.owner_id "
+    "WHERE c.encrypted_credential IS NOT NULL ORDER BY c.id"
+)
+_SET_CREDENTIAL = text("UPDATE connector_accounts SET encrypted_credential = :blob WHERE id = :id")
+_SET_DEK = text("UPDATE user_accounts SET wrapped_dek = :dek WHERE id = :id")
+
+
+def _authenticates(decrypt: Callable[..., bytes], *args) -> bool:
+    """True if `decrypt(*args)` succeeds. InvalidTag is the expected answer for a
+    blob in the other format, so it is the "no" here, not an error."""
+    try:
+        decrypt(*args)
+    except InvalidTag:
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def _unreadable(connector_id: str) -> RuntimeError:
+    return RuntimeError(
+        f"connector {connector_id}: credential is readable in neither the legacy "
+        "nor the envelope format; check DL_CREDENTIAL_KEY, or clear this row's "
+        "encrypted_credential (the user reconnects) and re-run"
+    )
+
+
+def _context(row) -> CredentialContext:
+    return CredentialContext(user_id=row.owner_id, connector_id=row.id, platform=row.platform)
+
+
+def _upgrade_row(conn: Connection, row, deks: dict[str, bytes]) -> bool:
+    context = _context(row)
+    dek = deks.get(row.owner_id)
+    blob = row.encrypted_credential
+    if dek is not None and _authenticates(decrypt_credential, blob, dek, context):
+        return False
+    try:
+        plaintext = decrypt_legacy_credential(blob)
+    except InvalidTag as e:
+        raise _unreadable(row.id) from e
+    if dek is None:
+        dek = deks[row.owner_id] = wrap_new_dek(row.owner_id)
+        conn.execute(_SET_DEK, {"dek": dek, "id": row.owner_id})
+    sealed = encrypt_credential(plaintext, dek, context)
+    conn.execute(_SET_CREDENTIAL, {"blob": sealed, "id": row.id})
+    return True
+
+
+def _downgrade_row(conn: Connection, row) -> bool:
+    blob = row.encrypted_credential
+    if _authenticates(decrypt_legacy_credential, blob):
+        return False
+    if row.wrapped_dek is None:
+        raise _unreadable(row.id)
+    try:
+        plaintext = decrypt_credential(blob, row.wrapped_dek, _context(row))
+    except InvalidTag as e:
+        raise _unreadable(row.id) from e
+    conn.execute(_SET_CREDENTIAL, {"blob": encrypt_legacy_credential(plaintext), "id": row.id})
+    return True
+
+
+def upgrade_credentials(conn: Connection) -> int:
+    """Legacy single-key blobs -> per-user envelopes. Returns rows rewritten."""
+    rows = conn.execute(_CREDENTIAL_ROWS).all()
+    deks = {row.owner_id: row.wrapped_dek for row in rows if row.wrapped_dek is not None}
+    return sum(_upgrade_row(conn, row, deks) for row in rows)
+
+
+def downgrade_credentials(conn: Connection) -> int:
+    """Per-user envelopes -> legacy single-key blobs. Returns rows rewritten.
+
+    Leaves `user_accounts.wrapped_dek` in place; the migration drops the column.
+    """
+    rows = conn.execute(_CREDENTIAL_ROWS).all()
+    return sum(_downgrade_row(conn, row) for row in rows)

+
+Revision ID: b4d6f8a0c2e4

+
+Adds `user_accounts.wrapped_dek` and re-encrypts every existing
+`connector_accounts.encrypted_credential` from the single root-key format into a
+per-user envelope bound to its user, connector and platform. Logic lives in
+services.core.db.credential_backfill so the migration and its test share one
+source; both directions are idempotent (see that module).

+initContainer carries both. Back up `user_accounts` and `connector_accounts`
+first. Rollback: run `alembic downgrade f1a2b3c4d5e6` with THIS release's image
+BEFORE deploying the previous image, so credentials are back in the format the
+old code reads (DESIGN section 29, "Envelope backfill runbook").
+"""
+
+import logging
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+
+import sqlalchemy as sa
+from alembic import op
+from services.core.db.credential_backfill import downgrade_credentials, upgrade_credentials
+
+log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+revision: str = "b4d6f8a0c2e4"
+down_revision: str | None = "f1a2b3c4d5e6"
+branch_labels: str | Sequence[str] | None = None
+depends_on: str | Sequence[str] | None = None
+
+
+def upgrade() -> None:
+    op.add_column("user_accounts", sa.Column("wrapped_dek", sa.LargeBinary(), nullable=True))
+    try:
+        upgrade_credentials(op.get_bind())
+    except Exception as exc:
+        log.error("credential envelope backfill failed: %s", exc)

+"""Connector credential sealing (DESIGN section 29, ISSUE-252).
+
+The ORM-facing side of `services.core.crypto`: callers pass the owning user and
+the connector, and this resolves the user's wrapped data key (creating it on
+first use) and the `CredentialContext` that binds the credential to both.
+"""
+
+from cryptography.exceptions import InvalidTag
+from sqlalchemy import update
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
+
+from services.core.crypto import (
+    CredentialContext,
+    decrypt_credential,
+    encrypt_credential,
+    wrap_new_dek,
+)
+from services.core.db.models import ConnectorAccount, UserAccount
+
+
+def _context(owner: UserAccount, connector: ConnectorAccount) -> CredentialContext:
+    if connector.owner_id != owner.id:
+        raise ValueError(f"connector {connector.id} is not owned by user {owner.id}")
+    if connector.id is None:
+        raise ValueError("connector must be flushed (have an id) before sealing its credential")
+    return CredentialContext(
+        user_id=owner.id, connector_id=connector.id, platform=connector.platform.name
+    )
+
+
+def _ensure_owner_dek(db: Session, owner: UserAccount) -> bytes:
+    """The owner's wrapped DEK, created on first use.
+
+    Written only WHERE it is still NULL, then re-read: if two first-time writes
+    for the same user race, both end up with the one DEK that landed, rather
+    than the later write orphaning the earlier credential.
+    """
+    if owner.wrapped_dek is None:
+        db.flush()
+        db.execute(
+            update(UserAccount)
+            .where(UserAccount.id == owner.id, UserAccount.wrapped_dek.is_(None))
+            .values(wrapped_dek=wrap_new_dek(owner.id))
+            .execution_options(synchronize_session=False)
+        )
+        db.refresh(owner, ["wrapped_dek"])
+    return owner.wrapped_dek
+
+
+def seal_credential(
+    db: Session, owner: UserAccount, connector: ConnectorAccount, plaintext: str | bytes
+) -> None:
+    """Encrypt `plaintext` under `owner`'s DEK onto `connector.encrypted_credential`."""
+    context = _context(owner, connector)
+    connector.encrypted_credential = encrypt_credential(
+        plaintext, _ensure_owner_dek(db, owner), context
+    )
+
+
+def open_credential(owner: UserAccount, connector: ConnectorAccount) -> bytes:
+    """Decrypt `connector.encrypted_credential`. Raises InvalidTag when it does
+    not authenticate for this owner + connector."""
+    context = _context(owner, connector)
+    if owner.wrapped_dek is None:
+        # No DEK means nothing was ever sealed for this owner, so the stored
+        # blob cannot be theirs: report it as the authentication failure it is.
+        raise InvalidTag(f"user {owner.id} has no credential data key")
+    return decrypt_credential(connector.encrypted_credential, owner.wrapped_dek, context)

--- /dev/null
+++ b/services/core/tests/test_credential_backfill.py
@@ -0,0 +1,119 @@
+"""Backfill of single-key credentials to per-user envelopes (ISSUE-252).
+
+The Alembic migration calls `upgrade_credentials` / `downgrade_credentials`;
+these exercise the same functions on SQLite. Both directions must be idempotent
+(re-running changes nothing) and an unreadable blob must abort, not be skipped.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+
+from services.core import crypto
+from services.core.db.credential_backfill import downgrade_credentials, upgrade_credentials
+from services.core.db.models import ConnectorAccount, ConnectorStatus, Platform, UserAccount
+from services.core.domain.credentials import open_credential
+
+
+def _seed(db):
+    """Two users with legacy (pre-envelope) credentials and one keyless user."""
+    for uid in ("alice", "bob", "carol"):
+        db.add(UserAccount(id=uid, email=f"{uid}@x.com", display_name=uid))
+    rows = [
+        ("alice-steam", "alice", Platform.STEAM, crypto.encrypt_legacy_credential("a-steam")),
+        ("alice-epic", "alice", Platform.EPIC, crypto.encrypt_legacy_credential("a-epic")),
+        ("bob-steam", "bob", Platform.STEAM, crypto.encrypt_legacy_credential("b-steam")),
+        ("carol-steam", "carol", Platform.STEAM, None),
+    ]
+    for cid, owner, platform, blob in rows:
+        db.add(
+            ConnectorAccount(
+                id=cid,
+                owner_id=owner,
+                platform=platform,
+                status=ConnectorStatus.CONNECTED,
+                encrypted_credential=blob,
+            )
+        )
+    db.commit()
+
+
+def _blobs(db):
+    return {c.id: c.encrypted_credential for c in db.query(ConnectorAccount).all()}
+
+
+def _opened(db, cid):
+    connector = db.get(ConnectorAccount, cid)
+    return open_credential(connector.owner, connector)
+
+
+def test_upgrade_reencrypts_every_credential_under_its_owner(db):
+    _seed(db)
+    assert upgrade_credentials(db.connection()) == 3
+    db.commit()
+    db.expire_all()
+    assert _opened(db, "alice-steam") == b"a-steam"
+    assert _opened(db, "alice-epic") == b"a-epic"
+    assert _opened(db, "bob-steam") == b"b-steam"
+
+
+def test_upgrade_creates_deks_only_for_credential_holders(db):
+    _seed(db)
+    upgrade_credentials(db.connection())
+    db.commit()
+    db.expire_all()
+    assert db.get(UserAccount, "alice").wrapped_dek is not None
+    assert db.get(UserAccount, "bob").wrapped_dek is not None
+    assert db.get(UserAccount, "carol").wrapped_dek is None
+    assert db.get(ConnectorAccount, "carol-steam").encrypted_credential is None
+
+
+def test_upgrade_is_idempotent(db):
+    _seed(db)
+    upgrade_credentials(db.connection())
+    db.commit()
+    before = _blobs(db)
+    assert upgrade_credentials(db.connection()) == 0
+    db.commit()
+    db.expire_all()
+    assert _blobs(db) == before
+
+
+def test_upgrade_aborts_on_unreadable_blob(db):
+    _seed(db)
+    db.get(ConnectorAccount, "bob-steam").encrypted_credential = b"not-a-credential"
+    db.commit()
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="bob-steam"):
+        upgrade_credentials(db.connection())
+
+
+def test_downgrade_restores_legacy_format(db):
+    _seed(db)
+    upgrade_credentials(db.connection())
+    db.commit()
+    assert downgrade_credentials(db.connection()) == 3
+    db.commit()
+    db.expire_all()
+    for cid, plaintext in [("alice-steam", b"a-steam"), ("bob-steam", b"b-steam")]:
+        blob = db.get(ConnectorAccount, cid).encrypted_credential
+        assert crypto.decrypt_legacy_credential(blob) == plaintext
+
+
+def test_downgrade_is_idempotent(db):
+    _seed(db)
+    upgrade_credentials(db.connection())
+    downgrade_credentials(db.connection())
+    db.commit()
+    before = _blobs(db)
+    assert downgrade_credentials(db.connection()) == 0
+    db.commit()
+    db.expire_all()
+    assert _blobs(db) == before
+
+
+def test_downgrade_aborts_on_unreadable_blob(db):
+    _seed(db)
+    upgrade_credentials(db.connection())
+    db.commit()
+    db.get(ConnectorAccount, "alice-epic").encrypted_credential = b"not-a-credential"
+    db.commit()
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="alice-epic"):
+        downgrade_credentials(db.connection())

+
+`seal_credential` / `open_credential` take the owning user and the connector, so
+a credential is bound to both. These pin lazy per-user DEK creation, cross-user
+and cross-connector isolation on stored rows, and fail-closed outside dev.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+from cryptography.exceptions import InvalidTag
+from sqlalchemy import update
+
+from services.core import crypto
+from services.core.config import settings
+from services.core.db.models import ConnectorAccount, ConnectorStatus, Platform, UserAccount
+from services.core.domain.credentials import open_credential, seal_credential
+
+
+def _user(db, uid):
+    user = UserAccount(id=uid, email=f"{uid}@x.com", display_name=uid)
+    db.add(user)
+    db.flush()
+    return user
+
+
+def _connector(db, owner, platform=Platform.STEAM):
+    connector = ConnectorAccount(
+        id=f"{owner.id}-{platform.name.lower()}",
+        owner_id=owner.id,
+        platform=platform,
+        status=ConnectorStatus.CONNECTED,
+    )
+    db.add(connector)
+    db.flush()
+    return connector
+
+
+def test_seal_open_round_trip(db):
+    alice = _user(db, "alice")
+    steam = _connector(db, alice)
+    seal_credential(db, alice, steam, "alice-key")
+    db.commit()
+    assert open_credential(alice, steam) == b"alice-key"
+    assert b"alice-key" not in steam.encrypted_credential
+
+
+def test_first_seal_creates_one_dek_and_reuses_it(db):
+    alice = _user(db, "alice")
+    assert alice.wrapped_dek is None
+    seal_credential(db, alice, _connector(db, alice, Platform.STEAM), "a")
+    first = alice.wrapped_dek
+    assert first is not None
+    seal_credential(db, alice, _connector(db, alice, Platform.EPIC), "b")
+    assert alice.wrapped_dek == first
+
+
+def test_seal_keeps_a_dek_written_concurrently(db):
+    """Another transaction created the DEK after this session loaded the user;
+    the conditional write must not clobber it (that would orphan its credential)."""
+    alice = _user(db, "alice")
+    db.commit()
+    assert alice.wrapped_dek is None
+    concurrent = crypto.wrap_new_dek("alice")
+    db.execute(
+        update(UserAccount)
+        .where(UserAccount.id == "alice")
+        .values(wrapped_dek=concurrent)
+        .execution_options(synchronize_session=False)
+    )
+    seal_credential(db, alice, _connector(db, alice), "a")
+    assert alice.wrapped_dek == concurrent
+
+
+def test_cross_user_transplant_fails(db):
+    alice, bob = _user(db, "alice"), _user(db, "bob")
+    alice_steam, bob_steam = _connector(db, alice), _connector(db, bob)
+    seal_credential(db, alice, alice_steam, "alice-key")
+    seal_credential(db, bob, bob_steam, "bob-key")
+    bob_steam.encrypted_credential = alice_steam.encrypted_credential
+    db.commit()
+    with pytest.raises(InvalidTag):
+        open_credential(bob, bob_steam)
+
+
+def test_cross_connector_transplant_fails(db):
+    alice = _user(db, "alice")
+    steam, epic = _connector(db, alice, Platform.STEAM), _connector(db, alice, Platform.EPIC)
+    seal_credential(db, alice, steam, "steam-key")
+    epic.encrypted_credential = steam.encrypted_credential
+    db.commit()
+    with pytest.raises(InvalidTag):
+        open_credential(alice, epic)
+
+
+def test_credential_without_owner_dek_fails_authentication(db):
+    alice = _user(db, "alice")
+    steam = _connector(db, alice)
+    steam.encrypted_credential = crypto.encrypt_legacy_credential("pre-envelope")
+    with pytest.raises(InvalidTag):
+        open_credential(alice, steam)
+
+
+def test_wrong_owner_is_rejected(db):
+    alice, bob = _user(db, "alice"), _user(db, "bob")
+    steam = _connector(db, alice)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        seal_credential(db, bob, steam, "x")
+
+
+def test_unflushed_connector_is_rejected(db):
+    alice = _user(db, "alice")
+    pending = ConnectorAccount(owner_id=alice.id, platform=Platform.STEAM)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        seal_credential(db, alice, pending, "x")
+
+
+def test_prod_without_root_key_fails_closed(db, monkeypatch):
+    alice = _user(db, "alice")
+    steam = _connector(db, alice)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "credential_key", "")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "dd_env", "prod")
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
+        seal_credential(db, alice, steam, "x")
+    assert steam.encrypted_credential is None

criteria.text: Each connector credential uses a per-user data key wrapped by the existing root key.
User and connector or provider context is authenticated on both DEK wrapping and credential encryption; cross-user or cross-connector transplant fails authentication.
Credential encrypt/decrypt callers pass the owning user and connector context.
An idempotent migration re-encrypts existing credentials and documents rollback.
Tests cover cross-user isolation, and non-development environments retain fail-closed behavior.
Documentation covers root-key custody and the backup prerequisite for running the backfill.

body:
## Why
Part of ISSUE-34. Loom runs eighteen lanes on different models (Opus 5.5 on the anthropic slots, gpt-6-luna on codex, Kimi on opencode-go, GLM flash on zai, Qwen on workersai, Gemini on agy, free OpenRouter models), and the brain chooses among them by a hand-written order. None of these models has a measurement on Loom's work, although every lane already leaves a full record: each lane pull request's body ends with a line naming its ticket, lane and model, and each ticket's comments record the claim, the pull request or the failure, and every fix round. On 2026-10-12 the agy lane failed every real ticket and the zai lane crashed on a medium one, and nothing measured it.

## Summary
- New suite `suites/loom_lanes/` (follow the existing suites' layout and README style): a collector that reads, with the GitHub CLI, the lane pull requests (head branch `loom/...`) and their tickets in the repos it is given, and builds one row per lane and model: tickets taken, pull requests opened, merged with no fix round, fix rounds per merged pull request, failures by reason, median minutes from claim to pull request, and review-bot findings per pull request (high severity separately).
- Repos come from the command line; for a <redacted> repo only counts are written, never titles, bodies or names.
- Results go to `suites/loom_lanes/results/scoreboard.json` with the date and window, and the README scoreboard gains a "Loom lanes" table (or column) generated from it, like the other suites.
- Tests with recorded fixture data (no network): parsing the lane footer line, counting fix rounds from ticket comments, classifying failures, and the <redacted>-repo rule that only counts are written.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The collector turns fixture pull requests and tickets into the right per-lane rows, counting fix rounds and failure reasons (tests that fail without the suite)
- [ ] A <redacted> repo contributes counts only, never text (test)
- [ ] Live: a run over the last 7 days of Loom work publishes the Loom lanes scoreboard with a row for every lane that took a ticket

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Changing Loom's lane choice (the brain uses the scoreboard in a later ticket)
- Running synthetic tasks against the lanes

---
Loom ticket example.bench-suite-35-r4, lane anthropic, model claude-opus-5-5.
Refs ISSUE-35
