## Intent
Class: sensitive
- A loom:running ticket on a local lane with no live heartbeat for 30 minutes moves to a free lane of its tier or Model (else back to loom:queued) with a comment naming the lane and its silence; it counts as no failure and no retry.
- The station files a silent-lane invariant naming each lane that held a running ticket while silent.
Files: 1 sensitive, 2 logic, 3 tests, 1 docs

## Why
A ticket stays `loom:running` for as long as its lane's runner never reports back. When a lane is stopped (unloaded, crashed, or its machine off), nothing reports, so the claim never ends. On 2026-10-16 four tickets (ISSUE-484, and one each in three other goal repos) sat `loom:running` for 20 hours on four Anthropic lanes that had been unloaded at about 00:05Z. No pass moved them, no invariant fired, and two standups listed them as in flight. `_retry` only runs on a failure the runner reports.

## Summary
- Each station pass, a `loom:running` ticket whose lane has had no live heartbeat (`_heartbeat_ok` false) for 30 minutes is moved like a transient failure: a comment naming the lane and how long it has been silent, then `loom:briefed` on a free lane of the ticket's tier (or its rung lane for a Model: ticket), or back to `loom:queued` when none is free.
- The move does not count as a failure on the ticket's model (it never climbs the ladder) and does not use one of its automatic retries.
- The station files or updates one invariant naming each lane that held a running ticket while silent.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A unit test with a running ticket on a lane silent for 31 minutes asserts it moves to a free lane of its tier with the comment, and that no failure or retry is recorded.
- [ ] A unit test asserts a lane silent for 29 minutes, or a live lane, leaves the ticket untouched.
- [ ] A unit test asserts that with no free lane of the tier the ticket goes back to `loom:queued`, and the invariant names the silent lane.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Restarting or reloading any lane.
- Remote pull lanes whose claims the existing remote heartbeat rules already cover.

## Intent
Class: logic
- Intent (ISSUE-934): classify a limit/credit even when more CLI output follows the limit line.
- classify_failure matches the limit and account-credit patterns against the whole run/tick output (from LOG_START), not only the last five non-blank lines, so a usage limit followed by more output is classed `limit` and holds the lane/parked brief until the reset.
- The auth and transient (network) patterns still match the short tail, so their classification and the failure reason shown to people are unchanged.
- lanes/mac/brain.sh classifies a tick's limit from the whole tick output, so a limit printed before more output still steps the ladder to the next rung.
Files: 3 logic, 1 tests

## Why
A run that ends on a provider usage limit is logged `[work] agent exited 1` when the CLI prints more lines after the limit message. `lanes/run_lane.sh` (line 1869) passes only the last 5 non-blank lines of the run's log to `classify_failure`. Codex prints `failed to record rollout items` three times, then `tokens used` and the count, after `You've hit your usage limit`. Those last 5 lines never contain the limit text. Each such run burns a work attempt, counts toward the runaway detector and the ladder, and leaves the lane unheld, so the next ticket hits the same limit.
Seen again 2026-10-19 03:33:49Z: review-bot ISSUE-1186 r7 on codex-2 ended with two `ERROR: You've hit your usage limit ... try again at Oct 19th, 2026 12:07 AM` lines, then three rollout lines, `tokens used` and `42,964`. The log reads `[2026-10-19T03:33:49Z] example.review-bot-1186-r7 failed: [work] agent exited 1`. The ticket now carries `loom:runaway` even though r4, r5 and r6 all finished. The same split was seen on 10-17 at 20:15Z for game-orchestrator ISSUE-1106 r3 on codex-2, while the same message on codex for ISSUE-1108 was read as `[limit]`.

## Summary
Classify a failed run's limit and credit patterns against the whole run output (from `LOG_START` to the end), not the last 5 non-blank lines. Keep the 5-line tail for the failure reason text shown to people. Any other pattern that needs the tail can keep it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A run whose output has a usage-limit line followed by 5 or more other non-blank lines is classed `limit`, and the lane is held until the reset. A test feeds the review-bot ISSUE-1186 r7 tail.
- [ ] A finished run whose summary mentions a rate limit is still not classed `limit` (the existing guard on `STATUS` and `EDITED` holds). A test covers it.
- [ ] The failure reason recorded for people is still the short tail.
- [ ] Live: over 24 hours after the deploy, no lane log line `failed: [work] agent exited 1` follows a run whose output contains `hit your usage limit` (grep of the codex and codex-2 lane logs).

Size: S

## Out of scope
Changing the limit patterns themselves, or the hold lengths.

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- The station restates shipped Live criteria that lack searchable exact strings using the configured rewrite command and shared hourly budget.
- Verify dispatch skips shipped tickets with Live criteria that provide no searchable exact strings.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
Most shipped tickets can never be verified, so Throughput stays near zero (3 of 72 verified on 2026-10-18). On 2026-10-19, 200 open `loom:shipped` tickets across the goal repos were read:
- 104 have no `Live:` criterion at all.
- 67 have a Live criterion that names no exact string (no backticks or quotes), so `evidence.needles` finds nothing and the verify brief carries no log data.
- 29 name an exact string.
The station still hands the 67 to verify lanes. The station log holds 134 "left it shipped: Missing evidence" results across 120 tickets; some were tried up to 8 times (dungeon-module ISSUE-23). Each attempt is a lane run that cannot succeed. docs/<redacted>.md tells the brain to restate such a Live line with `bus.brain live` (ISSUE-932), but neither log shows a restate since ISSUE-932 deployed.

## Summary
- A station step restates the Live criterion of a shipped ticket that names no exact string. It asks the configured rewrite command (the same sandboxed free model as the rewrite step) for one `Live:` line that names a string the merged pull request makes the live system print or serve. It applies the line with `brain.restate_live`, so `rewrite.validate` and `_check_live_criterion` still gate it.
- The step shares the rewrite step's hourly budget and posts no comment. A reply that fails the checks leaves the ticket as it was and logs one line; the ticket is not tried again for a day.
- The verify step skips a shipped ticket whose Live criterion names no exact string. It logs one line per pass with the count skipped, not one per ticket, so no lane run is spent on a verify that has no evidence to read.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test: a shipped ticket whose Live line names no exact string, with a rewrite reply naming `the string`, ends with a Live line containing `the string` and no new comment. It fails on main.
- [ ] A test: the verify step hands no lane a shipped ticket whose Live line names no exact string, and does hand one whose Live line does.
- [ ] Live: within a day of the deploy, the station log shows "restated the Live criterion of" for at least ten shipped tickets, and the count of "left it shipped: Missing evidence" lines per day falls below half of the 2026-10-19 count (station log).
Size: M

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Shipped tickets with no Live criterion at all (104); their verify path is a separate decision.
- Adding evidence commands for repos that have none.
Part of ISSUE-705

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- The factory sends lane pull requests back when they leave a non-Live ticket criterion unticked and files a follow-up for criteria marked not built with a reason.
- ## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A test: a 6-criterion ticket whose pull request body ticks 2 non-Live criteria is sent back and not merged; it fails on main.
- [x] A test: a pull request that ticks every non-Live criterion lands as before.
- [ ] Live: for 7 days after the deploy, every lane pull request the factory merges has every non-Live criterion ticked (GitHub search of merged lane pull request bodies).
Files: 1 sensitive, 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
A lane pull request that builds part of its ticket lands and marks the whole ticket merged. On 2026-10-20, game-module ISSUE-975 (a lane pull request, `Refs` its ticket) built about 2 of game-module ISSUE-964's 6 criteria. The factory landed it, and `brain.merge` set `loom:merged` two seconds later.
- The factory checks for a test, the review and the checks before landing, never the ticket's criteria (`bus/factory.py` `_land_or_ask_test`).
- `lanes/run_lane.sh` copies the ticket's criteria into the pull request body unticked, so nothing records what was built.
- Once shipped, `close_done_tickets` closes a ticket with no findable Live string, so the four unbuilt criteria close with it.
Reported on ISSUE-1026.

## Summary
- The lane ticks, in the pull request body, each criterion it built; Live criteria stay unticked.
- Before landing, the factory sends back a pull request with an unticked criterion other than a Live one, like the no-test send-back: build it, or say in the body why it is not this ticket's.
- A criterion the lane marks "not built: <reason>" is not sent back; the factory files the follow-up ticket for it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test: a 6-criterion ticket whose pull request body ticks 2 non-Live criteria is sent back and not merged; it fails on main.
- [ ] A test: a pull request that ticks every non-Live criterion lands as before.
- [ ] Live: for 7 days after the deploy, every lane pull request the factory merges has every non-Live criterion ticked (GitHub search of merged lane pull request bodies).
Size: M

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Proving the ticked criteria; review and verify runs still do that.
- Tickets merged before the change.
Part of ISSUE-705

+    """Checkbox criteria in the Acceptance criteria section."""
+    found = []
+    active = False
+    for line in (body or "").splitlines():
+        if line.strip() == "## Acceptance criteria":
+            active = True
+            continue
+        if active and line.startswith("## "):
+            break
+        match = CRITERION_RE.match(line)
+        if active and match:

+def missing_criteria(ticket_body: str, pull_body: str) -> List[str]:
+    """Ticket criteria that a lane PR leaves unticked, excluding Live checks."""
+    ticket = acceptance_criteria(ticket_body)
+    pull = acceptance_criteria(pull_body)
+    states = {}
+    for criterion in pull:
+        checked, _, text = criterion.partition(" ")
+        clean = NOT_BUILT_RE.sub("", text).strip().casefold()
+        states[clean] = (checked == "x", bool(NOT_BUILT_RE.search(text)))
+    missing = []
+    for criterion in ticket:
+        _, _, text = criterion.partition(" ")
+        if text.casefold().startswith("live:"):
+            continue
+        clean = NOT_BUILT_RE.sub("", text).strip().casefold()
+        checked, not_built = states.get(clean, (False, False))
+        if not checked and not not_built:
+            missing.append(text)
+    return missing
+

+def not_built_criteria(ticket_body: str, pull_body: str) -> List[str]:
+    """Ticket criteria explicitly marked not built with a reason in a PR."""
+    ticket = [item.partition(" ")[2] for item in acceptance_criteria(ticket_body)]
+    marked = {NOT_BUILT_RE.sub("", item.partition(" ")[2]).strip().casefold()
+              for item in acceptance_criteria(pull_body)
+              if NOT_BUILT_RE.search(item.partition(" ")[2])}
+    return [item for item in ticket
+            if not item.strip().casefold().startswith("live:")
+            and item.strip().casefold() in marked]

## Intent
Class: logic
- Public lane runs scan changed diffs and generated PR bodies before pushing, while <redacted> repository runs skip the leak scan.
- Public lane PR bodies put cross-repository issue references in words, and lane instructions direct test addresses to documentation ranges.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
Lane pull requests on public repos carry <redacted> identifiers, the leak-scan check blocks them, and each one costs at least one fix round. On 2026-10-20 three of the eight open pull requests idle for six hours or more were blocked this way, on three different lanes:
- link-bonder ISSUE-300 (lane claude): <redacted>-range IP addresses in the diff, five lines;
- link-bonder ISSUE-313 (lane <redacted>): a <redacted>-range IP address in the diff;
- link-bonder ISSUE-314 (lane codex): a cross-repo issue reference to the <redacted> infrastructure repo in the body.
- link-bonder ISSUE-312: CGNAT range bounds and test addresses in the diff, and <redacted>-repo references copied from the source ticket into the body (reported on ISSUE-1026).
No lane scans its own diff before pushing, so the first check of the rule is CI, after the pull request exists. The factory repairs a body-only hit (`body_leak_hits`, `repair_leak_text`), but only when the leak scan is the sole failing check. A diff hit always goes to a fix round.

## Summary
- Before a lane pushes to a public repo, the runner runs shared-workflows's scanner (`.github/scripts/check_<redacted>_leaks.py`, the one `_reusable.leak-scan.yml` runs) on the diff against the base. It uses the shape rules only; the deny-list stays in SSM, outside the lane.
- A hit fails validation like a failing check: the agent sees the scanner's lines and gets one more attempt, and nothing is pushed while hits remain.
- The PR body the runner writes is scanned the same way, and a cross-repo issue reference is put in words before it is posted (reuse `refs_in_words`).
- The lane instructions for a public repo say to use the documentation ranges (192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24) for test addresses, and to mark a deliberate range bound with `leak-guard-allow` on its line.
- <redacted> repos are not scanned.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test: a lane diff in a public repo that adds a <redacted>-range IP address fails validation with the scanner's hit line and pushes nothing; it fails on main.
- [ ] A test: the same diff in a <redacted> repo validates and pushes.
- [ ] Live: no new lane pull request on a public repo fails leak-scan in the 7 days after the change deploys (GitHub check runs named "leak-scan").
Size: M

Size: M

## Out of scope
- The deny-list terms; CI keeps catching those.
- Changes to the scanner or to `_reusable.leak-scan.yml`.
Part of ISSUE-705

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- Make `_pending_brain_fix` (or the claim scan it uses) find claim lines
- embedded in the ticket's status comment, not only whole-comment bodies.
- Keep the 2026-10-15 protection: a brain-fix ask newer than the last real
- claim still blocks the merge; only the *detection* of the claim changes.
Files: 1 sensitive, 1 tests

## Why
Three READY sensitive pull requests the brain reviewed criterion-by-criterion
(ISSUE-1117 for ticket ISSUE-1106, ISSUE-1202 for ticket ISSUE-1145,
ISSUE-1130 for ticket ISSUE-977) cannot merge: `bus.brain merge` refuses
each with "a brain fix is pending on the ticket; merge after it runs", and
the guard never clears tick after tick. The station's own watch filed
ISSUE-1203 on the repeated `Step merge: degraded` line.
Root cause, read in bus/brain.py this tick: `_pending_brain_fix` finds the
last claim with `_CLAIM.fullmatch(body.strip())`, which only matches when a
whole comment body is exactly `Claimed for lane <lane> (body sha256 <12>)`.
But the station writes claims as bullet lines *inside* the ticket's
`<!-- loom:status v1 -->` comment (for example on ISSUE-1145:
`- 2026-10-20T18:10:14Z Claimed for lane codex (body sha256 7b0568360b2b)`),
so `fullmatch` never fires, `last_claim` stays -1 forever, and any
`<!-- loom:brain-fix v1 -->` comment pins the guard permanently. Verified:
all three tickets show a brain-fix comment with no matching claim, while
their status comments do contain claim lines.
Noticed in this tick's work on ISSUE-30: "merge refused on three
READY PRs; guard root-caused to _CLAIM.fullmatch vs embedded claim lines."

## Summary
Make `_pending_brain_fix` (or the claim scan it uses) find claim lines
embedded in the ticket's status comment, not only whole-comment bodies.
Keep the 2026-10-15 protection: a brain-fix ask newer than the last real
claim still blocks the merge; only the *detection* of the claim changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A ticket whose status comment holds a claim line newer than its
      latest `loom:brain-fix` comment no longer reads "pending brain fix"
      in `bus.brain status`, and `bus.brain merge` proceeds past the guard
      for its pull request.
- [ ] A ticket whose latest `loom:brain-fix` comment is newer than its last
      claim line still refuses the merge with the same error as today.
- [ ] A regression test covers both directions: embedded claim newer than
      the fix ask clears; fix ask newer than the claim blocks.
- [ ] ISSUE-1117, ISSUE-1202 and ISSUE-1130 (or their tickets) show the
      guard cleared on the next `status` read after this ships, with no
      hand edits to their comments.

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Changing what the station writes into the status comment.
- Any other merge-validation rule.
Part of ISSUE-1034

## Intent
Class: logic
- A run that exits 124 after editing commits its edits and pushes them to a <branch>-timedout-<epoch> side branch, and the failure reason names it.
- The station's retry brief carries an "Earlier attempt" section telling the next attempt to start from that branch.
- ## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A run that edits and then exits 124 pushes its edits to a side branch and names it in the parked reason.
- [x] The next attempt's brief names that branch as its starting point.
- [x] A test that fails without the change covers both.
Files: 3 logic, 2 tests, 1 docs

## Why
Spark lanes timed out (exit 124) 8 times in the 24 hours to 2026-10-20 06:00 ET, and 40 times since 2026-10-14. The run classes a timeout as transient and re-briefs the ticket to another lane, which starts from the base again. The agent's edits are discarded. One run (another repo's ticket 1237 on spark-4) edited for 68 minutes before the timeout, and all of that work was lost. The runner already keeps a validation failure's edits on a `-unvalidated-` branch (`preserve_unvalidated` in `lanes/run_lane.sh`), but a timeout gets nothing.

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- pin_one now returns without writing only when the pin names the target revision and there is no open pull request or its mergeable_state is clean; a dirty open pull request triggers a rebuild instead of an early return.
- On every pin update, pin_one force-resets (or creates) the pin branch to the default branch's head before writing, and computes the pin file from the default branch's text rather than the branch's.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
The station's dashboard pin pull request goes dirty whenever the deployment repo's default branch moves after the pin branch was cut, and `status` still lists it READY. `pin_one` in bus/pin.py cuts `loom/pin-<sha12>` from the default branch only when the branch does not exist; every later update PUTs the new pin file onto the old branch, and it returns early when the branch already names the target revision. So after a hand pin or any other merge touches the pin file, the pull request conflicts forever and the dashboard stops deploying until a brain rebuilds the branch by hand.
The brain rebuilt it by hand three times: 2026-10-19 02:39Z, 2026-10-19 21:18Z and 2026-10-21 21:55Z (the last pin pull request, for 9b9d41aded4e, was dirty for 2.3 hours with checks and review green).

## Summary
- On every pin update, rebuild the pin branch from the default branch's head: force the branch ref to the default branch's head (or create it there), then write the pin file computed from the default branch's text, not the branch's.
- When the branch already names the target revision but its pull request is not mergeable (`mergeable_state` dirty), rebuild it the same way instead of returning.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With an existing pin branch whose base is behind the default branch, `pin_one` moves the branch to the default branch's head before writing the pin file (unit test with a fake GitHub asserting the ref PATCH with force and the PUT on the rebuilt branch).
- [ ] With the branch already at the target revision and its open pull request dirty, `pin_one` rebuilds the branch instead of returning (unit test).
- [ ] With the branch at the target revision and its pull request clean, `pin_one` still returns without writing (unit test).
Live: after the next deploy, the next dashboard pin pull request opened after a hand pin shows `mergeable_state` clean within one station pass, read from the REST pull request.
Size: S
One function in bus/pin.py and its tests.

Size: S

## Out of scope
- The READY verdict ignoring mergeability in `status` (a separate deferred brief).
- Closing a pin pull request whose revision main already contains.
Part of ISSUE-1299

criteria.text: With an existing pin branch whose base is behind the default branch, `pin_one` moves the branch to the default branch's head before writing the pin file (unit test with a fake GitHub asserting the ref PATCH with force and the PUT on the rebuilt branch).
With the branch already at the target revision and its open pull request dirty, `pin_one` rebuilds the branch instead of returning (unit test).
With the branch at the target revision and its pull request clean, `pin_one` still returns without writing (unit test).

## Intent
Class: logic
- A proof whose evidence source starts after the Live window's end closes the shipped ticket, with both times in the close comment.
- A Live window still open, or one the evidence source covers, keeps the ticket open as today.
- ## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A proof whose evidence source starts after the Live window's end closes the shipped ticket, with both times in the close comment.
- [x] A Live window still open, or one the evidence source covers, keeps the ticket open as today.
- [x] A test that fails without the change covers both.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
A shipped ticket whose Live line names a time window stays open for good when that window ended before the evidence source's earliest record. The verify run reads the logs, finds nothing from the window because the archive starts later, and the ticket waits on `loom:awaiting-evidence` forever. On 2026-10-20 the second operator's session proved 13 shipped tickets in another repo and found 4 in this state. The operator ruled on 2026-10-20 that such tickets close under the close rule: merged on green checks and shipped, with a Live proof required only where evidence can still find it.

## Summary


## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A proof whose evidence source starts after the Live window's end closes the shipped ticket, with both times in the close comment.
- [x] A Live window still open, or one the evidence source covers, keeps the ticket open as today.
- [x] A test that fails without the change covers both.
Size: M

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Live criteria tied to events that have not happened since ship.
- Changing how long logs are archived.
Part of ISSUE-705.

+def _evidence_log_path(repo: str, command: str, log_root: str) -> Optional[str]:
+    """Get the log file path for a repo and evidence command, or None.
+
+    Only a path that resolves inside the configured log root is returned, so
+    an evidence command cannot read a log outside it. A command that is not a
+    file path (an absolute path or a name ending in ".log") returns None.
+    """
+    if not (os.path.isabs(command) or command.endswith(".log")):
+        return None
+    root = os.path.realpath(log_root)
+    path = os.path.realpath(command)
+    if not path.startswith(root + os.sep):
+        return None
+    return path
+
+
+def _earliest_evidence_record(evidence_cmds: Dict[str, str], repo: str,
+                              log_root: str) -> Optional[datetime]:
+    """Get the earliest record from the evidence source for the given repo, or None.
+    
+    This reads the log file's modification time as a proxy for when the log
+    started being written. If the command is not configured for this repo or
+    the log file does not exist, return None; any other filesystem error
+    (a permission or directory problem) is raised. The log path must live inside
+    the configured log root.
+    """
+    command = evidence_cmds.get(repo)
+    if not command:
+        return None
+    log_path = _evidence_log_path(repo, command, log_root)
+    if not log_path:
+        return None
+    try:
+        mtime = os.path.getmtime(log_path)
+        return datetime.fromtimestamp(mtime, tz=timezone.utc)
+    except (FileNotFoundError, NotADirectoryError):
+        return None
+
+
+def _live_time_window(live: str) -> Optional[Tuple[Optional[datetime], Optional[datetime]]]:
+    """Extract the time window from a Live criterion, or None when none exists.
+    
+    Returns (window_start, window_end) as datetime objects (either may be None),
+    or None when the criterion has no time window (e.g., "Live: prints `foo`").
+    """
+    after_pattern = re.compile(r"on\s+or\s+after\s+(\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d)", re.I)
+    before_pattern = re.compile(r"before\s+(\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d)", re.I)
+    
+    after_match = after_pattern.search(live)
+    before_match = before_pattern.search(live)
+    
+    if not after_match and not before_match:
+        return None
+    
+    try:
+        window_start = (datetime.fromisoformat(after_match.group(1)).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+                        if after_match else None)
+        window_end = (datetime.fromisoformat(before_match.group(1)).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+                      if before_match else None)
+        return window_start, window_end
+    except ValueError:
+        return None

## Intent
Class: logic
- Agent sandbox denies file reads beneath agy's keychain directory while retaining the existing denial of keychain service access and /usr/bin/security execution.
- Agent internet egress remains restricted by port only; hostname-specific endpoint egress is not built because the required local proxy or resolved-address allowlist is not implemented.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
The shared lane sandbox profile (`lanes/agent_sandbox.sh`, `sandbox_profile`) starts from `(allow default)` and denies only localhost and unix-socket egress. Any shell command an agent runs can reach the internet. That holds for every API lane (the opencode family, agy), and the lane's provider key or token is reachable from that shell: an environment variable for the opencode lanes, the keychain through `/usr/bin/security` for agy. A command steered by text in a ticket or repo file could send either out. ISSUE-801 turned agy's own terminal sandbox off to stop the denials behind about 27% of its failures, so agy is now in the same position as the other API lanes.

## Summary
Make the outer profile the real boundary for every lane:
- Deny outbound network by default for the agent's child processes, and allow only what the lane needs: its model endpoint and, where the brief needs one, the package index. sandbox-exec filters by address and port, not hostname, so this may need a local egress proxy that the profile allows by port.
- Deny keychain reads and `process-exec` of `/usr/bin/security` for child processes, with agy's own token read moved outside the sandbox or passed in by the runner.
- Keep agy's inner terminal sandbox off only once this is live. Until then, lanes keep today's parity.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A shell command run by an agent under the lane profile cannot open a connection to an arbitrary internet host (a test under sandbox-exec proves it); not built: outbound port 443 remains allowed for every host.
- [x] A shell command under the profile cannot read a keychain item or run /usr/bin/security.
- [ ] Live: agy and the opencode lanes still complete runs against their model endpoints after the change.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Teaching agy's inner sandbox individual commands (an alternative if the egress proxy proves impractical).
- Codex, which already runs with no network.
Refs ISSUE-801

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Parse explicit metric, log, and endpoint claims from a PR's acceptance criteria.
- Retry absent claims after a delay and require a live same-source baseline before reporting missing.
- Report the criterion, per-attempt target and baseline counts, and an unverifiable verdict when evidence is insufficient.
- Provide a post-deploy CLI that reads a PR body and queries caller-supplied observation sources within the deploy window.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
A pod running the new image proves the image changed. It does not prove the change does anything.
On a real fix, the pod came back Ready on the correct digest with the new code present in the container. Every one of those checks passed while saying nothing about whether the behaviour worked. Only an end-to-end test and the metric the PR itself promised settled it.
Most PRs already state what success looks like, in their own acceptance criteria. Shepherd should hold them to it.

## Summary
Where a PR's acceptance criteria name an observable - a metric, a log event, an endpoint response - check it after deploy and report whether it appeared.
The hard part is not the lookup. It is not lying when the lookup is empty.
A first query for a genuinely-working metric returned zero datapoints, purely from ingestion lag. Reporting at that moment would have declared a working fix broken. The check must distinguish "absent" from "not yet ingested" by comparing against a known-live signal from the same source, and re-check before concluding.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Parses observables out of the PR's own acceptance criteria; absent any, says so rather than inventing one
- [x] Never reports "missing" from a single empty query
- [x] Distinguishes absent from not-yet-ingested using a known-live signal from the same source
- [x] Reports the evidence, so a wrong verdict is arguable

Size: L

## Out of scope
- Inferring intent for PRs that state no observable. Silence is reported as unverifiable, never as verified.
- Writing the tests. Shepherd checks claims already made; it does not author them.
Size: L
Part of ISSUE-828
Part of ISSUE-1311

--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -117,6 +117,36 @@ and 2 on a usage error. When `which epic` fails it lists the repo's open
 `Epic: ...` issues and the two fixes: add the ticket as a sub-issue of an
 epic, or write `Part of #<epic>` in the ticket's body.
 
+### Verify stated claims after a deploy
+
+`scripts/shepherd_verify.py` reads the PR's `## Acceptance criteria` bullets
+and checks explicitly named `Metric`, `Log event`, `Endpoint`, or `GET`
+signals. Names may be in backticks, and metric names or URLs may be plain
+text. It does not infer a signal from prose elsewhere in the PR. The caller
+runs it after deploy completion and supplies source-specific query commands
+and known-live baselines:
+
+```bash
+python3 scripts/shepherd_verify.py --pr 123 --repo example-org/example-repo \
+  --since-epoch "$DEPLOY_FINISHED_UNIX" \
+  --query-command /path/to/your-query-adapter \
+  --baseline metric=your.known_live.metric
+```
+
+The adapter receives `source signal start_epoch end_epoch criterion` as
+arguments and prints one nonnegative integer count. It must query the named
+source over that window, including both the target and its baseline from the
+same source. For an endpoint, it must count only responses matching the
+criterion's expected status or body. A nonzero exit or invalid count makes
+the result unverifiable.
+Supply a baseline for each source used by the PR. The baseline must be known
+to emit during the post-deploy window; a historical signal is not enough.
+The default is two checks 30 seconds apart. An absent target is `missing`

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Health-linked reviews now include quoted finding evidence and instruct the reviewer to flag symptom-only changes at high severity while recognizing changes that improve affected outcomes.
Files: 3 logic, 2 tests

## Why
The review check passed a pull request that silenced a problem instead of fixing it. On 2026-10-15, example/game-orchestrator PR 1029 answered a ticket filed from a live health finding ("the guild bank holds under a gold" while 65 members wait on refunds). It kept one gold back from refunds, so the bank could never cross the finding's threshold. The finding would stop while the members it counts got less. The review check reported "Elder clear - no markings", and the factory merged it; it was reverted (PR 1031) before it shipped. The new criteria coverage (ISSUE-1179) catches diffs that cannot change runtime behavior, but this one does change behavior, in the wrong direction.

## Summary
- When a linked ticket carries the health intake's marker (`<!-- loom:health key=` in its body) or its title starts with "Health:", the reviewer gets the finding's quoted evidence as context. It is asked whether the change improves the outcome for the affected, or only changes the measured symptom: a threshold, a reserve held back, an exclusion from the count, or a changed measure.
- A change that only moves the symptom is a high `symptom-only` finding naming the line that suppresses it.
- The rule is stated in the reviewer's own instructions, generic to any project that serves health findings.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test with a fixture shaped like PR 1029 (a reserve constant subtracted from the amount paid out, linked to a health ticket) produces a high symptom-only finding, and fails on main
- [ ] A test with a fix that raises what reaches the affected (more income routed to the store) produces no symptom-only finding
- [ ] Live: the next pull request linked to a health ticket gets the check, with its verdict in the review summary

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Tickets not filed from health findings
- How findings gate merges

## Intent
Class: logic
- Shadow traffic path for deep-tier only after replay harness baseline
- Pin image digests; document SM/FlashInfer/runtime flags in RUNBOOK
- Eval gate via elder_eval / ledger before cutover
- Ollama remains installed as rollback
Files: 6 logic, 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
Multi-model advice recommends continuous batching (e.g. vLLM) for long-prefill reviews and optionally a premier deep model. A prior cold large-model load path timed out production reviews so any serving change must keep the deep arm always-hot and provide one-config rollback to the current reasoner.

## Summary
- Shadow traffic path for deep-tier only after replay harness baseline
- Pin image digests; document SM/FlashInfer/runtime flags in RUNBOOK
- Eval gate via elder_eval / ledger before cutover
- Ollama remains installed as rollback

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Shadow mode does not serve production findings until eval gate passes
- [ ] Always-hot residency proven; no cold-load on review path
- [ ] Rollback to current reasoner is one config change
- [ ] Public docs avoid internal hostnames; ops notes live where appropriate

Size: L

## Out of scope
- Day-1 production model swap without eval
- TRT-LLM / NIM first
Rewritten from issue 649.

@@ -673,7 +673,113 @@ and production Elder traffic under `ml_app:grug-elder`.

 at that server with the same model id and re-running; keep the fixture
 set identical. Decision rule for ISSUE-649: only cut over if p95 complete at
-C=4/8 improves without a parse-fail regression.
+C=4/8 improves without a parse-fail regression. That cutover now goes
+through the optional vLLM deep arm below (ISSUE-1191).
+
+### Optional vLLM deep arm: shadow, eval gate, serve (ISSUE-1191)
+
+The deep (reasoner) pass can use a dedicated vLLM server. One env var,
+`GRUG_DEEP_ARM_MODE`, set the same on `grug-webhook` and `grug-consumer`,
+controls it (a test keeps the two equal):
+
+| Mode | What publishes | What the vLLM arm does |
+|---|---|---|
+| `off` (default) | the deep pass as before | nothing |
+| `shadow` | the deep pass as before | replays the same prompt on one background worker; logs `deep_shadow_compared` only |
+| `serve` | the vLLM arm, in place of the Cave reasoner call | answers; when it is not resident or fails, the Cave reasoner answers (`deep_vllm_failed_falling_back`) |
+
+`GRUG_DEEP_SHADOW_URL` is the server's base URL (no `/v1` suffix) and
+`GRUG_DEEP_SHADOW_MODEL` the id it serves (`--served-model-name`). Point
+the URL at vLLM itself, never at the <redacted>: a gateway can fail
+over to a cold Ollama load, which is the failure this arm must not repeat.
+The real host and model belong in the operator's <redacted> ops notes and
+the deployment's env, not in this file.
+
+**Order of work.** Each step needs the one before it.
+
+1. Latency baseline. Run the review latency harness above against the
+   current reasoner and the vLLM server with the same fixtures, and keep
+   the result. Shadow traffic starts only after this.
+2. Shadow. Set `GRUG_DEEP_ARM_MODE=shadow` plus the URL and model. Read
+   `deep_shadow_compared` (production vs shadow counts, `overlap`,
+   `shadow_latency_ms`, `shadow_kind`). `deep_shadow_skipped_busy` means a
+   review finished while the previous shadow call was still running; that
+   review is not shadowed, by design, so a slow host never builds a queue.
+3. Eval gate. Record the candidate as its own baseline entry, then commit
+   the refreshed `baseline.json`:
+
+   ```bash
+   export GRUG_BENCH_DEEP_SHADOW_URL='https://<your-vllm-host>/v1/chat/completions'
+   export GRUG_BENCH_DEEP_SHADOW_MODEL='<served-model-name>'
+   make elder-eval ARGS="--backend deep-shadow --record"
+   ```
+
+   `elder_eval.gate.deep_cutover_regressions` passes only when the
+   `deep-shadow` entry measured that exact model, scored at least as many
+   cases as the `cave` entry with none errored, and is no worse on overall
+   catch or noise. Both entries come from the same bench mode.
+4. Serve. Set `GRUG_DEEP_ARM_MODE=serve` in `k8s/*-deployment.yaml`. CI
+   (`test_a_committed_serve_mode_has_passed_the_eval_gate`) refuses the
+   change until step 3 passes for the model in `GRUG_DEEP_SHADOW_MODEL`. A
+   live `kubectl set env` skips that check, so do not cut over that way.
+
+**Always hot.** Before every call the arm reads `GET <url>/v1/models`
+(cached 60s) and goes ahead only when the configured id is listed with
+`owned_by: "vllm"`. vLLM loads its one model when the process starts, so a
+listed model is resident. An Ollama-style front lists models it would load
+on demand and is refused (`deep_vllm_not_resident`). To check by hand:
+
+```bash
+curl -s <url>/v1/models | jq '.data[] | {id, owned_by}'
+```
+
+A fresh `deep_vllm_not_resident` or `deep_vllm_probe_failed` in the pod
+logs means the arm is being skipped, not cold-loaded. Look at the server.
+
+**Running the server.** Pin the image by digest, never by tag, and record
+the digest in the <redacted> ops notes next to the host:
+
+```bash
+docker run -d --restart unless-stopped --gpus all --ipc host -p 8000:8000 \
+  -e TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST='<sm of the GPU, e.g. 12.1 for GB10, 9.0 for H100>' \
+  -e VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASHINFER \
+  -v <model-cache>:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+  vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:<digest> \
+  --model <hf-model-id> --served-model-name <served-model-name> \
+  --max-model-len <fits the largest cohort prompt> \
+  --gpu-memory-utilization <0.85-0.92; leave room for the KV cache> \
+  --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill
+```
+
+- `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST`: the GPU's SM version, used for kernels that
+  are compiled when the server starts. Check that the image's release
+  notes cover that SM before you pin its digest. A digest that does not
+  cover it can fail at load or run slow fallback kernels.
+- `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASHINFER`: FlashInfer attention, set
+  explicitly so an image bump that changes vLLM's default backend shows up
+  as a diff in the ops notes, not as a quiet change in latency. If the
+  image cannot run it on that SM, expect a startup failure. That is the
+  failure you want, because it shows before any review reaches the arm.
+- `--enable-prefix-caching` and `--enable-chunked-prefill`: Elder prompts
+  share a long system prefix, and cohorts are long prefills. These two
+  flags are the continuous-batching gain this arm exists to measure.
+- `--restart unless-stopped`, no idle timeout, no scale-to-zero: the model
+  must stay loaded. Anything that unloads it on idle breaks the always-hot
+  rule, and the probe above will then skip the arm.
+- No `--api-key` is assumed. If the server is reachable from outside the
+  cluster network, put it behind a network policy instead.
+
+**Rollback** is one change from either mode:
+
+```bash
+<redacted>grug set env deploy/grug-webhook deploy/grug-consumer GRUG_DEEP_ARM_MODE=off
+```
+
+Then commit `GRUG_DEEP_ARM_MODE: "off"` in both manifests so the next
+deploy does not undo it. The current reasoner (<redacted>,
+`<redacted>`) is never removed by this arm, so `off` always
+has something to go back to. Leave the existing Ollama install on its
+host as the gateway's rollback target. Nothing here uninstalls it.

@@ -0,0 +1,152 @@
+"""Optional vLLM deep arm: shadow it, then serve it, with one-switch rollback (ISSUE-1191).
+
+`GRUG_DEEP_ARM_MODE` decides what the deep (reasoner) pass does with a
+dedicated vLLM server named by `GRUG_DEEP_SHADOW_URL` (its base URL) and
+`GRUG_DEEP_SHADOW_MODEL` (the model id it serves):
+
+- `off`, the default: the deep pass runs exactly as it did before this module.
+- `shadow`: the deep pass still answers and is the only thing published. The
+  same prompt is replayed against the vLLM arm on one background worker, and
+  only a comparison is logged (`deep_shadow_compared`). Shadow findings never
+  reach a PR.
+- `serve`: the vLLM arm replaces the Cave reasoner call. When it is not
+  resident or fails, the Cave reasoner answers as before. A committed manifest
+  in this mode fails CI until the elder_eval baseline holds a passing
+  `deep-shadow` entry for the same model (`elder_eval.gate`).
+
+Rollback from either mode is one change: `GRUG_DEEP_ARM_MODE=off`.
+
+Always-hot: the arm is only called when the server's `/v1/models` lists the
+configured model as owned by vLLM. vLLM loads its one model at process start,
+so a listed model is resident. An Ollama-style front lists every model it
+could load on demand, and calling one of those is the cold load (an ~87GB
+read per review) that once timed out every production review; it is refused.
+The probe result is cached for `_RESIDENCY_TTL_S`, so a review pays at most
+one short GET per window.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import os
+import threading
+import time
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from concurrent.futures import Future, ThreadPoolExecutor
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Literal, get_args
+
+import httpx
+
+log = logging.getLogger("grug.deep_shadow")
+
+DeepArmMode = Literal["off", "shadow", "serve"]
+_MODES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(get_args(DeepArmMode))
+
+_RESIDENCY_TTL_S = 60.0
+_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S = 2.0
+
+# One worker, and a slot that is taken before submit: a shadow call that is
+# still running when the next review finishes means that review is not
+# shadowed, rather than a queue that grows behind a slow GPU host.
+_POOL = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1, thread_name_prefix="deep-shadow")
+_busy = threading.BoundedSemaphore(1)
+
+# (base_url, model) -> (resident, monotonic time checked)
+_residency_cache: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[bool, float]] = {}
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class DeepArm:
+    """A resolved, non-off deep arm: which mode, and where the vLLM server is."""
+
+    mode: Literal["shadow", "serve"]
+    base_url: str
+    model: str
+
+
+def resolve_deep_arm() -> DeepArm | None:
+    """The configured deep arm, or None for `off`.
+
+    An unknown mode, or a mode whose URL or model is unset, resolves to None
+    and is logged: a typo must fall back to the current reasoner, never to an
+    arm nobody has evaluated."""
+    raw = os.getenv("GRUG_DEEP_ARM_MODE", "off").strip().lower() or "off"
+    if raw not in _MODES:
+        log.warning("deep_arm_mode_unknown", extra={"mode": raw})
+        return None
+    if raw == "off":
+        return None
+    base_url = os.getenv("GRUG_DEEP_SHADOW_URL", "").strip().rstrip("/")
+    model = os.getenv("GRUG_DEEP_SHADOW_MODEL", "").strip()
+    if not base_url or not model:
+        log.error(
+            "deep_arm_unconfigured",
+            extra={"mode": raw, "has_url": bool(base_url), "has_model": bool(model)},
+        )
+        return None
+    return DeepArm(mode=raw, base_url=base_url, model=model)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+
+
+def _probe(arm: DeepArm) -> bool:
+    """True when the server's /v1/models lists `arm.model` as owned by vLLM."""
+    try:
+        resp = httpx.get(f"{arm.base_url}/v1/models", timeout=_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S)
+        resp.raise_for_status()
+        served = resp.json().get("data", [])
+    except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError) as e:
+        log.warning(
+            "deep_vllm_probe_failed",
+            extra={"model": arm.model, "error_type": type(e).__name__, "error": str(e)[:200]},
+        )
+        return False
+    return any(
+        m.get("id") == arm.model and m.get("owned_by") == "vllm"
+        for m in served
+        if isinstance(m, dict)
+    )
+
+
+def is_resident(arm: DeepArm) -> bool:
+    """Whether `arm.model` is loaded and served by vLLM right now (cached)."""
+    key = (arm.base_url, arm.model)
+    now = time.monotonic()
+    cached = _residency_cache.get(key)
+    if cached is not None and now - cached[1] < _RESIDENCY_TTL_S:
+        return cached[0]
+    resident = _probe(arm)
+    _residency_cache[key] = (resident, now)
+    if not resident:
+        log.warning("deep_vllm_not_resident", extra={"model": arm.model, "mode": arm.mode})
+    return resident
+
+
+def submit(job: Callable[[], None]) -> Future | None:
+    """Run `job` on the shadow worker, or skip it (None) when the worker is busy.
+
+    A job that raises is logged as `deep_shadow_failed`; the exception also
+    stays on the returned future."""
+    if not _busy.acquire(blocking=False):
+        log.info("deep_shadow_skipped_busy")
+        return None
+
+    def run() -> None:
+        try:
+            job()
+        except Exception:
+            log.exception("deep_shadow_failed")
+            raise
+        finally:
+            _busy.release()
+
+    try:
+        return _POOL.submit(run)
+    except RuntimeError:
+        # The pool is shut down (interpreter exit); nothing will run the job.
+        _busy.release()
+        log.exception("deep_shadow_failed")
+        return None
+
+

## Intent
Class: logic
- In the intent check's prompt, a criterion that forbids something ("no X", "never X", "X is not written", "stops X") is met when the diff removes or prevents X. The finding must quote the criterion and the PR sentence it claims contradicts it, and must name the diff hunk that does the opposite of the
- A post-filter drops an `intent-mismatch` finding that does not quote both texts, and lowers one to medium when the quoted PR sentence and the criterion share the same negation (both say "no" or "never" about the same thing).
- Tests with recorded inputs: the negated-criterion case above is not raised; a PR that adds the forbidden thing is still raised high.
Files: 3 logic, 2 tests

## Why
The intent check added by ISSUE-1165 raised a high `intent-mismatch` on a lane PR on 2026-10-14 that met its issue exactly. The issue's first criterion was phrased as a negative ("no guild job writes a leave row for a cohort whose queue did not pop; the leave counter ignores a refused leave"), the PR removed that row and narrowed the counter, and the review read the PR's "stop writing" and "no ... row" as the PR refusing to do the work. A high finding blocks the merge, so a correct fix to a held deploy waited on a person. Refs ISSUE-1143.

## Summary
- In the intent check's prompt, a criterion that forbids something ("no X", "never X", "X is not written", "stops X") is met when the diff removes or prevents X. The finding must quote the criterion and the PR sentence it claims contradicts it, and must name the diff hunk that does the opposite of the criterion.
- A post-filter drops an `intent-mismatch` finding that does not quote both texts, and lowers one to medium when the quoted PR sentence and the criterion share the same negation (both say "no" or "never" about the same thing).
- Tests with recorded inputs: the negated-criterion case above is not raised; a PR that adds the forbidden thing is still raised high.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tests: a negated criterion met by a removal raises no intent-mismatch; a PR that adds what the criterion forbids is still high; a finding without both quotes is dropped. Each fails without the change.
- [ ] The prompt text for negated criteria is present in the Elder header, checked by a test.
- [ ] Live: over the next 20 lane PRs with linked criteria, no intent-mismatch is raised on a PR whose diff does what its criterion says (spot-checked by the brain in its journal).

Size: M

## Out of scope
Other finding kinds; the Intent paragraph itself.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/services/_shared/personas/code_reviewer/intent_filter.py
@@ -0,0 +1,129 @@
+"""Deterministic post-filter for intent-mismatch findings (ISSUE-1170).
+
+The Elder prompt teaches that a negated acceptance criterion ("no X",
+"never X", ...) is MET when the diff removes or prevents the forbidden
+thing, and that every intent-mismatch finding must quote both the
+criterion and the PR sentence it claims contradicts it. This module is
+the deterministic backstop for when the model still raises: it runs on
+the LLM findings right after ``evaluate_diff`` (see the inline
+``filter_intent_mismatch_findings`` call in
+``dispatch_code_review`` in ``dispatch.py``), before the judge gate.
+
+Pure: findings in, findings out. No IO. Fail-open: an unexpected shape
+keeps the finding rather than dropping it.
+
+Rules, in order:
+1. A finding that does not quote BOTH texts (criterion + PR sentence) is
+   dropped - it carries no checkable evidence.
+2. A finding whose two quotes share the SAME negation (both say "no" or
+   "never" about the same thing) is lowered to medium: advisory, never
+   merge-blocking. This is the recorded ISSUE-1170 shape.
+3. Everything else (including a PR that ADDS the forbidden thing) passes
+   through untouched.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import dataclasses
+import re
+from collections.abc import Iterable
+
+from personas.code_reviewer.persona import Finding
+
+_INTENT_MISMATCH = "intent-mismatch"
+
+# A quote is a double-quoted span long enough to carry a real sentence,
+# not a lone identifier the model quoted for emphasis. 12 is the tuned
+# floor: shorter spans ("id", "row") are emphasis, not evidence.
+_QUOTED_SPAN_RE = re.compile(r'"([^"\n]{12,})"')
+
+# Negation vocabulary shared by criteria ("no X") and PR summaries
+# ("stop writing X"). Includes removal verbs: a PR that deletes the
+# forbidden code is describing the same prohibition, not defying it.
+_NEGATION_RE = re.compile(
+    r"\b(?:no|never|not|n't|cannot|can't|won't|without|"
+    r"stops?|stopped|prevents?|prevented|forbids?|forbidden|"
+    r"prohibits?|prohibited|removes?|removed|removal|"
+    r"deletes?|deleted|deletion|drops?|dropped|eliminates?|eliminated|"
+    r"ignores?|ignored)\b",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+
+# Content words for the "about the same thing" check: alphabetic tokens
+# of 5+ letters, minus the filler that would match on any two sentences.
+_STOPWORDS = frozenset({
+    "about", "after", "against", "being", "change", "criterion",
+    "criteria", "could", "demand", "demands", "diff", "does", "doing",
+    "having", "hunk", "issue", "message", "other", "quote", "quoted",
+    "quotes", "say", "says", "sentence", "should", "speaks", "tablet",
+    "these", "thing", "those", "under", "where", "which", "while",
+    "would", "write", "writes",
+})
+
+
+def _quoted_spans(message: str) -> list[str]:
+    """Double-quoted spans of sentence length, in order of appearance."""
+    return [m.group(1).strip() for m in _QUOTED_SPAN_RE.finditer(message or "")]
+
+
+def _content_words(text: str) -> set[str]:
+    return {
+        w for w in re.findall(r"[a-zA-Z]{5,}", text.lower())
+        if w not in _STOPWORDS
+    }
+
+
+def _action_negated(text: str) -> bool:
+    """The quote's main action is negated, forbidden, or removed.
+
+    Only the LEAD of the first clause counts: a "not" buried in a
+    relative clause ("cohorts whose queue did not pop") describes the
+    cohort, not the PR's action, and must not flip the polarity.
+    """
+    clause = re.split(r"[;,]", text, maxsplit=1)[0]
+    lead = " ".join(re.findall(r"[a-zA-Z']+", clause.lower())[:4])
+    return bool(_NEGATION_RE.search(lead))
+
+
+def _shares_negation(first: str, second: str) -> bool:
+    """Both quotes negate (or remove) the same thing.
+
+    Guards the ISSUE-1170 false positive: the criterion says "no leave rows"
+    and the PR summary says "stop writing leave rows" - same negation,
+    same topic, so the finding is a misread, not a real contradiction.
+    A PR whose lead action is AFFIRMATIVE ("writes a leave row") while
+    the criterion forbids it is the true positive and is never lowered.
+    """
+    if not (_action_negated(first) and _action_negated(second)):
+        return False
+    return bool(_content_words(first) & _content_words(second))
+
+
+def filter_intent_mismatch_findings(
+    findings: Iterable[Finding],
+) -> tuple[tuple[Finding, ...], int, int]:
+    """Apply the ISSUE-1170 post-filter.
+
+    Returns (kept, dropped, lowered). Lowered findings are re-emitted at
+    medium severity; dropped findings carry no checkable evidence.
+    Non-intent-mismatch findings pass through untouched.
+    """
+    kept: list[Finding] = []
+    dropped = 0
+    lowered = 0
+    for finding in findings:
+        if finding.rule_name != _INTENT_MISMATCH:
+            kept.append(finding)
+            continue
+        spans = _quoted_spans(finding.message)
+        if len(spans) < 2:
+            # No checkable evidence: the finding does not quote both the
+            # criterion and the PR sentence the prompt requires.
+            dropped += 1
+            continue
+        if _shares_negation(spans[0], spans[1]) and finding.severity == "high":
+            kept.append(dataclasses.replace(finding, severity="medium"))
+            lowered += 1
+            continue
+        kept.append(finding)
+    return tuple(kept), dropped, lowered

@@ -0,0 +1,147 @@
+"""Tests for the intent-mismatch post-filter (ISSUE-1170).
+
+Recorded inputs are the real incident: a negated acceptance criterion
+("no guild job writes a leave row for a cohort whose queue did not pop;
+the leave counter ignores a refused leave") met by a PR that REMOVED the
+row and narrowed the counter, while the Elder read the PR's own "stop
+writing" / "no ... row" summary as refusing the work and raised a high
+intent-mismatch that blocked a correct merge.
+
+The filter holds the line the prompt now teaches:
+- an intent-mismatch finding that does not quote BOTH the criterion and
+  the PR sentence is dropped;
+- one whose two quotes share the same negation (both say "no"/"never"
+  about the same thing) is lowered to medium (advisory, never blocks);
+- a finding where the PR ADDS the forbidden thing stays high.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from personas.code_reviewer.intent_filter import filter_intent_mismatch_findings
+from personas.code_reviewer.persona import Finding
+
+# Recorded from the ISSUE-1170 incident.
+_CRITERION = (
+    "no guild job writes a leave row for a cohort whose queue did not "
+    "pop; the leave counter ignores a refused leave"
+)
+_PR_SUMMARY_NEGATED = (
+    "stop writing leave rows for cohorts whose queue did not pop; the "
+    "leave counter now ignores refused leaves"
+)
+_PR_SUMMARY_ADDING = (
+    "writes a leave row for cohorts whose queue did not pop, to keep an "
+    "audit trail of refusals"
+)
+
+
+def _finding(rule: str, severity: str, message: str) -> Finding:
+    return Finding(
+        file="jobs.py",
+        line=88,
+        severity=severity,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+        rule_name=rule,
+        message=message,
+        suggestion=None,
+    )
+
+
+def _incident_finding(severity: str = "high") -> Finding:
+    """The recorded false positive: both texts quoted, shared negation."""
+    return _finding(
+        "intent-mismatch",
+        severity,
+        f'Grug see tablet demand "{_CRITERION}", yet the change boasts '
+        f'"{_PR_SUMMARY_NEGATED}" - the change refuses the work the tablet '
+        "commands. The hunk at jobs.py:88 deletes the writer. So speaks Grug.",
+    )
+
+
+def test_shared_negation_lowered_to_medium_not_high():
+    """The recorded ISSUE-1170 case: the PR removes the forbidden thing and both
+    the criterion and the PR sentence say "no" about leave rows. Not raised
+    as a blocking high; advisory medium at most."""
+    kept, dropped, lowered = filter_intent_mismatch_findings(
+        (_incident_finding("high"),)
+    )
+    assert dropped == 0
+    assert lowered == 1
+    assert len(kept) == 1
+    assert kept[0].severity == "medium"
+    assert kept[0].rule_name == "intent-mismatch"
+
+
+def test_shared_negation_already_medium_kept():
+    kept, dropped, lowered = filter_intent_mismatch_findings(
+        (_incident_finding("medium"),)
+    )
+    assert dropped == 0
+    assert lowered == 0
+    assert len(kept) == 1
+    assert kept[0].severity == "medium"
+
+
+def test_finding_without_both_quotes_dropped():
+    """An intent-mismatch that quotes nothing (or only one text) carries no
+    checkable evidence - the prompt requires both quotes, so drop it."""
+    no_quotes = _finding(
+        "intent-mismatch",
+        "high",
+        "Grug see change walk away from the tablet's command. The hunk at "
+        "jobs.py:88 deletes the writer the criterion demands. So speaks Grug.",
+    )
+    one_quote = _finding(
+        "intent-mismatch",
+        "high",
+        f'Grug see tablet demand "{_CRITERION}", and the change walks away. '
+        "The hunk at jobs.py:88 deletes the writer. So speaks Grug.",
+    )
+    kept, dropped, lowered = filter_intent_mismatch_findings((no_quotes, one_quote))
+    assert dropped == 2
+    assert lowered == 0
+    assert kept == ()
+
+
+def test_pr_adds_forbidden_thing_stays_high():
+    """The true positive the filter must NOT touch: the criterion forbids
+    the row and the PR's own sentence says it writes one anyway."""
+    finding = _finding(
+        "intent-mismatch",
+        "high",
+        f'Grug see tablet demand "{_CRITERION}", yet the change boasts '
+        f'"{_PR_SUMMARY_ADDING}" - the change writes the very row the tablet '
+        "forbids. The hunk at jobs.py:88 adds the writer. So speaks Grug.",
+    )
+    kept, dropped, lowered = filter_intent_mismatch_findings((finding,))
+    assert dropped == 0
+    assert lowered == 0
+    assert len(kept) == 1
+    assert kept[0].severity == "high"
+
+
+def test_other_rules_untouched():
+    other = _finding(
+        "missing-error-handling",
+        "high",
+        "Grug see net cast with no ward. `db.write(row)` may fail and none "
+        "catch the fall. So speaks Grug.",
+    )
+    kept, dropped, lowered = filter_intent_mismatch_findings((other,))
+    assert (dropped, lowered) == (0, 0)
+    assert kept == (other,)
+
+
+def test_mixed_batch():
+    incident = _incident_finding("high")
+    adding = _finding(
+        "intent-mismatch",
+        "high",
+        f'Grug see tablet demand "{_CRITERION}", yet the change boasts '
+        f'"{_PR_SUMMARY_ADDING}". The hunk at jobs.py:90 adds the writer. '
+        "So speaks Grug.",
+    )
+    kept, dropped, lowered = filter_intent_mismatch_findings((incident, adding))
+    assert dropped == 0
+    assert lowered == 1
+    severities = sorted(f.severity for f in kept)
+    assert severities == ["high", "medium"]
label: GOOD

body:
## Why
After a pull request in another repo merged on 2026-10-13, the Haunt notice said it "was merged with 1 high/critical Elder finding(s) from EARLIER in its review that never got a reply". Every high thread on it had been handled before the merge: two had Elder's own "Fixed in <sha>" reply (the flagged code changed) and were resolved; three had a written reply from the author and were resolved. A notice that counts Elder's own "Fixed in" as no reply sends the operator a false alarm, and teaches them to ignore the real ones. Part of ISSUE-1143.

## Summary
- The Haunt close-time check counts a high/critical finding as handled when its thread is resolved and its newest comment is Elder's own "Fixed in" reply, or any reply from someone other than Elder.
- It still reports a high/critical thread that is unresolved at merge, or resolved with no reply at all.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test with a merged PR whose only high thread has Elder's "Fixed in" reply and is resolved posts no Haunt notice; it fails without the change.
- [ ] A test with a resolved high thread that has an author reply posts no notice; a test with an unresolved high thread, or a resolved one with no reply, still posts it.
- [ ] Live proof: the next merged PR whose high findings were all fixed or answered gets no Haunt notice.

Size: S

## Out of scope
Elder's severities; Living Hunt's incremental scoping; carry-forward of open findings into the check.

body:
## Why
Part of ISSUE-1143. Measured 2026-10-12: the bot's 12 lint threads (7 `lint-security`, 5 `lint-bug`) duplicated CI 0 times, because `lint.py` runs `--select S,B,ASYNC` in a temp folder and never reads the repo's ruff config. Of the 7 `lint-security` threads, all high severity: 2 were real (S310 led to a fix for a redirect that could leak an auth header, loom PR 62), 3 were S102 `exec` in tests that load the repo's own source (settled with `noqa`), 1 was an already-guarded S310, and 1 was a false S608 on SQL joined from string literals and a call with literal arguments, which failed the Elder check on game-orchestrator PR 908. A repo whose own config selects or ignores a rule should never get a thread for it, and constant SQL is not an injection.

## Summary
- `services/_shared/personas/code_reviewer/lint.py`: add `S102` to `_TEST_NOISE_RULES`; in `_map_results`, parse the flagged file's AST, and an S608 whose string parts are all literals, module-level string constants or calls with only literal arguments becomes `medium` (otherwise it stays `high`).
- New pure module `repo_ruff_policy.py`: parse `ruff.toml`, `.ruff.toml` or `pyproject.toml` `[tool.ruff]` text into select/extend-select, ignore/extend-ignore and per-file-ignores. Dispatch reads the first that exists from the PR base ref (as `.grug.yaml` is read) and passes it to the lint scan. A finding is dropped when the repo ignores its code for that path, or explicitly selects it (the repo's own ruff run enforces it). The check summary counts findings dropped this way.
- Tests: `services/webhook/tests/test_lint.py::test_s608_constant_concatenation_is_medium` (fails today), `test_s608_interpolated_parameter_stays_high`, `test_s102_in_test_file_is_dropped`, `test_code_the_repo_ignores_is_dropped`, `test_code_the_repo_selects_is_dropped`, and new `services/webhook/tests/test_repo_ruff_policy.py` (a missing or malformed file means no policy).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `services/webhook/tests/test_lint.py::test_s608_constant_concatenation_is_medium` fails on main and passes with the change; the other new lint and policy tests pass
- [ ] A finding whose code the repo's ruff config ignores for that path, or explicitly selects, gets no thread, and the check summary counts it (test)
- [ ] Live proof (left to the brain): on the next 20 lane PRs no high `lint-security` thread is an S102 in a test file or an S608 over constant strings, and lint-caused Elder check failures are real defects

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Running ruff with the repo's full config as its CI does (only select/ignore are read)
- High-severity model findings that contradict an explicit comment in the diff
- Guard's static-analysis findings

+"""Small, fail-closed parser for the Ruff policy relevant to review findings."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import fnmatch
+import tomllib
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class RepoRuffPolicy:
+    select: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
+    ignore: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
+    per_file_ignores: tuple[tuple[str, frozenset[str]], ...] = ()
+
+    def drops(self, code: str, path: str) -> bool:
+        # A selected code is dropped on purpose (ISSUE-1148), not mistaken for an
+        # ignore: the repo's own ruff run already enforces it and fails CI on
+        # it, so a thread would only duplicate that failure. The drop is still
+        # visible, counted in the check summary.
+        if _matches(code, self.ignore) or _matches(code, self.select):
+            return True
+        return any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(path, pattern) and _matches(code, codes)
+                   for pattern, codes in self.per_file_ignores)
+
+
+def _codes(value: object) -> frozenset[str]:
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        value = [part.strip() for part in value.split(",")]
+    if not isinstance(value, list) or not all(isinstance(x, str) for x in value):
+        raise ValueError("expected rule-code list")
+    return frozenset(value)
+
+
+def _matches(code: str, patterns: frozenset[str]) -> bool:
+    """Ruff selectors are code prefixes ("S" selects S608), plus "ALL". A
+    trailing "*" is accepted as the same prefix. The codes come from a
+    repo-authored file, so a pattern that is empty once its asterisks are
+    stripped ("", "*", "**") is never a match: it cannot widen into "ALL"
+    and drop every finding. Only a literal "ALL" means every code."""
+    return any(pattern == "ALL" or (pattern.rstrip("*") and code.startswith(pattern.rstrip("*")))
+               for pattern in patterns)
+
+
+def parse_repo_ruff_policy(text: str | None) -> RepoRuffPolicy:
+    """Parse TOML policy. Missing, invalid, or unsupported input means no policy."""
+    if not text:
+        return RepoRuffPolicy()
+    try:
+        root = tomllib.loads(text)
+        tool = root.get("tool")
+        ruff = tool.get("ruff", {}) if isinstance(tool, dict) else {}
+        if not isinstance(ruff, dict):
+            return RepoRuffPolicy()
+        lint = ruff.get("lint", {})
+        if not isinstance(lint, dict):
+            lint = {}
+        select = _codes(lint.get("select", ruff.get("select", [])))
+        select |= _codes(lint.get("extend-select", ruff.get("extend-select", [])))
+        ignore = _codes(lint.get("ignore", ruff.get("ignore", [])))
+        ignore |= _codes(lint.get("extend-ignore", ruff.get("extend-ignore", [])))
+        pfi = lint.get("per-file-ignores", ruff.get("per-file-ignores", {}))
+        if not isinstance(pfi, dict):
+            raise ValueError("invalid per-file-ignores")
+        entries = tuple((pattern, _codes(codes)) for pattern, codes in pfi.items()
+                        if isinstance(pattern, str))
+        return RepoRuffPolicy(select, ignore, entries)
+    except (tomllib.TOMLDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):
+        return RepoRuffPolicy()

body:
## Why

Verify had no owner of its own. The station handed a shipped ticket to a verify run only on a lane that was free and had no build work, so a factory with build work for every lane never verified what it shipped, and shipped tickets piled up open with unchecked boxes (the incident in ISSUE-964). This gives verify a durable owner inside the station pass: a shipped ticket that has waited 2 hours is verified ahead of build work, on one free lane, at most every 30 minutes. Idle lanes still verify as before.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A failing-first test shows the old gap: with build work briefed for the only free lane, a shipped ticket gets no verify brief on main (test_a_busy_lane_verifies_the_oldest_shipped_ticket_ahead_of_build_work, test_a_queued_ticket_of_the_slots_tier_does_not_starve_a_shipped_ticket fail on main).
- [x] After the change a shipped ticket is picked up for verification within one station pass, on one reserved lane, no more than once per 30 minutes and never more than one lane per pass (test_only_one_lane_a_pass_is_taken_from_build_work, test_the_lane_is_taken_at_most_once_an_interval, test_the_lane_is_taken_again_after_the_interval); young shipped work (under 2 hours) leaves build work first, and a failed proof audit still holds the lane.
- [x] The close guard (ISSUE-539) is untouched: this change only decides which lane gets a verify brief; nothing in the close or proof paths changed, and the full suite (2969 tests) passes.
- [ ] Live: after deploy, the station log shows "handed ... to lane ... to verify" for shipped tickets older than 2 hours while build briefs are claimed in the same hour, and no open loom:shipped ticket in a scanned repo stays older than 24 hours without a verify attempt or a missing-evidence note.

Size: S

## Out of scope

- Changing what counts as proof for any ticket, or the 6-hour per-ticket cooldown.
- Enlarging the brain tick budget; the brain's verify-due sweep is unchanged.
- The Live criterion restate flow and the refusal cap.

Refs ISSUE-964
Part of ISSUE-703

body:
## Why
A lane in the middle of a long run is treated as silent, and its running ticket is taken away. A lane runner writes its heartbeat between runs, not during one, and a spark run can take over 30 minutes.
- On 2026-10-19 link-bonder ISSUE-283 was running on spark-3. At 14:15Z the factory found spark-3 "silent" past `SILENT_MAX`, removed `lane:spark-3` and re-queued the ticket.
- The run finished at 14:44Z, reported done, and the station moved the ticket to `loom:pr` with no lane label.
- The factory then failed every pass on its pull request (link-bonder ISSUE-312) with "ticket must have exactly one lane label". review-bot ISSUE-1194 and review-bot ISSUE-1296 went the same way.
- The same false silence filed invariants ISSUE-973 and ISSUE-974 ("Lane spark-4 held a running ticket while silent").

## Summary
- `bus/station.py`: `_silent_lanes` skips a lane whose runner holds `run/<lane>.lock` with a live pid. It reuses `_runner_alive`, the liveness check ISSUE-939 added for dead briefs. A lane with no lock, or a lock whose pid is gone, still counts as silent, so a runner that died mid-run still has its ticket moved.
- Test: a lane 40 minutes past its heartbeat is not silent while its lock holds a live pid, and is silent once the pid is dead. It fails on main; the full suite passes (2364).
- The two stranded tickets got `lane:spark-3` back by hand (a label change, no comment).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A lane whose runner holds its lock with a live pid is not reported silent, so its running ticket is not re-queued.
- [x] A lane with a stale heartbeat and no live runner is still reported silent.
- [x] The new test fails without the change and passes with it.

Size: XS

## Out of scope
- Writing heartbeats during a run.
- Restoring a lane label when a re-queued ticket reports done.

---
Loom ticket n/a (operator-session finding from factory errors on two lane pull requests), lane operator-session, model claude-opus-5-5.

body:
## Why
On 2026-10-13 the codex subscription hit its usage limit ("ERROR: You've hit your usage limit ... try again at 12:21 PM"). The runner recorded each run as "agent exited 1": 21 runs on codex and codex-2 became failures, each costing its ticket the codex rung of the model ladder (a failure on a ladder model counts that rung as tried), and the lanes kept advertising themselves as available, so the factory kept sending work there. Only the spark lane treated a provider refusal as a limit.

## Summary
- `provider_limit` in `lanes/run_lane.sh`: after a non-zero exit, read the last 40 lines of this run's own output (from the log offset taken before the run) for a provider limit error: an `ERROR`/`API Error` line naming a usage limit, rate limit, credit balance, quota, too many requests or overload, or the CLIs' "usage limit reached" / "N-hour limit reached". On a match the lane is marked limited for `LIMIT_HOLD` (heartbeat unavailable) and the brief is parked as `limit: ...`, which the station already hands back as not a failure.
- `lane_ready` now honors a recorded limit on every lane, so a limited lane hands its next briefs on without running the agent.
- Checked against every lane log on the machine: the pattern matches exactly the 21 codex limit failures and nothing else.
- Tests: a usage-limit run is parked as a limit, the heartbeat goes unavailable and the next brief is handed on unrun (fails on main); a failure whose brief mentions a rate limit stays an ordinary failure. 440 passed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A run that ends on a provider usage or rate limit is parked as a limit, marks the lane unavailable and hands later briefs on (test)
- [ ] A failure that merely mentions limits in its brief is still a failure (test)
- [ ] Live: the next provider limit on any lane shows "limit: lane ... provider reported a usage or rate limit" on its ticket and no rung is spent

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Reading the provider's reset time to hold exactly that long (LIMIT_HOLD stays 15 minutes).
- Restoring rungs the 21 earlier limit failures spent; done with rung markers after this is live.

Part of ISSUE-30

body:
## Why
A regression from PR 162: when every untried rung was busy, a climb waited on the lowest untried rung. During the restart wave every climb saw busy lanes, so 33 briefed tickets queued on the single claude lane (rung 1), while codex-2, anthropic, anthropic-3, -6, -7 and -8 sat idle. A briefed ticket only moved after a 2-hour stall.

## Summary
- `next_rung`: with no free untried rung, wait on the untried rung whose least-loaded lane holds the least (ties to the lower rung), not always the lowest.
- `Factory._spread`, in the briefed step: a ticket on a ladder model whose lane holds more than `RUNG_BUSY` briefed or running tickets moves to an untried rung with a free lane. It is recorded as "Not a failure"; first briefs (no ladder model) are never moved.
- docs/LANES.md says both.
- Tests: five rung-1 tickets on claude leave two there and move the rest to `gpt-6-sol`; first briefs stay put; `next_rung` picks rung 2 when claude holds 30. The first two fail on main. 429 passed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Ladder tickets queued on a lane past RUNG_BUSY move to a free untried rung (test)
- [ ] With every untried rung busy, the climb waits on the least-loaded one (test)
- [ ] Live: within three factory passes no ladder lane holds more than 2 briefed tickets while another ladder slot is idle

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Routing first briefs to free lanes (the brain's lane choice).
- The 2-hour briefed stall rule.

Part of ISSUE-30

+    def _briefed_since(self, repo: str, issue: Dict[str, Any]) -> float:
+        """When the ticket was last labeled briefed, or its hold ended if
+        later; 0 when it never was."""
+        events = self.gh.paginate("/repos/%s/issues/%d/events" % (repo, int(issue["number"])))
         since = max((_ts(e.get("created_at")) for e in events if isinstance(e, dict)
                      and e.get("event") == "labeled"
                      and (e.get("label") or {}).get("name") == "loom:briefed"), default=0.0)
-        since = max(since, hold) if since else since
+        return max(since, held_until(issue)) if since else since
+
+    def _unclaimed(self, repo: str, issue: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:

@@ -589,6 +602,29 @@ def briefed(self, repo: str, issue: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
         self.actions += 1

+    def _spread(self, repo: str, issue: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
+        """A ladder ticket waiting behind more than RUNG_BUSY others on its
+        lane moves to an untried rung with a free lane. Not a failure; the
+        rung it leaves stays on its record. True when it moved."""
+        here = current_rung(issue)
+        old = _lane(issue)
+        if not here or self.load.get(old, 0) <= RUNG_BUSY:
+            return False
+        comments = self._comments(repo, int(issue["number"]))
+        tried = tried_rungs(comments) | {here}
+        if not any(min(self.load.get(lane, 0) for lane in LADDER[n - 1][0]) < RUNG_BUSY
+                   for n in range(1, len(LADDER) + 1) if n not in tried):
+            return False

+                           failed_here=False, skip=here)
+        if lane is None:

body:
## Why
The station, every lane runner and the lane machine's brain run from one checkout, and nothing updates it. A Loom pull request the factory merges is merged but not deployed until a person runs `git pull` there; on 2026-10-13 every Loom change ran only because the interactive session pulled by hand after each merge. The north star tracks written, merged, deployed, running, verified for every ticket, and Loom's own tickets stopped at merged.

## Summary
- New `lanes/mac/station.sh`, the station's launchd entry: fetch main, and fast-forward the checkout to it when main's head has a passing `unittest` check run (`LOOM_DEPLOY_CHECK`). It never moves a checkout with local changes, off `LOOM_DEPLOY_BRANCH` (main), or one that is not a fast-forward; a head with CI running or failing waits. Then it runs `python3 -m bus station`. `LOOM_DEPLOY=0` turns deploying off.
- The update runs in shell before Python, so a station broken by a bad merge still receives the fix that follows it. Lane runners re-run each minute from the same checkout and pick up new code on their next pass.
- `install.sh` writes the new entry and `LOOM_DEPLOY`; docs/LANES.md describes it.
- Tests (`tests/test_station_sh.py`, the script run as a process against a local bare remote with fake gh and python3): a green head is deployed and the pass runs; a head with no or failing CI waits; local changes are kept; a diverged checkout is not moved; another branch or `LOOM_DEPLOY=0` is left alone. 438 passed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A green main head is fast-forwarded into the checkout before the station pass, and nothing else moves it (tests)
- [ ] Live: after this merges and the station is reinstalled, the next Loom merge appears in the station log as "deployed <sha>" within a few minutes of its CI passing
- [ ] No manual pull of the station checkout is needed for later Loom merges

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Deploying other goal homes (their goal issues say who deploys).
- Rolling back a bad deploy (fix forward through a pull request; the shell step still runs).

Part of ISSUE-30
