diff --git a/lanes/mac/station.sh b/lanes/mac/station.sh
new file mode 100755
index 00000000..00c5f97c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lanes/mac/station.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,42 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# The station's launchd entry (lanes/mac/install.sh). Before each pass it
+# brings this checkout up to date with its default branch, so a merged Loom
+# change runs within a minute instead of waiting for a person to pull: the
+# lanes and the brain run from this checkout too. It moves only by
+# fast-forward, only from a clean checkout on LOOM_DEPLOY_BRANCH (default
+# main), and only to a head whose CI check (LOOM_DEPLOY_CHECK, default
+# unittest) passed; a newer head with CI running or failing waits. The update
+# runs here, before Python, so a station a bad merge broke still receives the
+# fix merged after it. LOOM_DEPLOY=0 turns it off.
+set -uo pipefail
+REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
+BRANCH="${LOOM_DEPLOY_BRANCH:-main}"
+CHECK="${LOOM_DEPLOY_CHECK:-unittest}"
+say() { printf 'station: %s\n' "$*"; }
+g() { git -C "$REPO_ROOT" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null "$@"; }
+
+deploy() {
+  [ "${LOOM_DEPLOY:-1}" != 0 ] || return 0
+  [ "$(g symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD)" = "$BRANCH" ] || return 0
+  if [ -n "$(g status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ]; then
+    say "not deploying: the checkout has local changes"; return 0
+  fi
+  timeout 60 git -C "$REPO_ROOT" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null fetch -q origin "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null ||
+    { say "not deploying: fetch of $BRANCH failed"; return 0; }
+  local head target slug verdict
+  head="$(g rev-parse HEAD)"; target="$(g rev-parse FETCH_HEAD)"
+  [ "$head" != "$target" ] || return 0
+  if ! g merge-base --is-ancestor "$head" "$target"; then
+    say "not deploying: $BRANCH is not a fast-forward of the checkout"; return 0
+  fi
+  slug="$(g remote get-url origin | sed -E 's#^.*[:/]([^/]+/[^/]+)$#\1#; s#\.git$##')"
+  verdict="$(timeout 30 gh api "repos/$slug/commits/$target/check-runs?check_name=$CHECK" \
+    --jq '[.check_runs[].conclusion] | if length == 0 then "none" elif all(. == "success") then "success" else "other" end' 2>/dev/null)"
+  [ "$verdict" = success ] || return 0
+  if g merge -q --ff-only "$target"; then
+    say "deployed $(g rev-parse --short HEAD): $(g log -1 --format=%s HEAD | cut -c1-100)"
+  fi
+}
+
+deploy
+cd "$REPO_ROOT" && exec python3 -m bus station
diff --git a/tests/test_station_sh.py b/tests/test_station_sh.py
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..f71ee306
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_station_sh.py
@@ -0,0 +1,123 @@
+"""lanes/mac/station.sh run as a process: a local bare repo as the remote, a
+checkout made from it, and fake gh and python3 on PATH."""
+
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+SCRIPT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "lanes" / "mac" / "station.sh"
+
+# Fake gh: prints $FAKE_CHECK as the check verdict the script's --jq asks for.
+FAKE_GH = """#!/usr/bin/env bash
+printf 'gh %s\\n' "$*" >> "$FAKE_LOG"
+printf '%s\\n' "${FAKE_CHECK:-success}"
+"""
+# Fake python3: records that the station pass ran, from which directory.
+FAKE_PY = """#!/usr/bin/env bash
+printf 'python3 %s in %s\\n' "$*" "$PWD" >> "$FAKE_LOG"
+"""
+
+
+def git(*args, cwd=None):
+    subprocess.run(["git", "-c", "user.name=t", "-c", "user.email=<email>", *args],
+                   cwd=cwd, check=True, capture_output=True)
+
+
+class StationScriptTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
+        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.tmp, True)
+        self.remote = self.tmp / "remote.git"
+        git("init", "-q", "--bare", "-b", "main", str(self.remote))
+        seed = self.tmp / "seed"
+        git("clone", "-q", str(self.remote), str(seed))
+        (seed / "a.txt").write_text("one\n")
+        git("add", "a.txt", cwd=seed)
+        git("commit", "-qm", "one", cwd=seed)
+        git("push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:main", cwd=seed)
+        self.seed = seed
+        # The checkout under test holds the script, as the real one does.
+        self.checkout = self.tmp / "loom"
+        git("clone", "-q", str(self.remote), str(self.checkout))
+        (self.checkout / "lanes" / "mac").mkdir(parents=True)
+        shutil.copy(SCRIPT, self.checkout / "lanes" / "mac" / "station.sh")
+        (self.checkout / ".git" / "info" / "exclude").write_text("lanes/\n")
+        self.bin = self.tmp / "bin"
+        self.bin.mkdir()
+        for name, body in (("gh", FAKE_GH), ("python3", FAKE_PY)):
+            (self.bin / name).write_text(body)
+            (self.bin / name).chmod(0o755)
+        self.log = self.tmp / "calls.log"
+
+    def push_change(self, text="two\n"):
+        (self.seed / "a.txt").write_text(text)
+        git("commit", "-qam", "Change a.txt", cwd=self.seed)
+        git("push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:main", cwd=self.seed)
+        return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(self.seed), "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
+                              capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
+
+    def head(self):
+        return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(self.checkout), "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
+                              capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
+
+    def run_script(self, **env):
+        full = dict(os.environ, PATH="%s:%s" % (self.bin, os.environ["PATH"]),
+                    FAKE_LOG=str(self.log), **env)
+        return subprocess.run(["bash", str(self.checkout / "lanes" / "mac" / "station.sh")],
+                              env=full, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
+
+    def calls(self):
+        return self.log.read_text().splitlines() if self.log.exists() else []
+
+    def test_a_green_head_is_deployed_then_the_station_runs(self):
+        target = self.push_change()
+        result = self.run_script()
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        self.assertEqual(self.head(), target)
+        self.assertIn("station: deployed %s: Change a.txt" % target[:7], result.stdout)
+        self.assertEqual(self.calls()[-1], "python3 -m bus station in %s" % self.checkout)
+
+    def test_a_head_whose_ci_has_not_passed_waits(self):
+        before = self.head()
+        self.push_change()
+        for verdict in ("none", "other"):
+            result = self.run_script(FAKE_CHECK=verdict)
+            self.assertEqual(self.head(), before)
+            self.assertNotIn("deployed", result.stdout)
+        self.assertTrue(self.calls()[-1].startswith("python3 -m bus station"))
+
+    def test_local_changes_are_never_overwritten(self):
+        before = self.head()
+        self.push_change()
+        (self.checkout / "a.txt").write_text("edited here\n")
+        result = self.run_script()
+        self.assertEqual(self.head(), before)
+        self.assertEqual((self.checkout / "a.txt").read_text(), "edited here\n")
+        self.assertIn("not deploying: the checkout has local changes", result.stdout)
+
+    def test_a_diverged_checkout_is_not_moved(self):
+        self.push_change()
+        (self.checkout / "b.txt").write_text("local\n")
+        git("add", "b.txt", cwd=self.checkout)
+        git("commit", "-qm", "local", cwd=self.checkout)
+        local = self.head()
+        result = self.run_script()
+        self.assertEqual(self.head(), local)
+        self.assertIn("not a fast-forward", result.stdout)
+
+    def test_another_branch_or_deploy_off_is_left_alone(self):
+        before = self.head()
+        self.push_change()
+        self.run_script(LOOM_DEPLOY="0")
+        self.assertEqual(self.head(), before)
+        git("checkout", "-q", "-b", "work", cwd=self.checkout)
+        self.run_script()
+        self.assertEqual(self.head(), before)
+        self.assertFalse([c for c in self.calls() if c.startswith("gh ")])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

body:
## Why

Epics finish under decision 0003, but nothing noticed when one was done, and nothing caught the shape breaking: a ticket outside any epic, an epic past 15, a goal past 6 open epics, a closed epic with open tickets. The factory must catch its own failures (epic ISSUE-634).

This builds on ISSUE-669 (ISSUE-637): its base is that branch until ISSUE-669 merges, then main.

## Summary

- `bus/brain.py`: `finished_epics(tree)` (an open epic with at least one ticket, every one closed); `goal_epic_cap` (6, or the goal home's recorded exception); `close_epic` and `bus.brain close-epic OWNER/NAME#N --note TEXT`, which closes an open epic as completed with a one-line note and refuses while any ticket under it is open; `bus.brain resume` gains a "Finished epics" section with one `close-epic` item per finished epic.
- `bus/station.py`: the overdue standup reads the goal through `goal_tree` and names finished epics under "Next" ("Epics with every ticket closed (check the done-when, then close)"). Invariant facts now carry a `GoalShape` per goal home (its epics, cap, and open tickets under no epic) from one walk, replacing the sub-issue-count search.
- `bus/invariants.py`: four invariants, filed like the others, replace `goal_full`: `ticket-outside-epic` (one per goal), `epic-over-cap`, `goal-epics-over-cap`, `closed-epic-open-tickets`.
- Docs: `docs/LANES.md` (Invariants), `docs/BRAIN.md` (Filing under an epic), `docs/<redacted>.md` (the close-epic item).

## Acceptance criteria

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Reconcile moves a queued, briefed, running or answered "Land or supersede #P" ticket to loom:merged when its target pull request P has merged, posting a note naming P, its merge commit and merge time.
- Reconcile drops the lane label from that adoption ticket, freeing the lane it held.
- A "Land or supersede #P" ticket whose target P is still open or was closed unmerged is left where it is.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
A "Land or supersede #P" ticket exists only to land pull request P. When P merges some other way (the factory lands it, or a brain merges it), the ticket is never moved, so it stays queued, running or answered and counts against the goal cap. On 2026-10-19 at 22:30Z the Loom goal read 16 of 16 in flight and refused a P0 factory brief; 8 of those 16 were such tickets, all over pull requests already merged:
- ISSUE-996 over ISSUE-995 (merged 18:40Z), ISSUE-991 over ISSUE-989 (18:10Z), ISSUE-980 over ISSUE-979 (15:17Z): queued
- ISSUE-986 over ISSUE-983 (17:17Z), ISSUE-972 over ISSUE-970 (14:07Z), ISSUE-971 over ISSUE-966 (13:56Z), ISSUE-965 over ISSUE-963 (13:28Z): running, holding lanes zai, spark-4 and spark-2
- ISSUE-940 over ISSUE-939 (05:49Z): answered for 17 hours
The brain moved all eight to loom:merged by hand at 22:31Z. The earlier fix for queued tickets over merged work (memory of 2026-10-17, folded into ISSUE-588) covers PRs that carry `Refs`, but a land-or-supersede ticket names its target in its title ("Land or supersede #P") and the target PR's `Refs` points at the original ticket, not at this one.

## Summary
In the station's reconcile pass, for each open ticket whose title starts `Land or supersede #P` (or whose body names the adopted PR the way the adoption brief writes it), read PR P: when it is merged, move the ticket to `loom:merged` with a note naming P, its merge commit and time, and drop its lane label so the lane is free. When P is closed unmerged and the ticket is still queued or briefed, leave it (the ticket's job is then to supersede it).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A queued, briefed, running or answered ticket titled `Land or supersede #P` whose PR P is merged moves to `loom:merged` in the next station pass, with a note naming P and its merge commit.
- [ ] Its `lane:` label is removed, so the lane it held is free for other work.
- [ ] A ticket whose PR P is closed unmerged is not moved.
- [ ] Tests cover merged, closed-unmerged and open target PRs.
- [ ] Live: after the deploy, no open ticket titled `Land or supersede #P` sits outside `loom:merged` or later for more than one station pass after P merged (station log line naming the move, read over 24 hours).

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Changing how adoption tickets are written.
Part of ISSUE-956

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Quiet invariant issues still in triage receive a cleared comment and close as not planned after six hours, while keys with three recent breaches stay open and recurring.
Files: 2 logic, 1 tests

## Why
The station files an invariant issue the moment a factory invariant breaks (`bus/invariants.py`), but nothing clears it when the breach goes away. On 2026-10-15, 24 invariant issues were open in `loom:triage`. Many describe conditions that ended within the hour: ISSUE-434 and ISSUE-428 report lane PRs held by the plan check for about 40 minutes, and both PRs have since passed the check and merged. Anthropic slots were held by a credit limit that lifts at midnight UTC. Each one still waits for the triage rewriter to turn it into a ticket, which spends lane runs on problems that already fixed themselves, and buries the recurring ones.

## Summary
- Each pass, for an open invariant issue still in `loom:triage` whose key has not breached for 6 hours, the station posts one comment naming the time it cleared. It then closes the issue as not planned, unless the same key breached 3 or more times in the last 7 days.
- An invariant key that breached 3 or more times in 7 days gets the label `loom:recurring` and stays open, so the rewriter turns it into a ticket that fixes the cause.
- A closed invariant issue still reopens on a later breach, as today.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test shows an invariant issue in triage whose key has been quiet for 6 hours gets one cleared comment and is closed as not planned, and fails on main
- [ ] A test shows a key with 3 breaches in 7 days is labelled loom:recurring and left open, and an issue already rewritten (not in triage) is never closed
- [ ] Live: within a day of the deploy, the open invariant issues in triage fall below 10, and each closed one carries its cleared comment

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Adding or changing invariants
- Closing tickets that came out of a rewrite

body:
## Why
The brain on its remote VM cannot read the lane machine's heartbeats, so it cannot tell which lanes can take work. And when the brain needs the operator, its ask has to reach the operator's phone without the Discord webhook secret ever sitting on the brain's VM. docs/BRAIN.md ("Lane status", "Asks") gives both jobs to the station; this ticket adds them.

## Summary
Read docs/BRAIN.md and `bus/station.py` first; extend the station's pass, reusing its client, flock, state directory and trust check. Standard library only, Python 3.9 and 3.12, unittest only, no network in tests.
1. Lane status, every pass:
   - Read every `$LOOM_HOME/state/usage/<lane>.json` for the lanes in `bus.labels.LANES`. A lane is "yes" when its heartbeat says available and is at most 600 seconds old, else "no".
   - Find the open issue labelled `loom:lanes` in `LOOM_STATUS_REPO` (default: the owner/name of this checkout's `origin` remote); create it when missing (title `Loom lane status`, label `loom:lanes`, a one-line body saying the station keeps the comment below current).
   - Keep one comment on it starting `<!-- loom:lanes v1 -->`, then `Updated <UTC time>`, then a markdown table: lane, available (yes or no), heartbeat time (UTC). Never include the heartbeat's `reason`.
   - Edit (or create) the comment only when the set of yes or no values differs from the last published one, or when the last publish is more than 60 minutes old. Remember the comment id and last values in `$LOOM_HOME/state/station/lanes.json`.
2. Asks, every pass:
   - Read `GET /repos/{repo}/issues?labels=needs-operator&state=open` for each repo in `LOOM_REPOS` with ETags, like the briefed poll.
   - Only asks whose author and latest `needs-operator` labeller are in `LOOM_BRIEF_AUTHORS` count.
   - The webhook URL comes from SSM: the parameter named by `LOOM_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_SSM`, read with `aws ssm get-parameter --with-decryption` in region `LOOM_AWS_REGION` (default us-east-1), the same way lanes/run_lane.sh reads keys (honour the same `FAKE_SECRET_*` test hook if it has one, otherwise inject a reader function). Never print it. With the setting empty, asks are not forwarded and the pass says so once per run.
   - An ask that also carries `loom:urgent` is posted at once, once per issue: content `Urgent ask: <title> <html_url>`. Others go in one daily digest after `LOOM_DIGEST_HOUR` (local hour, default 9), once per day, listing every open trusted ask as `- <title> <html_url>`; no digest when there are none. Post with `allowed_mentions` set to no mentions, except one `<@id>` mention of `LOOM_DISCORD_MENTION` (a numeric user id) when set. Remember what was sent in `$LOOM_HOME/state/station/asks.json`. A failed post is logged and retried on the next pass, never in a loop.
3. `lanes/mac/install.sh` passes `LOOM_STATUS_REPO`, `LOOM_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_SSM`, `LOOM_DISCORD_MENTION`, `LOOM_DIGEST_HOUR` and `LOOM_AWS_REGION` to `com.loom.station`. Document both jobs in docs/LANES.md in one short paragraph each.
4. Tests in `tests/test_bus_station.py`: status published on first run, not re-published when nothing changed, re-published on a change and after 60 minutes, never containing a reason, issue created when missing; asks: untrusted ignored, urgent sent once, digest once per day after the hour and not before, nothing sent without the webhook setting, a failed post retried next pass.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The `loom:lanes` comment shows each lane's yes or no and heartbeat time, never a reason, and is edited only on change or hourly (tests)
- [ ] Trusted urgent asks reach the webhook once each, the rest once a day in a digest, with the URL read from SSM and never printed (tests)
- [ ] The installer passes the new settings to the station, and docs/LANES.md describes both jobs

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Creating the Discord channel or webhook (infrastructure-as-code elsewhere)
- The brain's tick commands

body:
## Why
The operator, 2026-10-13: "Can we start loom on all my other open tickets across all repos too public and <redacted>? If it can't do something please just make it human in the loop tagged". About 1,080 issues are open across 20 repos, and 13 of those repos are not in `LOOM_REPOS`. Adding a repo today is several hand steps (labels, a goal home, checking the review bot runs there, telling the lanes it is <redacted>), and the north-star goal on ISSUE-30 asks that adding a repo be one config line plus a test.

## Summary
- `python3 -m bus.brain onboard OWNER/NAME`:
  - creates any missing Loom labels in the repo (every `loom:` state, `loom:ticket`, `loom:goal`, `loom:urgent`, `loom:human`, `loom:triage`, `needs-operator`, and each `lane:` label from `bus/labels.py`), with the colors and descriptions the existing repos use;
  - creates the repo's backlog goal home when none is open: title "Backlog: every open issue in OWNER/NAME is worked through Loom or handed to a person", label `loom:goal`, and a body with the destination, the metric (open issues not yet tickets, tickets, `loom:human`), and the rules (never close an issue from triage; <redacted> repos never go to lanes that train on prompts);
  - checks that the review check (`LOOM_REVIEW_CHECK`) ran on the repo's recent pull requests and says plainly when it did not (the factory never merges there without it);
  - prints the `LOOM_REPOS` value with the repo added, and changes nothing else on the machine.
- Running it twice changes nothing the second time.
- Tests with the brain test fakes: labels created only when missing, one goal home only, the review-check warning, the printed value.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `onboard` creates missing labels and one backlog goal home, and a second run is a no-op (tests that fail without the change)
- [ ] It warns when the review check has not run on the repo's pull requests (tests)
- [ ] Live: onboarding one new repo gives it the labels and a goal home that `bus.brain status` lists

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Triage of the repo's open issues (its own ticket)
- Editing the lane machine's install
Part of ISSUE-30

---
Loom ticket example.factory-148, lane anthropic, model claude-opus-5-5.
Refs ISSUE-148

+BACKLOG_TITLE = "Backlog: every open issue in %s is worked through Loom or handed to a person"

+def _backlog_body(repo: str) -> str:
+    return "\n".join([
+        "## Destination",
+        "",
+        "Every open issue in %s is either a Loom ticket worked by a lane or "
+        "labelled `loom:human` with one comment naming what only a person can do."
+        % repo,
+        "",
+        "## Metric",
+        "",
+        "- Open issues not yet tickets (neither `loom:ticket` nor `loom:human`): "
+        "falls to 0.",
+        "- Open `loom:ticket` issues: rise, then fall as they ship.",
+        "- Open `loom:human` issues: each has its ask.",
+        "",
+        "## Rules",
+        "",
+        "- Triage never closes an issue. It rewrites one as a ticket, marks what "
+        "is missing with `loom:triage`, or hands it to a person with `loom:human`.",
+        "- If this repo is <redacted>, its briefs never go to a lane whose provider "
+        "may train on prompts.",
+        "- No pull request merges here without the review check.",
+    ])
+
+
+def _review_check_line(gh: GitHub, repo: str, check: str) -> str:
+    """Whether the review check ran on any of the repo's latest pull requests."""
+    prs = gh.rest("GET", "/repos/%s/pulls?state=all&per_page=%d"
+                  % (repo, REVIEW_SAMPLE)).data or []
+    prs = [p for p in prs if isinstance(p, dict)][:REVIEW_SAMPLE]
+    if not prs:
+        return ("warning: %s has no pull requests yet, so it is unknown whether %s runs "
+                "there; the factory never merges a pull request without it"
+                % (repo, check))
+    for pr in prs:
+        sha = str((pr.get("head") or {}).get("sha") or "")
+        if not sha:
+            continue
+        runs = gh.rest("GET", "/repos/%s/commits/%s/check-runs?check_name=%s&per_page=1"
+                       % (repo, sha, quote(check, safe=""))).data or {}
+        if int(runs.get("total_count") or 0) > 0:
+            return "review check: %s ran on %s#%s" % (check, repo, pr["number"])
+    return ("warning: %s did not run on the last %d pull requests in %s (%s); the "
+            "factory never merges there without it, so install the review bot first"
+            % (check, len(prs), repo, ", ".join("#%s" % p["number"] for p in prs)))
+
+
+def onboard(gh: GitHub, repo: str, review_check: Optional[str] = None,
+            env: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None) -> List[str]:
+    """Make a repo ready for Loom: the labels, one backlog goal home, a check
+    that the review check runs there, and the LOOM_REPOS value with the repo
+    in it. A second run changes nothing. Returns the lines to print."""
+    from . import factory, labels  # factory imports this module
+    env = os.environ if env is None else env
+    check = (review_check or env.get("LOOM_REVIEW_CHECK", "").strip()
+             or factory.DEFAULT_REVIEW_CHECK)
+    info = gh.rest("GET", "/repos/%s" % repo).data or {}
+    lines = ["%s is %s" % (repo, "<redacted>: its briefs never go to lanes that train on prompts"
+                           if info.get("<redacted>") else "public")]
+    changed = labels.ensure_labels(gh, repo)
+    lines.append("labels: %s" % (", ".join(changed) if changed else "no changes"))
+    title = BACKLOG_TITLE % repo
+    goals = gh.paginate("/repos/%s/issues?state=open&labels=loom%%3Agoal" % repo)
+    home = [g for g in goals if "pull_request" not in g and g.get("title") == title]
+    if home:
+        lines.append("backlog goal home: #%s, already open" % home[0]["number"])
+    else:
+        body = _backlog_body(repo)
+        _check_written_text(body)
+        made = gh.rest("POST", "/repos/%s/issues" % repo,
+                       {"title": title, "body": body, "labels": ["loom:goal"]}).data or {}
+        lines.append("backlog goal home: #%s, created" % made.get("number"))
+    lines.append(_review_check_line(gh, repo, check))
+    repos = env.get("LOOM_REPOS", "").replace(",", " ").split()
+    if repo not in repos:
+        repos.append(repo)
+    lines.append('LOOM_REPOS="%s"' % " ".join(repos))
+    return lines

## Why

Right after ISSUE-153 shipped, game-orchestrator ISSUE-897 still reached the last rung. Its pull request is 11 hours old, and the age rule ("older than 6 hours") was true on every round, so each send-back climbed and three rounds used the whole ladder. Age should mark a pull request as stuck once per window, not on every round.

## Summary

- `bus/factory.py`: `stuck()` counts age only when the pull request is over 6 hours old and its ticket has not moved on the ladder for 6 hours (`last_climb()` reads the newest rung marker's time). Surviving threads and still-failing checks climb as before.
- `docs/LANES.md`: the rule.
- `tests/test_bus_factory.py`: an old pull request an hour after its last climb stays on its rung, and climbs once 6 hours have passed. This fails on the current factory.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Age climbs at most once per 6 hours per ticket (test that fails without the change)
- [ ] Surviving threads and still-failing checks still climb (existing tests pass)
- [ ] Live: no ticket climbs twice within 6 hours on age alone in the station log after this ships

Size: XS

## Out of scope

- The other stuck signals
- Ladder models

Part of ISSUE-30

## Why
On 2026-10-13 the spark lane's run of a wow ticket made the right change (25 tests passed, summary written), then vLLM answered two requests with 400 Bad Request, opencode exited 1, and the runner recorded a failure and dropped the change. The 400s carry no reason in vLLM's log, and the run log shows none either. Part of ISSUE-30.

## Summary
- Find the request vLLM rejects: run opencode against the spark endpoint with a long session (as the lane does) and capture the 400 response body (for example by pointing the lane at a logging proxy in a test, or by reading opencode's own log in the agent home, which the runner should also archive with the transcript).
- Fix the cause in the runner's opencode config for the spark lane (for example a max_tokens or context setting that fits the server's limit, or the helper model calls), so a finished run exits 0.
- The runner archives opencode's log directory with the session store, so the next failure shows its reason.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The cause is named in the pull request with the 400 response body that shows it.
- [ ] A test covers the config change (and the log archive), and fails without it.
- [ ] Live proof: the next spark ticket ends "done" with a pull request.

Size: M

## Out of scope
The vLLM server's own settings (the infra repo); other lanes.

body:
## Why

Health intake matches a live finding to its open ticket and then only updates it: a Priority band change, an evidence comment every 6 hours. When that ticket has already shipped, a finding that is still reported means the fix did not work, and nothing turned that into work. A finding that sat matched to a shipped ticket for a day was briefed as a regression by hand.

## Summary

- `bus/health.py`: after the usual update, a finding whose open ticket is `loom:shipped` or `loom:verified` and that is still reported 24 hours after `loom:shipped` was applied (read once from the issue events, then kept in the ledger) re-briefs the ticket through `brain.brief(..., regresses=N)`. The brief starts with "Regresses #N", then the hours since the ship, the affected count, hours and impact, and the finding's words fenced as untrusted data, followed by a full ticket body for when brain files a new ticket instead.
- At most once per ticket every 48 hours (a `regressed` map in the health ledger). A refusal from brain (the goal's regression slot held, say) is logged once and tried again next pass. After a re-brief the intake re-reads the ticket, so another finding's Priority edit in the same pass cannot write back the old body.
- A ticket in a build state (queued to merged) gets only the usual update, and its events are never read. A finding that goes absent gets the usual absent note and nothing else.
- `docs/HEALTH.md` describes the new rule.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `tests/test_bus_health.py` `Regression` and `RegressionThroughBrain` show a finding still reported 24 hours after its ticket shipped re-briefs that ticket as a regression (the real brain brief moves it to `loom:queued` + `loom:regression`, with the evidence and hours), once per 48 hours. The six that brief a regression fail against origin/main's `bus/health.py`.
- [ ] Tests show a ticket in a build state (queued, running, pr, merged) gets only the usual evidence comment, and a finding absent after the ship files nothing.
- [ ] Live: within a day of the deploy, a finding that outlived its ticket's ship has a regression brief filed by the station, with no person writing it.

Size: M

## Out of scope

- Findings with no matched open ticket (already filed as new tickets), including a ticket closed as completed.
- A ticket that is merged but not shipped: its fix is not deployed, and `brief --regresses` refuses it.
- How the endpoint picks findings.

Refs ISSUE-484

body:
## Why

The station and brain moved onto the Loom GitHub App (ISSUE-648) and stopped spending the operator account's request budget. The dashboard still reads GitHub with a token that bills that account, and every fresh pod's first snapshot costs hundreds of requests. ISSUE-648 lets the dashboard use the App only when both the openssl and aws CLIs exist; the dashboard container has openssl but no aws CLI and no parameter-store access, so it could never mint an App token.

## Summary

- `bus/github.py`: `AppToken.from_env` accepts `LOOM_GITHUB_APP_KEY_FILE`, a path to the App's <redacted> key, as an alternative to `LOOM_GITHUB_APP_KEY_SSM` (the file wins when both are set). The file is read at each mint (`read_key_file`), so a rotated secret is picked up, and the existing rules hold: signed by openssl on stdin, never written, never logged. The token records `key_source` and `key_file`.
- `dashboard/github.py`: `app_from_env` needs only openssl for a key file (the aws CLI only for the parameter store). A key file that cannot be opened at start keeps the configured token, with one warning naming the file and the error kind, never the contents.
- `docs/DASHBOARD.md` names the three settings and says the deployment mounts the key from a Kubernetes secret; `.env.example` adds a placeholder.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `DashboardAppTests.test_a_mounted_key_file_makes_the_dashboard_send_an_installation_token`: with the App id, installation id and a key file set, the dashboard's client sends an installation token minted from that file; it fails on main.
- [ ] `DashboardAppTests.test_an_unreadable_key_file_keeps_the_token_and_names_only_the_file`: an unreadable key file falls back to the configured token with one log line naming the file, never its contents; it fails on main.
- [ ] Live: after the deployment mounts the key and sets the settings, the dashboard's requests no longer count against the operator account's budget, read from the App's and the account's rate limits.

Proof: both new tests fail on main and pass here. Full suite on this branch: 1663 tests, OK (1 skipped).

Size: S

## Out of scope

- The deployment change that mounts the secret (an infrastructure pull request).

Refs ISSUE-652

## Intent
Class: sensitive
- # Summary
- ## Behavior Changes
- `brief --lane <redacted>` files tickets as `loom:queued` (not `loom:briefed`), so the <redacted> remote lane can claim them; a <redacted> repo or a difficulty tier outside the lane's (`easy`, `medium`) is refused before any issue is created.
- `brief --regresses N --lane <redacted>` re-briefs the shipped ticket back to `loom:queued` with the same public-scope and tier checks.
- `brief --lane codex` and other local lanes still file as `loom:briefed`.
Files: 1 sensitive, 1 tests

## Why
`python3 -m bus.brain brief OWNER/NAME --lane <redacted>` files the ticket as `loom:briefed` + `lane:<redacted>` (`_file_ticket` in bus/brain.py: `"loom:briefed" if lane else "loom:queued"`). The remote <redacted> lane claims only open issues labelled `loom:queued` and `lane:<redacted>` (`_candidates` in bus/lane.py, `labels=loom:queued,lane:<lane>`). A ticket briefed onto <redacted> is therefore never claimed.
On 2026-10-19, ISSUE-1019 (P0, the fix for factory incident ISSUE-1000, which holds every local loom lane run) was briefed on <redacted> at 22:33Z. It was still `loom:briefed` with `Remote claims: <redacted> 0/1` at 23:41Z. The brain moved it to queued by hand at 23:45Z. `move` already refuses a remote lane outside `--to queued`, and `fix` refuses a remote lane outright (bus/brain.py, "remote lane %s only works with --to queued"). Only `brief` (and the regression re-brief path, `_rebrief_regressed`) skip that rule.

## Summary
In `brief` and the regression re-brief, when `lane` is in `REMOTE_LANES`, file the ticket as `loom:queued` + `lane:<lane>` and run the same remote checks `move --to queued` runs (`_check_remote_queue`: public repo, a tier the lane takes). Refuse with the same message when they fail.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `brief --lane <redacted>` on a public repo with an easy or medium Difficulty files the ticket with `loom:queued` and `lane:<redacted>`, not `loom:briefed`.
- [ ] `brief --lane <redacted>` on a <redacted> repo, or with a hard Difficulty, is refused with the remote-lane reason and files nothing.
- [ ] `brief --regresses M --lane <redacted>` re-queues M as `loom:queued` + `lane:<redacted>` under the same checks.
- [ ] Tests cover the three cases above, and a local lane still files `loom:briefed`.
- [ ] Live: after the deploy, the next ticket briefed onto <redacted> shows `loom:queued` in its first labelled event, and the <redacted> lane's `claim` returns it (GitHub issue events).

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Changing how the <redacted> lane claims work.
Part of ISSUE-1034

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- Goal repos without a Backlog home now triage under their goal while fewer than three queued tickets exist, with at most five not-ready comments per run.
- The station reports queued and triage counts for fallback goal homes and includes those homes in rewrite processing.
Files: 1 sensitive, 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
The station triages and rewrites issues only under goal homes titled `Backlog:` (`bus/station.py` `_backlog_goals`, `_rewrite_goals`). On 2026-10-16, 6 of the 10 goal repos had no such home (assay among them), holding 461 open issues with no `loom:` label. Their loose issues never become tickets, and `loom:triage` issues there are never rewritten (bench-suite ISSUE-42 has waited since 2026-10-13). When such a goal's queue runs dry nothing refills it: assay merged 0 on 2026-10-16 and failed the Throughput number.

## Summary
- A goal repo with no open `Backlog:` home is triaged and rewritten under its goal home from the station config, with the same per-run limit (25, oldest first) and the same skips (pull requests, epics, asks, anything with a `loom:` label).
- To avoid a flood, triage in such a repo runs only while the goal has fewer than 3 `loom:queued` tickets, and comments on at most 5 not-ready issues per run.
- The hourly status line names each goal repo triaged this way and how many issues it queued.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A unit test with a goal repo that has no `Backlog:` home asserts `triage_backlogs` and `rewrite_triaged` both process it under the configured goal home.
- [ ] A unit test asserts no triage runs in that repo while its goal has 3 or more `loom:queued` tickets, and that not-ready comments stop at 5 per run.
- [ ] A repo that does have a `Backlog:` home behaves exactly as today (existing station tests pass untouched).

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Opening new `Backlog:` issues in any repo.
- Closing or marking done any old issue from triage (the existing rule stands).
- Changing the rewrite model list.

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- bus.brain brief takes an optional --holder; a brief filed with it on a goal whose newest brief-stage marker is a defer posts a journal on the goal home with the brief done line and the new ticket, so resume stops listing the finished brief.
- A brief without --holder, on a goal with no standing brief defer, a refused brief, or a --regresses brief posts no journal and changes no marker.
- If the done journal fails to post after the ticket is filed, brief exits with an error naming the ticket and the done line to journal by hand.
- docs/<redacted>.md and docs/BRAIN.md say a written brief records its own done marker, and the <redacted> tick's brief command passes --holder <redacted>.
Files: 1 sensitive, 1 tests, 2 docs

## Why
A brief written from a `resume brief` item only retires that item when the brain pastes the `loom:done v1 stage=brief` line into its journal by hand. When it forgets, `resume` lists the finished brief again and the next brain spends its tick on work already done.
Evidence from ISSUE-30 on 2026-10-16: the lane machine deferred a brief at 13:21Z; <redacted> filed it as ISSUE-521 at 14:13Z and its 14:17Z journal said "Stage done recorded for ISSUE-30 brief" but carried no marker line. Resume re-listed the item, and the lane machine's 14:28Z tick spent its resume time finding ISSUE-521 and pasting the missing done line. A brief defer's item is the goal home, whose revision is always `open`, so `handoff.live` never drops it on its own (bus/handoff.py `live`, bus/brain.py `defer` / `_goal_resume_lines`).

## Summary
When `python3 -m bus.brain brief OWNER/NAME --goal N ...` creates a ticket and the goal home N carries a live brief defer (the newest brief-stage marker for that goal is a defer), the brief stage for that goal is recorded as done without the brain's journal having to carry it. For example: `brief` takes an optional `--holder` and, after the ticket is created, posts a `<!-- loom:journal v1 -->` comment on the goal home holding the `handoff.done_marker("brief", goal, holder)` line and the new ticket number, or `resume` treats a ticket created under the goal after the defer as retiring it. Pick the smaller change that keeps the newest-marker-wins rule in bus/handoff.py intact.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After `brief` creates a ticket under a goal whose newest brief-stage marker is a defer, `resume` no longer lists that `resume brief` item, with no done line written by hand.
- [ ] A `brief` on a goal with no live brief defer posts no extra comment and changes no marker.
- [ ] A refused brief (missing sections, bad title, GitHub error) records no done marker.
- [ ] Tests in tests/test_handoff.py or tests/test_brain.py cover the three cases above.
- [ ] docs/<redacted>.md (Handing off stage work) and docs/BRAIN.md say a written brief records its own done marker.

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Done markers for other stages (merge, failed, ask, regression).
- The mismatch between the brief's required sections and the ticket.md template (a separate finding).
- Changing the defer marker format.
Part of ISSUE-30

+                with self.assertRaises((ValueError, GitHubError)):

+                                case.get("title", "Ticket"), case.get("body", BRIEF),
+                                holder=case.get("holder", "lane-machine"), env=ENV)
+                self.assertEqual([], self.journals_posted(fake))
+
+    def test_a_failed_done_post_names_the_ticket_and_the_line_to_journal(self):

body:
## Why
The remote lane implements tickets and commits locally, but it cannot publish the ticket branch: `git push` over HTTPS fails with "could not read Username for 'https://github.com'". No git HTTPS credential exists on the lane machine, and the approved surrogate token cannot be placed into a git credential store (the runtime redacts PAT values in tool I/O). Without a push, `bus.lane pr` cannot open the pull request and the ticket stalls at `loom:running`.

## Summary
- New `bus.lane push OWNER/NAME#N` subcommand pushes the ticket's branch through the GitHub git-database API using the same token the `GitHub` client already carries (the approved surrogate mechanism)
- Recreates the branch's new commits in order (blobs, trees, commits) and creates or updates the remote ref; verifies tree SHAs match local before creating each commit
- Refuses to push when the current branch does not match the ticket's branch; no-op when the remote is already up to date
- For a new remote branch, bases the push on the repo's default branch from the API (not hardcoded `main`)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `bus.lane push` creates the remote branch via the git-database API with no git HTTPS credential configured
- [ ] Pushing a multi-commit branch recreates every commit in order with matching tree SHAs
- [ ] Re-running push on an up-to-date branch makes zero API write calls
- [ ] Push refuses when the checkout is not on the ticket's branch
- [ ] All 17 `test_remote_lane.py` tests pass, including the 4 new push tests

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Changing the surrogate mechanism itself
- Wiring `push` into the scheduled lane runbook (the command exists; the runbook update is separate)
- Deleting the standalone workaround script (kept until the lane adopts the command)

Refs ISSUE-481

     return result.stdout.strip()
 
 
+def _git_bytes(*args: str) -> bytes:
+    result = subprocess.run(["git", *args], capture_output=True, check=False)
+    if result.returncode:
+        raise OSError("git %s failed" % (args[0],))
+    return result.stdout
+
+
+def _push_commit(gh: GitHub, repo: str, local_sha: str, local_parent: str,
+                 api_parent: str) -> str:
+    """Recreate one local commit through the git-database API. Returns the new
+    remote commit SHA. Blob and tree SHAs are content-addressed, so re-running
+    recreates identical objects."""
+    tree_updates = []
+    for line in _git("diff", "--name-status", local_parent, local_sha).splitlines():
+        status, _, path = line.partition("\t")
+        if status.startswith("D"):
+            tree_updates.append({"path": path, "mode": "100644",
+                                 "type": "blob", "sha": None})
+            continue
+        blob_sha = _git("rev-parse", local_sha + ":" + path)
+        content = _git_bytes("cat-file", "blob", blob_sha)
+        made = gh.rest("POST", "/repos/%s/git/blobs" % repo, {
+            "content": base64.b64encode(content).decode("ascii"),
+            "encoding": "base64"}).data or {}
+        if made.get("sha") != blob_sha:
+            raise GitHubError("blob SHA mismatch for %s" % path)
+        mode = _git("ls-tree", local_sha, path).split()[0]
+        tree_updates.append({"path": path, "mode": mode,
+                             "type": "blob", "sha": blob_sha})
+    base_tree = _git("rev-parse", local_parent + "^{tree}")
+    new_tree = (gh.rest("POST", "/repos/%s/git/trees" % repo, {
+        "base_tree": base_tree, "tree": tree_updates}).data or {}).get("sha")
+    if new_tree != _git("rev-parse", local_sha + "^{tree}"):
+        raise GitHubError("tree SHA mismatch for commit %s" % local_sha[:12])
+    author = {
+        "name": _git("log", "-1", "--format=%an", local_sha),
+        "email": _git("log", "-1", "--format=%ae", local_sha),
+        "date": _git("log", "-1", "--format=%aI", local_sha),
+    }
+    commit = (gh.rest("POST", "/repos/%s/git/commits" % repo, {
+        "message": _git("log", "-1", "--format=%B", local_sha),
+        "tree": new_tree, "parents": [api_parent],
+        "author": author, "committer": author}).data or {})
+    if not commit.get("sha"):
+        raise GitHubError("GitHub did not return the created commit")
+    return str(commit["sha"])
+
+
+def push_branch(gh: GitHub, repo: str, number: int) -> str:
+    """Push the current branch through the git-database API and return the
+    remote HEAD SHA. The lane has no git HTTPS credential, so `git push`
+    cannot work; the API accepts the same token the GitHub client carries.
+    The current branch must be the ticket's branch. Idempotent: pushing an
+    up-to-date branch changes nothing."""
+    issue = gh.rest("GET", "/repos/%s/issues/%d" % (repo, number)).data or {}
+    branch = tickets.branch_for(number, str(issue.get("title") or ""))
+    current = _git("branch", "--show-current")
+    if current != branch:
+        raise ValueError("current branch %r does not match the ticket branch %r"
+                         % (current, branch))
+    local_head = _git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
+    try:
+        ref = gh.rest("GET", "/repos/%s/git/refs/heads/%s"
+                      % (repo, quote(branch, safe=""))).data or {}
+        remote_head = str(((ref.get("object") or {}).get("sha")) or "")
+    except GitHubError as err:
+        if err.status != 404:
+            raise
+        remote_head = ""
+    if remote_head == local_head:
+        return local_head
+    if remote_head:
+        base, exists = remote_head, True
+    else:
+        info = gh.rest("GET", "/repos/%s" % repo).data or {}
+        default = str(info.get("default_branch") or "main")
+        base, exists = _git("merge-base", "HEAD", "origin/" + default), False
+    commits = _git("rev-list", "--reverse", base + "..HEAD").splitlines()
+    api_parent, local_parent = base, base
+    for sha in commits:
+        api_parent = _push_commit(gh, repo, sha, local_parent, api_parent)
+        local_parent = sha
+    ref_path = "/repos/%s/git/refs/heads/%s" % (repo, quote(branch, safe=""))
+    if exists:
+        gh.rest("PATCH", ref_path, {"sha": api_parent, "force": False})
+    else:
+        try:
+            gh.rest("POST", "/repos/%s/git/refs" % repo,
+                    {"ref": "refs/heads/" + branch, "sha": api_parent})
+        except GitHubError as err:
+            if err.status != 422:
+                raise
+            gh.rest("PATCH", ref_path, {"sha": api_parent, "force": False})
+    return api_parent
+

+class FakeGitDatabase:
+    """A GitHub API fake that speaks the git-database endpoints push_branch
+    needs: ref reads, blob/tree/commit creation, ref creation."""
+
+    def __init__(self, tree_sha="t" * 40, commit_sha="c" * 40, trees=None,
+                 commits=None):
+        self.tree_sha = tree_sha
+        self.commit_sha = commit_sha
+        # Optional per-call answers, consumed in order, for multi-commit pushes.
+        self.trees = list(trees or [])
+        self.commits = list(commits or [])
+        self.refs = {}  # branch -> sha
+        self.calls = []
+        self.bodies = []
+
+    def _blob_sha(self, content_b64):
+        import base64
+        import hashlib
+        content = base64.b64decode(content_b64)
+        # Git's own object id, not a security use: the fake must answer the
+        # same blob SHA git computes locally.
+        return hashlib.sha1(b"blob %d\0" % len(content) + content,
+                            usedforsecurity=False).hexdigest()
+
+    def rest(self, method, path, body=None, **kwargs):
+        from bus.github import GitHubError
+        from urllib.parse import unquote
+        self.calls.append((method, path))
+        self.bodies.append((method, path, body))
+        if method == "GET" and "/git/refs/heads/" in path:
+            branch = unquote(path.split("/git/refs/heads/", 1)[1])
+            if branch in self.refs:
+                return type("Response", (), {"data": {
+                    "object": {"sha": self.refs[branch]}}})()
+            raise GitHubError("GET %s -> 404" % path, 404, "")
+        if method == "POST" and path.endswith("/git/blobs"):
+            return type("Response", (), {"data": {
+                "sha": self._blob_sha(body["content"])}})()
+        if method == "POST" and path.endswith("/git/trees"):
+            sha = self.trees.pop(0) if self.trees else self.tree_sha
+            return type("Response", (), {"data": {"sha": sha}})()
+        if method == "POST" and path.endswith("/git/commits"):
+            sha = self.commits.pop(0) if self.commits else self.commit_sha
+            return type("Response", (), {"data": {"sha": sha}})()
+        if method == "POST" and path.endswith("/git/refs"):
+            branch = body["ref"].split("refs/heads/", 1)[1]
+            self.refs[branch] = body["sha"]
+            return type("Response", (), {"data": {}})()
+        if method == "PATCH" and "/git/refs/heads/" in path:
+            branch = path.split("/git/refs/heads/", 1)[1]
+            self.refs[branch] = body["sha"]
+            return type("Response", (), {"data": {}})()
+        raise AssertionError("unexpected API call: %s %s" % (method, path))
+
+
+def _make_repo(tmp, extra_commit=False):
+    import subprocess
+    def git(*args, **kwargs):
+        subprocess.run(["git", *args], capture_output=True, check=True, cwd=kwargs.get("cwd", tmp),
+                       env={**__import__("os").environ,
+                            "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME": "t", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL": "t@t",
+                            "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME": "t", "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL": "t@t"})
+    origin = __import__("os").path.join(tmp, "origin.git")
+    git("init", "--bare", origin)
+    work = __import__("os").path.join(tmp, "work")
+    __import__("os").makedirs(work)
+    git("init", "-b", "main", cwd=work)
+    git("remote", "add", "origin", origin, cwd=work)
+    with open(__import__("os").path.join(work, "file.txt"), "w") as f:
+        f.write("base\n")
+    git("add", "file.txt", cwd=work)
+    git("commit", "-m", "base", cwd=work)
+    git("push", "-u", "origin", "main", cwd=work)
+    git("checkout", "-b", "loom/4-add-a-feature", cwd=work)
+    with open(__import__("os").path.join(work, "file.txt"), "w") as f:
+        f.write("changed\n")
+    git("add", "file.txt", cwd=work)
+    git("commit", "-m", "change", cwd=work)
+    if extra_commit:
+        with open(__import__("os").path.join(work, "second.txt"), "w") as f:
+            f.write("second\n")
+        git("add", "second.txt", cwd=work)
+        git("commit", "-m", "second change", cwd=work)
+    return work
+
+
+class PushBranchTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_push_creates_remote_branch_via_git_database_api(self):
+        import os
+        import subprocess
+        import tempfile
+        from bus import lane
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            repo = _make_repo(tmp)
+            tree_sha = subprocess.run(
+                ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD^{tree}"], capture_output=True,
+                text=True, check=True, cwd=repo).stdout.strip()
+            gh = FakeGitDatabase(tree_sha=tree_sha)
+            issue = {"number": 4, "title": "Add a feature"}
+            gh_issue = FakeGitHub()
+            # FakeGitHub serves the issue; FakeGitDatabase speaks git-database.
+            # Combine: issue GETs go to FakeGitHub, git-database to FakeGitDatabase.
+            class Combined:
+                def rest(self, method, path, body=None, **kwargs):
+                    if "/git/" in path:
+                        return gh.rest(method, path, body, **kwargs)
+                    return gh_issue.rest(method, path, body, **kwargs)
+            old = os.getcwd()
+            os.chdir(repo)
+            try:
+                sha = lane.push_branch(Combined(), "example/project", 4)
+            finally:
+                os.chdir(old)
+            self.assertEqual(sha, gh.commit_sha)
+            self.assertEqual(gh.refs["loom/4-add-a-feature"], gh.commit_sha)
+            posts = [c for c in gh.calls if c[0] == "POST"]
+            self.assertTrue(any(p[1].endswith("/git/blobs") for p in posts))
+            self.assertTrue(any(p[1].endswith("/git/trees") for p in posts))
+            self.assertTrue(any(p[1].endswith("/git/commits") for p in posts))
+            self.assertTrue(any(p[1].endswith("/git/refs") for p in posts))
+
+    def test_push_recreates_every_commit_of_a_multi_commit_branch_in_order(self):
+        import os
+        import subprocess
+        import tempfile
+        from bus import lane
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:

+
+            def rev(spec):

+                    ["git", "rev-parse", spec], capture_output=True,
+                    text=True, check=True, cwd=repo).stdout.strip()
+            base = rev("main")

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- Added a sandboxed Copilot Free lane that reads its token from SSM and accepts public easy tickets.
- Copilot usage-limit failures hold the lane until the next UTC month begins.
Files: 1 sensitive, 2 logic, 2 tests, 2 docs

## Why
GitHub Copilot Free includes the Copilot CLI and agent mode, with a small monthly allowance that nothing in Loom uses today. The operator's rule is that every free tier gets used up. The CLI (`@github/copilot` 1.0.100) is installed on the lane machine and signed in for the operator's account. Each prompt to the Copilot CLI counts as one request (GitHub's billing docs), so a lane run that is one prompt may cost one request. GitHub's plan pages disagree on the Free allowance (50 chat requests a month, or an allowance of AI credits), so the real cost per ticket has to be measured.
The CLI keeps its sign-in outside `~/.copilot/config.json`, likely in the macOS keychain, which a lane must never touch. The CLI reads `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (then `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`) ahead of any stored sign-in, so the lane can take a token from SSM like the other API lanes.

## Summary
- A `copilot` lane slot in `lanes/run_lane.sh`. It runs `copilot -p "<brief>" --allow-all-tools` inside the shared agent sandbox, with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` read from SSM (`LOOM_COPILOT_KEY_SSM`) and no keychain access.
- Free tier, public repos only. It takes easy tickets, like the zen lane, and is listed in `PUBLIC_ONLY` until the operator decides otherwise.
- A usage-limit answer is a `[limit]` that holds the lane until the next monthly reset.
- Before the lane takes queued work, one trial ticket records how many requests a run cost, read from the CLI's own usage output or GitHub's usage page.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A test: the copilot lane runs the CLI with the brief as its prompt, with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` from the lane's key and no HOME keychain or credential files reachable. It fails on main.
- [x] A test: a Copilot usage-limit message holds the lane until the next month starts, not one hour.
- [ ] Live: one easy public ticket merges through the copilot lane, and its run records how many requests it used (lane log).
Size: M

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Copilot cloud agent sessions (Copilot Pro only).
- Paid Copilot plans.

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- Stale ticket banners show snapshot age, a plain language cause, and the next refresh time.
- Results cells explain which issue-comment window was not read and when it will be checked again.
Files: 3 sensitive, 2 tests

## Why
The dashboard shows "Showing stale ticket data." on every page with no cause or age, and many panels say "not recorded", "missing", or "not looked" with an internal reason, such as "optional view sources were not refreshed because the GitHub request budget is below its floor". The operator asked what the banner means and why things fail. A message that names neither the cause in plain words nor what fixes it is noise.

## Summary
- The stale banner says since when the data is stale and why, in one line: for example "Ticket data is 40 minutes old: GitHub's request budget ran low; it refreshes at 15:30 ET."
- Each empty-panel message names the source it could not read and the next refresh time, in plain words, without internal terms like "optional view sources" or "floor".
- "not looked" on Results says what window was not read and why.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test: when the snapshot is stale, the banner includes the data's age and the reason; it fails on main.
- [ ] A test: no rendered page contains the phrase "optional view sources" or "below its floor".
- [ ] Live: every page checked in a browser shows no unexplained "missing" or "not recorded" text after a fresh deploy.

Size: S

## Out of scope
- The GitHub budget itself.

title: Every stale banner and empty panel says what is missing, why, and when it refreshes, in plain words

body:
## Why
From the factory audit of 2026-10-12 (finding F10). Part of ISSUE-30.
[merge in brain.py:256-273](https://github.com/example/loom/blob/6968e0ca3bb09484e17210589d68b08c29e92629/bus/brain.py#L256) accepts an optional ticket tuple, validates the PR's checks/branch, merges it, then moves that supplied ticket to merged. It never verifies that the ticket is a Loom ticket or that the PR links to it. In contrast, fix() has an explicit _linked check. A full source-only merge probe with fake GitHub accepted a PR linking ticket 1 but supplied issue 999 carrying only an unrelated label, then issued a fake merge followed by a fake label update on 999. No real write was made. A mistyped reference can therefore credit unrelated work; a closed supplied ticket fails only after the irreversible merge. This is a current source-level risk, not a claim that a wrong-ticket merge was observed today. review-bot ISSUE-1146 reads acceptance context; it does not authorize Loom's lifecycle mutation.

## Summary
Before merging, resolve and validate one authoritative Loom ticket association: trusted repo, open ticket, expected state, and the exact PR/branch relationship. Reject disagreement before the merge request. Use the same association parser across fix, merge, and reconciliation, with supported same-repo reference forms. Record the chosen relationship with the merge result.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tests for an unrelated, closed, or non-ticket supplied issue make zero merge calls; they fail without the change.
- [ ] A valid linked ticket merges at the inspected head SHA and supplies the identical association to the reconciliation path.
- [ ] Live proof: the next lane merge records the validated PR/ticket pair, and a read-only preflight with an intentionally mismatched ticket refuses it before any write.

Size: S

## Out of scope
Changing bot review policy, automatically approving semantics, or treating a merged ticket as live-verified.

Loom ticket example.factory-111, lane codex, model gpt-6-luna.
Refs ISSUE-111
